kahoot.q: Reading Passage 3 has three question groups: YES/NO/NOT GIVEN, a summary and multiple choice. What should you do first?
options: Find which part of the text each group covers
Read the whole passage slowly twice
Underline every unknown word in the text
kahoot.explain: Avval xarita: 1–2 daqiqada har savol guruhi matnning qaysi xatboshilariga tegishli ekanini belgilaymiz.

kahoot.q: Text: 'Some claim that e-books will soon replace paper books. I find this hard to believe.' Statement: 'Paper books will soon disappear.'
options: NO – the writer doubts this claim
YES – the text mentions this claim
NOT GIVEN – no dates are given
NOT GIVEN – e-books are not described
kahoot.explain: "I find this hard to believe" — yozuvchi da'voga qo'shilmaydi, demak NO. Da'voning matnda tilga olinishi YES degani emas.

kahoot.q: Text: 'In my view, the examples in this new dictionary are exceptionally clear.' Statement: 'The new dictionary is better value than older ones.'
options: NOT GIVEN – value is not discussed
YES – the writer praises the dictionary
NO – the writer criticises older dictionaries
YES – clear examples mean better value
kahoot.explain: Yozuvchi misollarni maqtaydi, lekin narx yoki qiymat haqida fikr bildirmaydi — NOT GIVEN.

kahoot.q: Text: 'Online courses are probably the most flexible way to study.' Statement: 'Online courses are more flexible than other ways of studying.'
options: YES – a cautious view is still a view
NOT GIVEN – the writer is not certain
NOT GIVEN – other ways are not named
kahoot.explain: "Probably" — ehtiyotkor ohang, lekin baribir yozuvchining fikri; gap unga mos, demak YES.

kahoot.q: Text: 'Only a small number of schools still teach Latin.' Statement: 'Most schools still teach Latin.'
options: YES – both mention schools teaching Latin
NOT GIVEN – the number of schools is unknown
NOT GIVEN – the writer gives no opinion
kahoot.explain: "Only a small number" va "most" bir-biriga zid — javob NO.

kahoot.q: A YES/NO/NOT GIVEN statement uses the same word as the passage, e.g. 'popular'. What does this tell you?
options: Nothing yet – check the whole claim
The answer is almost certainly YES
The answer cannot be NOT GIVEN
The answer is almost certainly NO
kahoot.explain: Bir xil so'z bir xil da'vo degani emas: so'z matnda nimaga tegishli ekanini va yozuvchi nima deyotganini tekshiramiz.

kahoot.q: Passage: 'Learners seldom notice their own errors.' Which sentence has the same meaning?
options: Learners rarely spot their own mistakes.
Learners never notice their own mistakes.
kahoot.explain: seldom = rarely (kamdan-kam), errors = mistakes; "never" — mutlaq so'z, ma'noni o'zgartiradi.

kahoot.q: A summary gives a box of options A–H. What do you write on the answer sheet?
options: The letter of the correct option
The word or words from the passage
The full phrase copied from the box
Both the letter and the phrase
kahoot.explain: Variantlar ro'yxati berilgan bo'lsa, faqat HARF yoziladi (masalan, F); so'z yoki ibora yozilsa (matndan ham, ro'yxatdan ham) — 0 ball.

kahoot.q: Before you look at the options in the box, what should you decide for each gap?
options: What type of word the gap needs
How many words the passage uses
Which option is the longest one
Whether the gap is near the title
kahoot.explain: Avval bo'shliqqa qanday so'z kerakligini (ot, sifat, fe'l) aniqlaymiz — shunda 8 variantdan 2–3 tasi qoladi.

kahoot.q: Summary: 'Many teenagers feel too ___ to speak in front of the class.' Which option fits the gap grammatically?
kahoot.explain: "feel too ___ to ..." qolipida sifat kerak: nervous. Silence, courage, anxiety — otlar.

kahoot.q: A paragraph describes three studies and ends: 'All of this suggests that sleep improves memory.' What is its main purpose?
options: To support a claim about sleep and memory
To describe one study in great detail
To criticise the methods of sleep research
To compare the results of three researchers
kahoot.explain: Main purpose — butun xatboshining vazifasi: uchta tadqiqot bitta xulosani (uyqu xotirani yaxshilaydi) qo'llab-quvvatlaydi.

kahoot.q: In a multiple-choice question, one option repeats several exact words from the passage. What should you think?
options: It may be a trap – compare the meaning
It is almost always the correct answer
It must be wrong because it copies the text
It is correct if it is the longest option
kahoot.explain: Tuzoq variantlar ko'pincha matndagi so'zlarni takrorlaydi, lekin ma'no boshqa — variantni isbot gap bilan solishtiramiz.

kahoot.q: 'Children acquire their first language without lessons.' Here 'acquire' means…
kahoot.explain: acquire — egallamoq, o'zlashtirmoq: bola ona tilini darssiz, tabiiy ravishda o'zlashtiradi.

kahoot.q: Babies ___ the sounds that they hear around them.
kahoot.explain: imitate — taqlid qilmoq: chaqaloqlar eshitgan tovushlarini takrorlaydi.

kahoot.q: 'Fluency' in a language is the ability to…
options: understand every word of a text
pronounce words like a native speaker
kahoot.explain: fluency — ravonlik: ko'p to'xtamasdan, erkin gapirish.

kahoot.q: 'The course tests your proficiency in English.' The course tests…
kahoot.explain: proficiency — bilim yoki malaka darajasi (a high level of proficiency).

kahoot.q: Special words used by one profession, often hard for outsiders to understand, are called…
kahoot.explain: jargon — kasbiy atamalar: faqat shu soha odamlari yaxshi tushunadigan so'zlar.

kahoot.q: A sentence that can be understood in two different ways contains…
kahoot.explain: ambiguity — noaniqlik, ikki ma'nolilik.

kahoot.q: 'They made progress, albeit slowly.' 'Albeit' is closest in meaning to…
kahoot.explain: albeit = although (garchi ... bo'lsa ham): ular sekin bo'lsa ham oldinga siljishdi.

kahoot.q: 'She used simple words to get her message across.' She wanted people to…
kahoot.explain: get the message across — fikrni tushunarli qilib yetkazmoq.

intro: Section 3 — o'quv mavzusidagi suhbat: odatda talaba(lar) va o'qituvchi (tutor), ba'zan uch kishi. Unda faqat ma'lumot emas, FIKR va BAHO ham bo'ladi: "a bit dull", "went down well", "I wasn't sure they could be justified". Imtihonda Section 3 (21–30-savollar) odatda ikki, ba'zan uch savol turidan iborat; bugungi kitob mashqlarida uchalasi ketma-ket keladi: TWO letters, matching va short answer.

Tayyorlanish vaqtini uchga bo'ling. TWO letters: savol o'zagidagi kalit g'oyani tagiga chizing ("WILL students do", "MUST check", "IMPRESSIVE according to the tutor"). Matching: sarlavha va variantlardagi kalit so'zlarni belgilang (repetitive, long time to write, shorter, well structured, relevant, popular). Short answer: so'z chegarasini doiraga oling.

Choose TWO letters (A–E): beshta variantning deyarli hammasi suhbatda tilga olinadi. Uch variant tuzoq bo'ladi: taklif qilinib RAD ETILADI ("something from one of the textbooks" → "a much better idea"), kelajakdagi yoki boshqa ishga tegishli bo'ladi ("the starting point for a whole other piece of work"), yoki salbiy baholanadi. Javoblar variantlar tartibida emas, suhbat tartibida keladi. Har harf — alohida ball; ikkala harfni istalgan tartibda yozish mumkin.

Matching (A–F): savollar (5, 6, 7, 8) suhbat tartibida keladi, variantlar esa aralash. 6 variantdan 4 tasi kerak — 2 tasi ortiqcha. Har bir savol bo'yicha gapiruvchi odatda bir nechta narsa aytadi: masalan, "History of English" haqida "a bit dull" ham, "clearly sequenced" ham aytiladi — faqat ikkinchisi ro'yxatda bor.

Suhbatdagi fikr o'zgarishi: talaba bir narsani aytadi, tutor to'g'rilaydi ("No — that's an obvious one"). Oxirgi, kelishilgan fikr javob bo'ladi. "But", "though", "whereas", "actually" so'zlaridan keyin diqqatni kuchaytiring.

Short answer: savolga to'g'ridan-to'g'ri javob; NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS — "digital recorders" (2 so'z) to'g'ri, "department's digital recorders" — 3 so'z, xato. Ko'plik kalitda ko'pincha qavs bilan beriladi: mobile phone(s).
presentation: TWO letters da ikkala harfni bitta katakka yozamanmi?
Yo'q. Imtihonda 1 va 2 alohida katak: har biriga bitta harf, tartib ahamiyatsiz (A, D yoki D, A).
Uchala variant ham eshitildi, qaysini tanlayman?
Qaysi biri qabul qilinganini tinglang. "That's a much better idea", "that's also important" — tasdiq; "No", "I wouldn't worry about" — rad.
Matching da bitta harfni ikki marta yozsam bo'ladimi?
Bu turdagi ro'yxatda odatda har harf bir marta. Ko'rsatmani o'qing: "Choose FOUR answers from the box".
Matching savollari tartibdami?
Ha — 5, 6, 7, 8 suhbat tartibida. Variantlar (A–F) tartibda emas.
Kim gapirayotganini qanday bilaman?
Ismlar boshida aytiladi (Amanda, Dr White). Savolda "according to the tutor" bo'lsa, faqat tutor fikri hisobga olinadi.
Short answer da artikl yozamanmi?
Shart emas. "mobile phones" yetarli — "the mobile phones" esa 3 so'z (artikl ham so'z sanaladi) va TWO WORDS chegarasini buzadi.
notes: 5.0 da multiple choice, matching va short answer ni alohida mashq qilgan edik. Endi ular bitta Section 3 da ketma-ket keladi: o'tishda adashmaslik va suhbatdagi FIKRni kuzatish — asosiy ko'nikma.
Tekshiruvda har javobdan keyin skriptdan tasdiq gapni va tuzoq gapni alohida rangda ko'rsating. TWO letters da uchta noto'g'ri variant nega noto'g'ri ekanini ham so'rang.

Kuchli o'quvchilarga: Workbook audiosini tinglab, 5–8 savollar uchun tutor aytgan har bir baho so'zini (original, backed up, trouble, well put together) yozib olish. Qavsdagi so'zlar — ustoz uchun kalit: o'quvchiga oldindan aytilmaydi (WB — imtihon rejimi).

answers: went down well / everyone liked it
I spent ages putting it together
closely linked to / connected with your topic

Audioda ko'pincha teskari shakl tuzoq bo'ladi: "I didn't take long to put that together".
"Mini-lecture" so'zining o'zi qisqalikni bildiradi.
"Structure" o'rniga "sequenced", "organised", "put together well".
"Relevant" = "related to", "linked to".

class_ex.title: "Qaysi biri qoldi?" — rad etilgan variant tuzog'i
class_ex.instr: Ustoz gapni o'qiydi. O'quvchilar savolga javob beradi va rad etilgan variantni aytadi.
items: "We thought about interviewing teachers, but in the end we went for a questionnaire." — Which method will they use?
"I'd love to use video, but we'll have to make do with audio recordings." — What will they record?
"It's not the length that worries me — it's the lack of examples." — What is the tutor's concern?
"You could use your phones, or we can lend you some cameras if you book them." — Which TWO pieces of equipment?
"The first lecture was long and detailed, whereas this one is quite short." — Which lecture is short?
why: "But in the end" — oxirgi qaror. Interview — rad etilgan.
"I'd love to" — istak, lekin "have to make do with" — haqiqiy tanlov.
"It's not X — it's Y" — Y javob.
Ikkalasi ham taklif qilingan va rad etilmagan — ikkalasi javob (SB 9–10 dagidek).
"Whereas" — qarama-qarshilik: birinchisi uzun, ikkinchisi qisqa.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 1: Teachers
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda so'rang va javob bering; har javob 2–3 gap: javob + sabab/misol (because, for example, to be honest).
items: Who was your favourite teacher at school? Why?
What makes a good teacher?
Would you like to be a teacher in the future?
Do you prefer teachers who are strict or relaxed?
answers: Well, it was definitely my history teacher, Mr Rustamov. He never just read from the textbook; instead, he told us stories that made the past come alive, so even students who hated history actually looked forward to his lessons.

In my opinion, patience is the most important quality. A good teacher explains things in different ways until everyone understands, and they also give honest feedback, because students can't improve if they only hear praise.

To be honest, I don't think so. I enjoy helping my younger brother with his homework, but standing in front of thirty teenagers every day would be exhausting. I'd rather work in IT, although I might teach coding part-time.

Actually, I prefer something in between. Strict teachers keep the class focused, which is useful before exams, but if a teacher is too strict, students become afraid to ask questions. So ideally, a teacher should be firm but friendly.
why: 'Well' bilan tabiiy boshlanish, relative clause ('stories that made...', 'students who hated...') va 'make the past come alive', 'look forward to' iboralari.
'In my opinion' diskurs belgisi, 'until' va 'because ... if' bilan murakkab gap; 'honest feedback' kollokatsiyasi.
'To be honest' + qarama-qarshi fikr ('but'), 'would be exhausting' faraz va 'I'd rather ..., although ...' tuzilmasi.
'Actually' va 'something in between' — ikki tomonni solishtirish; 'which is useful' relative clause, 1-tur shart gap va 'firm but friendly' juftligi.
class_ex.note: Mavzu: IELTS Speaking Part 1 to'plami (Teachers); savollar va namunalar — Jony Academy original materiali.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 2: A presentation or project at school
class_ex.instr: 1 daqiqa tayyorlanish (qog'ozga 5–6 kalit so'z), keyin 1–2 daqiqa to'xtovsiz gapiring; sherigingiz vaqtni o'lchaydi va S6_CLASS bo'yicha band qo'yadi.
items: Describe a presentation or project that you did at school.
You should say:
what the topic was
how you prepared for it
how other people reacted
and explain how you felt afterwards.
answers: I'd like to talk about a presentation I gave in Year 9 for my geography class. The topic was the Aral Sea, and our teacher asked us to explain why it has shrunk so dramatically and what is being done about it now.

I worked with two classmates, Dilnoza and Sardor, and we had two weeks to meet the deadline. First, we did some research online and in the school library, and Sardor's grandfather, who used to live in Muynak, told us what the area was like in the past. Then we made slides with maps and photos, and we rehearsed at least five times, because none of us wanted to forget our lines.

On the day itself, I had butterflies in my stomach, especially when I saw that the head teacher had come to watch. But once I started speaking, I relaxed. My classmates asked lots of questions, and our teacher gave us really positive feedback, particularly about the interview with Sardor's grandfather.

Afterwards, I felt relieved and quite proud. We had put a lot of effort into it, and it paid off — we got the highest mark in the class. On the whole, it showed me that if I prepare properly, speaking in public isn't as frightening as I thought.
why: FC: kartochka tartibida — mavzu → tayyorgarlik → boshqalarning munosabati → his-tuyg'u; First / Then / But once / Afterwards bilan bog'langan, taxminan 2 daqiqaga yetadi.

LR: box iboralari (did some research, meet the deadline, rehearsed, had butterflies in my stomach, positive feedback, put a lot of effort into, it paid off, on the whole) va mavzu so'zlari (slides, head teacher, the highest mark) o'z joyida.

GRA: relative clause (who used to live in Muynak), past perfect (had come, had put), passive (is being done), present perfect (has shrunk), 1-tur shart gap (if I prepare properly) va solishtirma (isn't as frightening as).
Nega Band 7 emas: hikoya aniq va izchil, lekin idioma va nozik ma'noli iboralar kam, gaplar asosan to'g'ri chiziqli — Band 6–6.5 uchun namunaviy daraja.
box: to do some research — ma'lumot to'plamoq, izlanish qilmoq
to rehearse — chiqishdan oldin mashq qilib olmoq
to have butterflies in my stomach — hayajondan ichim titramoq
to meet a deadline — ishni belgilangan muddatda topshirmoq
positive feedback — ijobiy fikr-mulohaza, maqtov
to put a lot of effort into — ...ga ko'p kuch sarflamoq
on the whole — umuman olganda
it paid off — mehnat o'zini oqladi
class_ex.note: Namunani ustoz o'qiydi (taxminan 1:50); o'quvchilar box iboralarini eshitganda qo'l ko'taradi. Bog'lanish: bugungi Listening ham taqdimot va topshiriq haqida edi.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 3: Presentation skills and group work
class_ex.instr: Ustoz savol beradi, 2–3 o'quvchi javob beradi: fikr → sabab → misol → qarama-qarshi fikr yoki xulosa (har javob 30–40 soniya).
items: Why are presentation skills important for young people?
Is group work at school more useful than working alone?
Should students be allowed to choose their own assignment topics?
answers: I think they're essential nowadays. Most jobs involve explaining ideas to colleagues or clients, so people who can present clearly have a real advantage. For instance, in a job interview, candidates who speak confidently usually make a better impression, even if their knowledge is similar to others'. Presentation skills also build self-confidence, which helps in everyday life. That's why I believe schools should give students more chances to practise them from an early age.

It depends on the task, but on the whole I'd say group work is more useful. When students work together, they learn to share responsibilities, listen to different opinions and resolve conflicts, which are skills they'll need at work. On the other hand, group work isn't always fair, because sometimes one or two people do everything while others do very little. So I think teachers should combine both and assess each person's contribution separately.

Yes, to some extent. If students can choose a topic they're genuinely interested in, they're likely to put more effort into it and do deeper research. For example, my friend who loves football wrote a brilliant science project about sports injuries. However, total freedom can be a problem, because some students would simply pick the easiest option. A good solution would be for teachers to offer a list of topics and let students choose from it.
why: Strategiya: fikr (essential) → sabab (most jobs involve...) → misol (job interview) → qo'shimcha foyda (self-confidence) → 'That's why I believe' xulosa.
Strategiya: 'It depends on...' bilan ehtiyotkor boshlanish → foydalar ro'yxati → 'On the other hand' qarama-qarshi fikr → 'So I think' murosali xulosa.
Strategiya: 'to some extent' qisman rozilik → 1-tur shart gap bilan sabab → shaxsiy misol → 'However' cheklov → 'A good solution would be' taklif.

listenings.title: Student's Book, Track 10: Amanda's assignment (Q1–4)
listenings.qtype: Multiple choice — Choose TWO letters (A–E), Section 3, 1-qism
intro: Amanda o'z tutori Dr White bilan talaffuz bo'yicha topshirig'ini muhokama qiladi. SB 2-mashq: tinglashdan oldin savol o'zagidagi kalit g'oyani tagiga chizing (variantlarni emas): "WILL students do", "MUST check".
Beshta variantning ko'pi eshitiladi — qaysi biri qabul qilinib, qaysi biri rad etilganini belgilab boring. Savollar sahifasi quyida rasm sifatida.

tasks.title: Questions 1–4
tasks.type: Choose TWO letters, A–E
tasks.instr: Har savol uchun ikkita harf. Javoblar variantlar tartibida emas, suhbat tartibida keladi.
items: 1–2 Which TWO activities will students do as part of Amanda's assignment? A) analyse their own speech B) record other students' speech C) read something from a book D) repeat part of a lecture E) remember part of a lecture

3–4 Which TWO features must Amanda check when she chooses the extract? A) the time it takes to read B) the overall organisation C) the number of words D) the number of sentences E) the inclusion of key ideas
why: A: "record themselves ... then listen back and see where their weaknesses lie". D: "look up one of my lectures on the website and find a suitable extract" — talabalar uni ovoz chiqarib o'qiydi. Tuzoqlar: B — "peer evaluation" (sheriklarni baholash, ularni yozib olish emas); C — "one of the textbooks" taklifi "a much better idea" bilan almashtirilgan; E — "it isn't a memory test".

B: "a clear, well-structured passage". E: "what you do need are some obvious main points". Tuzoqlar: A — "taking a while to make the selection" (Amandaning vaqti, o'qish vaqti emas); C — "shouldn't consist entirely of short words" (so'zlar soni emas, turi); D — "I wouldn't worry about how many sentences there are".
tasks.note: Ikkala savolda ham beshta variantning to'rttasi yoki beshtasi tilga olinadi. O'quvchilar har variant yoniga ✓ (qabul) yoki ✗ (rad) qo'yib tinglasin — kalitdagi izohlar ham shu gaplarni ko'rsatadi.

listenings.title: Workbook, Track 4: Beth's dissertation (Q1–10)
listenings.qtype: TWO letters + Matching + Short answer — imtihon rejimi
intro: Talaba Beth tutori bilan "Communication Skills in the Workplace" dissertatsiyasi haqida gaplashadi. Avval Workbook 1-mashqi: suhbat qanday dissertatsiya haqida?
Keyin imtihondagidek: tayyorlanish vaqti, audio BIR MARTA, 10 savol.

tasks.title: 1-mashq: suhbat nima haqida?
tasks.type: Choose A, B or C
tasks.instr: Barcha savollarga ko'z yugurting: "did Beth include", "were impressive", "comments about each section", "in her conclusion".
items: 1 What are the speakers talking about? A) a dissertation the student is planning B) a dissertation the student is writing C) a dissertation the student has completed
why: Savollar o'tgan zamonda ("did Beth include", "were impressive") va xulosa haqida — ish tugagan. Audioda tutor oxirida: "this is a good piece of work. Well done."

tasks.title: Questions 1–4
tasks.type: Choose TWO letters, A–E
tasks.instr: 3–4 savolda faqat TUTOR fikri: "impressive, according to the tutor".
items: 1–2 Which TWO areas of work did Beth include in her dissertation? A) retail B) banking C) call centres D) tourism E) translation

3–4 Which TWO aspects of the dissertation were impressive, according to the tutor? A) summary of academic research B) analysis of videos C) observation of live interactions D) interviews E) analysis of data on the outcomes
why: A: "the retail sector had to be in there". D: "that led you to the idea of tourist guides". Tuzoqlar: B — "banking would probably lead to the same sort of results as retail" (kiritilmagan); C — "I decided to spread the focus away"; E — "the starting point for a whole other piece of work".

C: "your analysis from watching people in action was very effective". D: intervyular — "it's very interesting to compare what people think they're doing with the way they're actually communicating. I was very struck by that aspect". Tuzoqlar: A — "a bit more on the academic research ... would have been good"; B — "it would have been good if you could have filmed people" (qilinmagan); E — "it would be fascinating to get data on the outcomes" (kelajak uchun g'oya).
tasks.note: 3–4 savol — "would have been good" tuzog'i: bu qilinMAGAN ish haqida. Doskada "would have + V3" = amalga oshmagan narsa ekanini ko'rsating.

tasks.title: Questions 5–8 — Sections of Dissertation
tasks.type: Choose FOUR answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–F
tasks.instr: Har bo'lim haqida tutor ham, Beth ham gapiradi. Kelishilgan baho — javob.
box: A There is not enough evidence.
B The conclusion is confusing.
C It highlights a real problem.
D It is particularly well organised.
E There are too many examples.
F It includes new ideas.
items: 5 Dealing with Complaints
6 Collaborating with Colleagues
7 Interacting with Managers
8 Giving Instructions
why: "This section had some really original thinking on your part"; Beth: "come up with something fresh".
"I didn't feel that your conclusions were really backed up by the research you did" + "I wasn't sure they could be justified by the examples". Tuzoq: E — misollar ko'p emas, ular dalil bo'la olmagan.
"Your conclusions there point to something that causes all sorts of trouble in organisations".
"The Giving Instructions section was very well put together". Tuzoq: E — "lots of examples" maqtov sifatida; B — "a conclusion that made logical sense" (teskari).

tasks.title: Questions 9–10
tasks.type: Answer the question. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer.
tasks.instr: Which TWO aspects of communication does Beth emphasise in her conclusion?
items: 9 Aspect of communication — first answer
10 Aspect of communication — second answer
why: "You see Listening Skills as a much bigger issue". Tuzoq: "Writing Skills" — asosiy qismda, xulosada emas.
"There are lots of instances where this is less of an issue than Formal Language". Tuzoq: "Grammatical Accuracy" — tutor taklif qiladi, Beth "up to a point" deb cheklaydi.
tasks.note: Javoblar istalgan tartibda. 10-savolda ko'p o'quvchi "grammatical accuracy" yozadi — "Well, up to a point, but..." ni skriptda ko'rsating.

listenings.title: Workbook: recording script (Track 4) — ustoz uchun
intro: Recording script sahifasi — tekshiruvdan keyin ekranga chiqariladi.
transcript: [Ustoz uchun] Skript bilan qayta tinglashda xato qilingan savollarning gapini topishga ishlatiladi. "would have been good" va "up to a point" gaplarini alohida belgilang.

listenings.title: Jony Academy mashqi: Planning a group presentation (Q1–10)
intro: Ikki talaba (Kamola va Daniel) "Communication Skills" kursi uchun guruh taqdimotini tutor bilan muhokama qiladi. Suhbatni BIR MARTA tinglaysiz.
Tayyorlanish: 1 daqiqa. Ko'rsatmalar: Q1–4 — Choose TWO letters; Q5–8 — Choose FOUR answers from the box (A–F); Q9–10 — NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.
transcript: [Ustoz uchun] Ustoz TUTOR rolini o'qiydi, ikki kuchli o'quvchi — KAMOLA va DANIEL. Qolganlar BIR MARTA tinglaydi. Rol o'qiydigan ikki o'quvchiga skriptni tayyorlanish vaqtida bering. Tabiiy tezlikda o'qing (taxminan 150 so'z/daqiqa — jami 4–5 daqiqa), ovozlarni farqlang; Q1–4 dan keyin ("So, which four sections have you decided on?" dan oldin) 20–30 soniya pauza qiling — o'quvchilar Q5–10 ni o'qiydi. Rol o'qigan ikki o'quvchi savollarni yechmaydi; ularning alohida topshirig'i — tahlil bosqichida har savolning isbot gapini va rad etilgan variantini skriptdan topib ko'rsatish.
TUTOR: Come in, both of you. So, you wanted to talk about your group presentation for the Communication Skills module?
KAMOLA: Yes. We've chosen our topic — communication in online meetings.
TUTOR: Good choice. Everyone has had some experience of those now. How are you planning to collect your data?
DANIEL: Well, our first idea was to record some real meetings at the companies where we do our part-time jobs, and then analyse them.
TUTOR: Hmm. You'd need everyone's permission for that, and companies are often worried about privacy.
KAMOLA: That's exactly what my manager said, so we've dropped that idea. Instead, we're going to put a short questionnaire online and send the link to students and staff.
TUTOR: Fine. And will that be enough on its own?
DANIEL: We thought about interviewing some managers as well, but most of them told us they simply don't have time this month.
KAMOLA: So we're going to run a focus group instead — six or seven students who use online meetings every week, discussing their experiences for about an hour.
TUTOR: That should give you some rich detail. Last year's group observed online lessons, but I think your approach suits your topic better.
TUTOR: Now, I've read the plan you sent me. Can I be honest about it?
DANIEL: Of course.

TUTOR: The length is fine — fifteen minutes is exactly what's required, so don't worry about that. And I know the deadline is close, but you've got plenty of time. My main concern is that you're trying to cover too much. You've listed eight different topics. In fifteen minutes you'd only have time to mention each one.
KAMOLA: So we should choose three or four?

TUTOR: Four at most. The other thing is your reading list. A lot of the articles on it were written before most people had ever used video calls. The situation has changed completely since then, so look for more recent research.
DANIEL: OK. What about the number of people answering our questionnaire? We're hoping for about forty.
TUTOR: Forty is perfectly reasonable for a student project.
TUTOR: So, which four sections have you decided on?

KAMOLA: First, camera use — whether people keep their cameras on or off. Most of our friends assumed that everyone keeps the camera on. But in our small trial, more than half the people switched it off. I think that's going to shock people.
TUTOR: Yes, that could well be the most unexpected part for your audience. Good.
DANIEL: Then interrupting. In online meetings, people either talk over each other or nobody speaks at all.
TUTOR: That's hard to explain with slides alone.
DANIEL: We know. So Kamola and I are going to act out a short meeting — two minutes, one version where everyone interrupts and one with clear turn-taking.
KAMOLA: We thought about putting it at the very end, but it's better in the middle, to wake everyone up.
TUTOR: The audience will enjoy that.
KAMOLA: Third, the chat box — how people use written messages during a meeting.
TUTOR: Hmm. Isn't a lot of that already covered in your section on interrupting? People type in the chat when they can't get a word in.
KAMOLA: Yes, I suppose there is some repetition there.
TUTOR: Think about how to separate the two. I wouldn't worry about finding more figures for it, though — you've got plenty.
DANIEL: And finally, background noise — dogs barking, traffic, that kind of thing.
TUTOR: It's a real issue, but it's more technical than the others.
DANIEL: Yes, we've agreed that if we're running over fifteen minutes in rehearsal, that's the section we'll drop.
TUTOR: Sensible. Right — before Friday, could you send me a couple of things?
KAMOLA: The slides?
TUTOR: No, not yet — I'll look at those next week. First, I'd like to see your new reading list, with the recent articles.
DANIEL: OK, the reading list.
TUTOR: And the questionnaire itself, before you put it online. I'd like to check the wording of the questions.
KAMOLA: Of course. We'll send both on Thursday.
TUTOR: Excellent. Good luck with it.

tasks.title: Questions 1–4
tasks.type: Choose TWO letters, A–E
tasks.instr: Rad etilgan variantlarni ✗ bilan belgilab boring.
items: 1–2 Which TWO methods will the students use to collect data? A) an online questionnaire B) recordings of real meetings C) interviews with managers D) observation of online lessons E) a focus group

3–4 Which TWO problems does the tutor mention about the students' plan? A) It covers too many topics. B) The number of people in the survey is too small. C) There is not enough time before the deadline. D) The presentation will be too long. E) Some of the sources are out of date.
why: A: "we're going to put a short questionnaire online". E: "we're going to run a focus group instead". Tuzoqlar: B — "we've dropped that idea"; C — menejerlarning vaqti yo'q; D — o'tgan yilgi guruh qilgan.

A: "you're trying to cover too much. You've listed eight different topics". E: "a lot of the articles ... were written before most people had ever used video calls". Tuzoqlar: B — "forty is perfectly reasonable"; C — "you've got plenty of time"; D — "the length is fine".

tasks.title: Questions 5–8 — Sections of the presentation
tasks.type: Choose FOUR answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–F
tasks.instr: Bo'limlar suhbatda tartib bilan keladi.
box: A It needs more statistics.
B It will probably surprise the audience.
C It should be moved to the end.
D It overlaps with another section.
E It will include a short demonstration.
F It may be left out.
items: 5 Camera use
6 Interrupting
7 Chat box
8 Background noise
why: "I think that's going to shock people" + tutor: "the most unexpected part for your audience".
"We're going to act out a short meeting — two minutes". Tuzoq: C — "we thought about putting it at the very end, but it's better in the middle".
"Isn't a lot of that already covered in your section on interrupting?" — "there is some repetition". Tuzoq: A — "I wouldn't worry about finding more figures".
"If we're running over fifteen minutes in rehearsal, that's the section we'll drop".

tasks.title: Questions 9–10
tasks.type: Answer the question. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer.
tasks.instr: Which TWO things will the students send to the tutor before Friday?
items: 9 Thing to send before Friday — first answer
10 Thing to send before Friday — second answer
why: "First, I'd like to see your new reading list". "New reading list" — 3 so'z; "reading list" yozing.
"And the questionnaire itself, before you put it online". Tuzoq: "The slides?" — "No, not yet".
tasks.note: Javoblar istalgan tartibda. 9-savolda "new reading list" (3 so'z) — chegara buziladi, shuning uchun 0 ball.

homework_intro: Bugun Section 3 da uch savol turini ketma-ket yechdik: TWO letters, matching va short answer. Eng ko'p ball rad etilgan variantlarda va paraphrase'da yo'qoladi.

Birinchi vazifa — shadowing: ustoz guruhga SB Track 10 audiosini va SB skript rasmini yuboradi. Track 10 ni qo'yib, Amandaning gaplarini ovoz bilan birga takrorlang (kamida 3 marta). Keyin Amanda rolini audiosiz, skriptdan o'qib, ovozli xabar qilib guruhga yuboring.

Ikkinchi vazifa — diktant: ustoz guruhga WB Track 4 audiosini yuboradi. Uning ikkinchi qismini ("Now, looking at the content of your dissertation..." dan "Pause" gacha) to'xtatib-to'xtatib yozing va guruhga yuboring. Shundan keyin ustoz WB skript rasmini yuboradi — u bilan tekshiring va xatolarni qizil bilan belgilang.

Uchinchi vazifa — paraphrase ro'yxati: SB Track 11 va WB Track 4 ni (ustoz yuborgan audio) skriptsiz qayta tinglab, 5–8 savollardagi har bir variant (A–F) audioda qanday aytilganini yozing (masalan, popular → went down well). Avval faqat quloq bilan toping, keyin skript rasmi bilan tekshiring. Ro'yxatni guruhga yuboring va xatolar daftariga ham qo'shing.
Speaking vazifasi — bugungi Part 2 kartochkasini uyda ovozli yozib yuboring (1 daqiqa tayyorlanish, 2 daqiqa gapirish).

homework.title: Shadowing: SB Track 10 (Amanda)
homework.instr: Ustoz guruhga SB Track 10 audiosi va SB skript rasmini yuboradi. 3 marta audio bilan birga, keyin audiosiz (skriptdan); ovozli xabar guruhga.
homework.answers: Ustoz ohang, urg'u va to'xtashlarni tekshiradi.

homework.title: Diktant: WB Track 4 (2-qism)
homework.instr: Ustoz guruhga WB Track 4 audiosini yuboradi. Bo'limlar haqidagi qismni to'xtatib yozish; diktant yuborilgach, skript rasmi bilan tekshirish.
homework.answers: Diktant guruhga yuborilgandan keyin ustoz WB skript rasmini yuboradi; o'quvchi o'zi tekshiradi, ustoz yuborilgan diktantdan 3 ta gapni tekshiradi.

homework.title: Paraphrase ro'yxati: matching variantlari
homework.instr: SB Track 11 va WB Track 4 (ustoz yuborgan audio): avval skriptsiz tinglab, har variant uchun audiodagi iborani yozish; keyin skript bilan tekshirish.
homework.answers: Kamida 8 juftlik; ro'yxat guruh chatiga yuboriladi, ustoz skript bo'yicha tekshirib normativni belgilaydi.

homework.title: Speaking (og'zaki): Part 2 ovozli yozuv — A presentation or project at school
homework.instr: Bugungi Part 2 kartochkasi: 1 daqiqa tayyorlanish, 1:40–2:00 gapiring, ilovaga ovozli yuboring; oxirida Part 1 dan 2 savolga javob qo'shing.
homework.answers: Ustoz S6_CLASS bo'yicha 4 mezonga band qo'yadi; tekshiruv: 2:00 gacha to'xtovsiz, box'dan 3 ibora, kamida 1 murakkab gap (because/which/if).

normativ: Amandaning gaplari — to'xtovsiz, aniq talaffuz bilan
1:40–2:00 to'xtovsiz, 3 ta yangi ibora, 4 mezon o'rtachasi ≥ 5.5 (S6_CLASS)

kahoot.q: What is IELTS Listening Section 3 usually like?
options: students and a tutor discussing a task
one speaker talking about a local place
two friends chatting about weekend plans
a lecturer giving a talk on one topic
kahoot.explain: Section 3 — o'quv mavzusidagi suhbat: odatda talaba(lar) va tutor; Section 1 — kundalik suhbat, 2 — bitta so'zlovchi, 4 — ma'ruza.

kahoot.q: Section 3 has 'Choose TWO letters' questions, a matching box and short answers. How should you use the time before you listen?
options: Look quickly at all three question types
Read only the first question very carefully
Learn all the box options by heart
Write a guessed answer for every question
kahoot.explain: Vaqtni uchga bo'ling: TWO letters da savol o'zagi, matching da variant kalit so'zlari, short answer da so'z chegarasi.

kahoot.q: In a 'Choose TWO letters (A–E)' question, how many of the five options are you likely to hear mentioned?
kahoot.explain: Odatda beshala variantning ko'pi tilga olinadi — uchtasi rad etiladi, boshqa narsaga tegishli bo'ladi yoki salbiy baholanadi.

kahoot.q: A 'Choose TWO letters' question is worth two marks. You write B and D, but the key is D and E. What is your score?
kahoot.explain: Har to'g'ri harf — alohida ball: D to'g'ri (1 ball), B noto'g'ri (0 ball).

kahoot.q: 'We considered a poster, but we've decided to make a short podcast instead.' What will they make?
kahoot.explain: "But ... instead" — oxirgi qaror; poster taklif qilinib rad etilgan.

kahoot.q: The tutor says: 'It would have been good to include a few photos.' What does this tell you about the photos?
kahoot.explain: "Would have been good" — qilinmagan ish haqida afsus: demak rasmlar ishda yo'q.

kahoot.q: A matching task has four questions (5–8) and six options (A–F). How many options will NOT be used?
kahoot.explain: 6 variant, 4 savol — 2 tasi ortiqcha; ular ko'pincha suhbatda tuzoq sifatida tilga olinadi.

kahoot.q: In a Section 3 matching task (questions 5–8, options A–F), in what order do you usually hear the information?
options: in the order of the box, A to F
kahoot.explain: Ma'lumot savollar tartibida (5, 6, 7, 8) eshitiladi; qutidagi variantlar (A–F) esa aralash keladi.

kahoot.q: A question asks which TWO things were good, according to the tutor. The student praises the charts, but the tutor criticises them. Are the charts an answer?
options: No — only the tutor's view counts
No — charts are never the answer
kahoot.explain: "According to the tutor" — faqat tutor fikri hisobga olinadi: tutor diagrammalarni tanqid qildi, talabaning maqtovi esa javob emas.

kahoot.q: Student: 'Let's start with the background section.' Tutor: 'I'd rather you began with your results.' Student: 'Fair enough.' Which section will come first?
kahoot.explain: "Fair enough" — talaba tutor taklifiga rozi bo'ldi; oxirgi kelishilgan fikr javob bo'ladi.

kahoot.q: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS. You hear: 'We'll use the library's online catalogue.' Which answer is correct?
kahoot.explain: "Library's" va "the" ham so'z sanaladi — 3 so'zli javob 0 ball; "online catalogue" — 2 so'z.

kahoot.q: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS. Is 'well-known writer' an acceptable answer?
options: Yes — it counts as two words
No — it counts as three words
Yes — but only in capital letters
kahoot.explain: Chiziqcha bilan yozilgan so'z (well-known) bitta so'z sanaladi: well-known + writer = 2 so'z.

kahoot.q: 'I have to hand in my history ___ by Friday — it's a 2,000-word essay.' Which word fits?
kahoot.explain: Assignment — topshiriq (insho, loyiha): o'qituvchi beradi va belgilangan muddatda topshiriladi.

kahoot.q: A long piece of writing based on your own research, usually at the end of a degree, is a ___.
kahoot.explain: Dissertation — bitiruv ishi: o'z tadqiqotingizga asoslangan uzun yozma ish.

kahoot.q: When students judge the quality of their own work, this is called ___.
kahoot.explain: Self-assessment — o'z-o'zini baholash: o'z ishingizning kuchli va zaif tomonlarini aniqlash.

kahoot.q: 'Read this extract from a newspaper article.' Here, 'extract' means ___.
options: a short part taken from a longer text
a summary of it written in your own words
a list of the most important words
a picture printed next to the article
kahoot.explain: Extract (n) — parcha: uzunroq matndan olingan qisqa qism.

kahoot.q: 'Our teacher likes to use authentic materials in class.' What does 'authentic' mean here?
kahoot.explain: Authentic — haqiqiy, asl: til o'rganuvchilar uchun soddalashtirilmagan (masalan, haqiqiy yangiliklar).

kahoot.q: 'The researchers published their findings last year.' What are 'findings'?
options: the people who took part in it
the money paid for a study
the place where it was done
kahoot.explain: Findings — topilmalar, natijalar: tadqiqot natijasida aniqlangan narsalar.

kahoot.q: 'The writer makes a bold assertion in the first paragraph.' An assertion is ___.
options: a claim that something is true
a question that has no clear answer
kahoot.explain: Assertion — da'vo, qat'iy fikr: to'g'ri deb ta'kidlangan gap (unga dalil kerak bo'ladi).

kahoot.q: In IELTS Writing, what is 'coherence' mainly about?
options: how many rare words you use
how quickly you finish the task
kahoot.explain: Coherence — izchillik: g'oyalar mantiqiy tartibda va bir-biriga bog'langan bo'lishi.

lessons.title: Unit 4 Reading — Passage 1: True / False / Not Given + Note completion + Short answer
lessons.grammar_topic: Uch savol turi bitta passage'da: TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN + Note completion + Short-answer questions
lessons.vocab_topic: Unit 4 (New media) — internet, ilm-fan va onlayn jamiyat
lessons.book_ref: Complete IELTS Bands 5–6.5: Student's Book, Unit 4, 37–40-betlar (Reading Section 1); Workbook, Unit 4, 24–26-betlar. Practice 1–3 — Jony Academy matnlari; Speaking — Jony Academy original materiali (Part 1 mavzusi: Taking photos).

TRUE, FALSE va NOT GIVEN ni isbot gap bilan ajratish; "so'z bor, da'vo yo'q" tuzog'ini tanish.
Note completion'da notes sarlavhasidan kerakli xatboshini topish va bo'shliq turini (ot, fe'l, sifat, ko'plik) oldindan aytish.
Short-answer savollarida savol so'ziga qarab javob turini aniqlash: Whose → shaxs/nom, Which publication → nom, What type → ot birikmasi.
Javobni matndan aynan ko'chirish va so'z chegarasiga (NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS / AND/OR A NUMBER) rioya qilish.

Doskada uch ustun: "T/F/NG → qaysi xatboshilar?", "Notes → sarlavha qaysi qismga?", "Short answer → savol so'zi → javob turi".

intro: Oldingi darslarda passage'da ikki savol turi bor edi. Bugun — uchta: TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN (1–6), note completion (7–10) va short-answer questions (11–13). IELTS'da bu juda keng tarqalgan kombinatsiya.

Birinchi qadam — XARITA. Matnni o'qishdan oldin uchala guruhga 2 daqiqa ko'z yugurtiring. Student's Book'da 1–6 matnning birinchi yarmi (Berners-Lee, CERN, galaktikalar loyihasi), 7–10 — notes sarlavhasi "Social networks and internet use", ya'ni ijtimoiy tarmoqlar tadqiqoti xatboshisi, 11–13 — oxirgi xatboshi (jurnalistlar, bloggerlar, Nature).

T/F/NG: savoldagi kalit so'zni (ism, raqam, noyob so'z) belgilang va matndan toping. Savollar matn tartibida keladi. Eslatma: "so'z bor — da'vo yo'q" bo'lsa, NOT GIVEN (masalan, matnda "political campaigning" bor, lekin Berners-Lee siyosat bilan shug'ullangani haqida gap yo'q).

Note completion: notes sarlavhasi kerakli xatboshini ko'rsatadi. Har bo'shliqqa qanday so'z kerakligini oldindan ayting: "the ___ of social networks" — ot; "Most ___ intended for" — ko'plikdagi ot. Notes'dagi so'zlar matnda paraphrase bilan keladi ("limited number of people" = "a few specific friends").

Short-answer questions: savol so'zi javob turini aytadi. "Whose writing...?" — kishilar guruhi; "What type of writing...?" — ot birikmasi; "Which publication...?" — nom. Javob matndan aynan olinadi va savoldagi so'zlarni takrorlamaydi.

So'z chegarasi uchala guruhda ham muhim: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS — ikki so'zdan oshsa, javob to'g'ri bo'lsa ham 0 ball. Workbook'da chegara boshqacha: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER ("100,000 children" — raqam + bitta so'z).
Vaqt: 17–20 daqiqa. Taxminiy taqsimot: T/F/NG — 7 daqiqa, notes — 5 daqiqa, short answer — 4 daqiqa, tekshiruv — 2 daqiqa. Qiyin savolda 2 daqiqadan ko'p turmang.
formulas: T/F/NG kalit so'zlarini belgilang va tartib bilan ishlang
Short answer: savol so'zi → javob turi
Javobni matndan aynan ko'chiring va sanang
presentation: Qaysi guruhdan boshlayman?
Odatda tartib bilan. Lekin short answer'lar ko'pincha matn oxirida — xaritada buni oldindan belgilang.
Notes va short answer'lar ham matn tartibidami?
Guruh ichida odatda (USUALLY) ha. Lekin guruhlar orasida sakrash bo'lishi mumkin: Workbook'da 11–13 matnning oxirgi qismidan, 7–10 esa o'rtasidan.
Short answer'da gap bilan javob yozsam bo'ladimi?
Yo'q. Faqat kerakli 1–2 so'z: "Whose writing improves?" → "bloggers", "The bloggers' writing" emas.
Notes'da so'z matnda boshqacha shaklda bo'lsa-chi?
Javob matndan aynan ko'chiriladi. Grammatika mos kelmasa — ehtimol boshqa so'zni topgansiz.
FALSE va NOT GIVEN ni qanday ajrataman?
FALSE — matnda qarshi isbot gap bor. NOT GIVEN — isbot gap umuman yo'q; mavzu bo'lishi mumkin, da'vo yo'q.
Raqam so'z hisoblanadimi?
"AND/OR A NUMBER" bo'lsa, raqam alohida hisoblanadi: "100,000 children" — to'g'ri. Faqat "TWO WORDS" bo'lsa, raqam ham so'z hisoblanadi.

Har javobdan keyin ikki savol bering: "isbot qaysi gapda?" va "savol yoki notes'dagi qaysi so'z matnda qanday aytilgan?"
Kuchli o'quvchilarga: xaritani 2 daqiqada chizib, har guruh qaysi xatboshilarga to'g'ri kelishini oldindan aytish; Workbook'ni 15 daqiqada ishlash.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 1: Taking photos
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda so'rang va javob bering; har javob 2–3 gap: javob + sabab/misol (because, for example, to be honest).
items: Do you like taking photos? Why / Why not?
What do you usually take photos of?
Do you prefer taking photos with a phone or a camera?
Do you often share your photos online?
answers: Yes, I really do. I think photos are a great way to keep memories, because you can look at them years later and remember exactly how you felt. To be honest, I take a few pictures almost every day.
Mostly nature and food, actually. Whenever my family goes to the mountains in Chimgan, I take pictures of the views. I also love photographing the dishes my grandmother cooks for Navruz.
Definitely a phone. It's always in my pocket, so I never miss a good moment. A proper camera takes sharper pictures, of course, but it's quite heavy and I'd be afraid of breaking it.
Not very often, to be honest. I used to post a lot when I was younger, but these days I only share photos with close friends in a group chat, because I think some moments should stay private.
why: Javob + sabab (because you can look at them years later) va 'to be honest' diskurs belgisi — FC: javob kengaytirilgan.
Relative clause (the dishes my grandmother cooks) va 'Whenever...' ergash gapi — GRA uchun murakkab gap.
Solishtirma (sharper) va shart mayli (I'd be afraid of breaking it) — Band 6 grammatik xilma-xillik.
'used to' + 'these days' — o'tmish va hozirni solishtirish; 'stay private' — tabiiy kollokatsiya (LR).
class_ex.note: Mavzu: IELTS Speaking Part 1 to'plami (Taking photos). Namuna javoblar — Jony Academy original matni.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 2: A website or app that I use a lot
class_ex.instr: 1 daqiqa tayyorlanish (qog'ozga 5–6 kalit so'z), keyin 1–2 daqiqa to'xtovsiz gapiring; sherigingiz vaqtni o'lchaydi va S6_CLASS bo'yicha band qo'yadi.
items: Describe a website or app that you use a lot.
You should say:
what it is
how you found out about it
what you use it for
and explain why it is useful to you.
class_ex.answers: I'd like to talk about an online dictionary app that I use almost every day. It's a free app which explains English words in simple English and also gives example sentences and the pronunciation. I found out about it about two years ago, when I started my IELTS course in Samarkand. Our teacher noticed that I was translating every single word into Uzbek, so she recommended this app and showed us how to use it. Now I use it for several things. Firstly, when I come across a new word in a reading text, I check its meaning and copy one of the examples into my vocabulary notebook. Secondly, I listen to the pronunciation, because I often put the stress in the wrong place. It also sends me a word of the day, so I learn something new even when I'm not studying. The main reason it's so useful is that it saves me a lot of time. Before, I had to scroll through long lists of translations and guess which one was right. It's also really user-friendly, so even my younger brother has started using it. If I hadn't discovered it, my vocabulary would be much weaker now. The only downside is that it needs the internet, so it's useless on the bus to my village.
why: Kartochkaning 4 bandi tartib bilan yoritilgan (nima → qanday topdi → nima uchun ishlatadi → nega foydali) va Firstly / Secondly / The main reason bilan bog'langan — FC: izchil tuzilma.
Box iboralari (come across, saves me a lot of time, scroll through, user-friendly, the downside is that) o'z joyida — LR: mavzu lug'ati va 'less common' iboralar.
Past continuous (I was translating), present perfect (has started), relative clause (which explains...) va mixed conditional (If I hadn't discovered it, ... would be) — GRA: turli tuzilmalar.
Brend nomi yo'q — umumiy tavsif (an online dictionary app); shaxsiy misollar (Samarqanddagi kurs, ukasi, qishloqqa avtobus) javobni ishonarli qiladi.
box: to keep up with — (yangiliklar, o'qish) dan orqada qolmaslik, xabardor bo'lib turmoq
user-friendly — foydalanish oson, qulay
to come across — tasodifan duch kelmoq, uchratib qolmoq
a reliable source — ishonchli manba
to be glued to the screen — ekrandan ko'z uzmaslik
to scroll through — (ro'yxat, lenta) ni varaqlab ko'rib chiqmoq
it saves me a lot of time — bu menga ko'p vaqt tejaydi
the downside is that... — kamchiligi shundaki...
class_ex.note: Cue card va namuna monolog — Jony Academy original materiali (Unit 4 mavzusi: New media). Namunada brend nomi ataylab ishlatilmagan.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 3: The internet and young people
class_ex.instr: Ustoz savol beradi, 2–3 o'quvchi javob beradi: fikr → sabab → misol → qarama-qarshi fikr yoki xulosa (40–60 soniya).
items: How has the internet changed the way young people learn?
Can we trust the information we find online? How can we check it?
What are the dangers of spending too much time online?
Should parents limit their children's internet use?
answers: I'd say it has changed almost everything. In the past, students depended on textbooks and their teacher, but now they can watch video lessons, use online dictionaries and even take free courses from foreign universities. For example, many teenagers in Uzbekistan have learned English mainly through videos and podcasts. On the other hand, it is very easy to get distracted online, so young people need more self-discipline than their parents did.

Only partly, I think. Some websites are a reliable source, such as official or university pages, but a lot of what people share on social media is simply opinion or even fake news. The best way to check information is to compare two or three different sources and see who wrote it and when. If a story sounds too shocking to be true, it probably is, so it is worth waiting before you share it.

There are quite a few. The most obvious one is health: people who are glued to the screen for hours often sleep badly and hardly do any exercise. Another danger is that they spend less time with real people, which can make them feel lonely. What's more, endless scrolling can make it hard to concentrate on long tasks like reading a book. So I believe the problem is not the internet itself, but losing control of our time.

To some extent, yes, especially for younger children. Kids under ten cannot always judge what is safe, so it makes sense for parents to set clear rules, for instance no phones at the dinner table. However, with teenagers I think strict bans often backfire, because they simply find a way around them. A better approach would be to agree on limits together and explain the reasons, so that young people learn to manage their own screen time.
why: O'tmish va hozirni solishtirish (In the past... but now) + misol + qarama-qarshi fikr (On the other hand) — Part 3 uchun to'liq zanjir.
Savolning ikki qismiga ham javob berilgan (ishonsa bo'ladimi + qanday tekshirish); shart gap (If a story sounds...) — fikr to'liq va asoslangan.
Sanash (The most obvious one, Another danger, What's more) va xulosa gapi (So I believe...) — FC: fikr mantiqiy rivojlangan.
'To some extent' bilan qisman rozilik, yosh guruhlarini ajratish va yechim taklif qilish (A better approach would be...) — muvozanatli, Band 6.5 ga xos javob.
class_ex.note: Part 3 savollari jamiyat darajasida: 'I' emas, 'young people / parents / society' haqida gapiriladi; har javob 60–90 so'z.

tasks.title: Questions 1–6
tasks.type: TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN
tasks.instr: TRUE — matn xuddi shu ma'noni aytadi; FALSE — matn qarshisini aytadi; NOT GIVEN — matnda bu haqida ma'lumot yo'q. Kalit so'zlar (famous, original intention, politics, amateur, second galaxy project, Herbaria@home) matnning 1–4-xatboshilarida.
items: Tim Berners-Lee was famous for his research in physics before he invented the World Wide Web.
The original intention of the Web was to help manage one extremely complex project.
Tim Berners-Lee has also been active in politics.
The Web has allowed professional and amateur scientists to work together.
The second galaxy project aims to examine more galaxies than the first.
Herbaria@home's work will help to reduce the effects of climate change.
why: "A then little-known computer scientist" — mashhur emas edi, va u fizik emas, kompyuter olimi. Ikki tomondan ham qarshi.
"The Web was invented to deal with a specific problem" — LHC loyihasi; "How will we ever keep track of such a large project?"
"Political campaigning" — Web o'zgartirgan sohalardan biri. Berners-Lee o'zi siyosat bilan shug'ullangani haqida gap yo'q. So'z bor, da'vo yo'q.
"It also permits professional scientists to recruit thousands of amateurs to give them a hand". "Give a hand" = yordam berish, birga ishlash.
Birinchisi — bir million rasm; keyingisi — "the brightest quarter of a million of them in finer detail". Ko'proq emas, kamroq (lekin batafsilroq).
Loyiha iqlim o'zgarishi ta'sirida turlar tarqalishini KUZATADI ("track the changes"), ta'sirini kamaytirishi haqida gap yo'q.
tasks.note: 3- va 6-savol — darsning asosiy NOT GIVEN namunasi: mavzu (politics, climate change) matnda bor, lekin savoldagi da'vo yo'q.

tasks.type: Complete the notes below. Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage for each answer.

why: "Scientists made observations about the sizes of human social networks using data from Facebook". "Investigate" = "made observations about".
"The majority of the messages were directed at a few specific friends". "Most" = "the majority of"; "limited number of people" = "a few specific friends".

"Dr Huberman has also helped uncover several laws of web surfing, including the number of times an average person will go from web page to web page on a given site". "Laws" emas — nimani tekshirgani: web surfing.
"A few sites on a given subject attract most of the attention, and the rest get very little" — "winner takes all" hodisasi.
tasks.note: 9-savolda ba'zi o'quvchilar "laws" yoki "laws of web surfing" yozadi. Birinchisi ma'noni bermaydi, ikkinchisi — uch so'z. Notes grammatikasiga eng mosi — "web surfing".

"Although people have tried to have scientific research reviewed in the same way, most researchers only accept reviews from a few anonymous experts".
"When Nature ... experimented with open peer review in 2006" — mualliflarga maqolasini Web'da muhokamaga qo'yishni taklif qilgan. Jurnal nomi — katta harf bilan.

tasks.title: Questions 1–6
tasks.type: TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN
tasks.instr: TRUE — matn xuddi shu ma'noni aytadi; FALSE — matn qarshisini aytadi; NOT GIVEN — matnda bu haqida ma'lumot yo'q.
items: Some people believe that modern electronic media only have a negative effect on young people.
Nicholas Carr's book on the subject is a bestseller.
Nicholas Carr believes that electronic media have affected his enjoyment of reading books.
Gary Small's research supports Nicholas Carr's beliefs.
Management beliefs on multi-tasking are proved correct by scientific research.

why: "The human mind, particularly the young mind" va "We are, say the worriers, losing the ability..." — tashvish hammaga ("the human mind", "we"), ayniqsa yoshlarga tegishli; "only ... young people" matnga zid. Yakuniy javob: FALSE. NOT GIVEN qabul qilinmaydi: matnda qarshi isbot gap bor.
Kitob nomi (The Shallows) bor, lekin sotuv yoki mashhurligi haqida gap yo'q.

"Years of internet use have, he suspects, dented his ability to read deeply, to absorb himself in books"; uzun matnda "fidgety" bo'lib qoladi. "Believes" = "suspects"; "affected" = "dented"; "enjoyment of reading books" = "to absorb himself in books" (kitobga berilib, zavq bilan o'qish). Yakuniy javob: TRUE. FALSE ham, NOT GIVEN ham qabul qilinmaydi: ta'sir borligi isbot gapda aniq aytilgan.
"For Carr, this is proof that the net can rewire the mind" — Small tadqiqoti Carr fikrini tasdiqlaydi.
"Modern management tends to promote multi-tasking ... Science, on the other hand, does not".
Meyer fikri keltirilgan ("it's a myth"), lekin u bahs-munozara qo'zg'atgani haqida gap yo'q. "People may think otherwise" — bahs emas.

Ustoz sinfda "isbot gap qaysi?" deb so'rasin. 1-savolda cheklovchi so'z "only" matnga zid: tashvish faqat yoshlar haqida emas ("the human mind, particularly the young mind") — FALSE. 3-savolda so'zlar boshqa, ma'no bir xil: "affected his enjoyment of reading books" = "dented his ability ... to absorb himself in books" — TRUE. Qoida: so'z o'zgargani javobni NOT GIVEN qilmaydi, javobni isbot gap hal qiladi.

readings.title: Practice 1: Podcasts — radio for the internet age
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 1 darajasi)
text: In 2004, a journalist writing for a British newspaper was looking for a name for a new kind of radio. Programmes could now be recorded as digital files and downloaded from the internet onto portable music players, so listeners no longer had to tune in at a fixed time. Among the names he suggested was 'podcasting', a combination of 'iPod', the most popular music player of the day, and 'broadcasting'. The word caught on so quickly that, within a year, it had been chosen as word of the year by a major American dictionary.

At first, podcasts were made mainly by amateurs: teachers recording their lessons, fans discussing their favourite football team, or friends chatting about films. Equipment was cheap, and anyone with a microphone and a laptop could publish a programme. Traditional radio stations were slow to react. Many of them saw podcasts as a hobby rather than a threat, and it was several years before they began to offer their own programmes for download.

The real growth came with the smartphone. Once people could download and play episodes on a device they carried everywhere, listening became part of daily routines such as commuting, cooking and exercising. One survey of listeners in several countries found that more than half usually listened while doing something else. Perhaps surprisingly, the most common place to listen was at home, with the car in second place.

Podcasts differ from radio in several important ways. Because there is no schedule, an episode can be any length: some last ten minutes, others more than three hours. There are also far fewer rules about content. Presenters can explore a narrow subject in great depth, knowing that even a small audience scattered around the world may be enough to make the programme worthwhile. Many listeners say that podcasts feel more personal than radio, as if the presenter were talking directly to them.

Making money, however, has been a challenge. Most podcasts are free, so producers depend on advertising, which is usually read aloud by the presenter at the start or in the middle of an episode. Some ask listeners for voluntary donations, while a smaller number charge a monthly subscription for extra episodes. People who study the industry point out that only a small proportion of podcasts earn enough to pay their makers a full salary; for the majority, it remains a part-time activity.

Perhaps the most surprising development is the return of the long spoken story. Many successful podcasts are investigations that follow a single case over ten or twenty episodes, and some of these have been turned into television series. For an audience that is said to have a short attention span, listeners seem remarkably willing to spend hours with a good storyteller.

readings.title: Practice 2: Local news in the digital age
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 1 darajasi)
text: For most of the twentieth century, local newspapers were at the centre of community life. They reported on council meetings, school sports results and planning decisions, and they carried the advertisements through which people sold cars, rented flats and found jobs. In many towns, the local paper was also the only source of information about the courts and the police.

The internet changed this business very quickly. Classified advertisements, which had once provided a large part of a local paper's income, moved to free websites. At the same time, readers began to expect news to be free online. As a result, a great many local titles have closed or merged over the last two decades, and many of those that survive employ only a handful of reporters.

The effect has not been the same everywhere. Papers in large cities have often survived by building strong websites and attracting readers from outside their area, while those in small towns and rural districts have found it much harder. In some regions there is now no local reporter at all, a situation that journalists describe as a 'news desert'. Residents in such places may know more about events in the capital than about decisions taken by their own council.

Researchers have begun to study what happens when a town loses its newspaper. One study in the United States compared towns that had lost their paper with similar towns that had not. It found that in the first group, fewer people stood as candidates in local elections, and the cost of borrowing money for public projects rose. The researchers suggest that without reporters watching, local government becomes less efficient.

Not everyone agrees that the picture is so bleak. Social media groups now allow residents to share news about road closures, lost pets and local events within minutes, and some groups have more members than the local paper ever had readers. However, critics point out that such groups rarely check facts, and that rumours can spread as quickly as real news. Volunteers who run the groups are also unlikely to sit through a three-hour council meeting.

New models are appearing. Some local news sites are run as non-profit organisations and funded by donations from readers and grants from charitable foundations. Others ask readers to become members and pay a small monthly fee. A few towns have experimented with journalism students reporting on local affairs as part of their university course, supervised by experienced editors.

Whether any of these models can replace the traditional newspaper is still unclear. What is clear is that people value local news more than they are willing to pay for it: surveys regularly show that most residents think local journalism is important, but only a small minority have ever paid for it.

stand as a candidate — nomzod bo'lib qatnashmoq

readings.title: Practice 3 (uyga): The digital detox
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 1 darajasi), uy vazifasi
text: A growing number of people are choosing to take a break from their phones, laptops and social media accounts. The practice, known as a 'digital detox', can last anything from a single evening to several weeks. Hotels in some countries now offer detox holidays, in which guests hand in their devices at reception on arrival and receive them back only when they leave.

The idea is not entirely new. For centuries, religious traditions have encouraged periods of silence and withdrawal from daily life, and some families have long kept mealtimes free of television. What is new is the scale of the habit that people are trying to break. Many adults now spend more of their waking hours looking at a screen than doing anything else, and for teenagers the figure is often higher still.

Supporters argue that constant connection has costs. Notifications interrupt concentration, and many people check their phones many times a day without really noticing. Using screens late in the evening has also been linked to poor sleep, partly because bright light from screens can delay the body's release of melatonin, the hormone that makes us feel sleepy.

In one small experiment, researchers at a university asked a group of students to give up social media for a week, while a second group continued as normal. At the end of the week, the first group reported feeling less anxious and more satisfied with their lives. However, the effect was modest, and the researchers noted that the students knew the purpose of the study, which may have influenced their answers.

Critics of the detox movement make several points. First, many jobs now depend on being online, so a complete break is unrealistic for most workers. Second, the internet is where many people keep in touch with family and friends, especially those who live far away. Cutting this link, they argue, may increase loneliness rather than reduce it. Finally, a short break may achieve little if people simply return to their old habits afterwards.

For this reason, many psychologists now recommend small, permanent changes rather than dramatic breaks. Suggestions include switching off all non-essential notifications, keeping phones out of the bedroom, and choosing a fixed time in the evening after which screens are not used. Some people use apps that record how long they spend on each website, which can be a surprising experience. Others simply leave their phone in another room while they work or study, so that checking it requires a deliberate decision.

The irony, of course, is that much of the advice about disconnecting is found online. Even so, the popularity of the idea suggests that many people feel their relationship with technology needs to change.

kahoot.q: A passage has T/F/NG, note completion and short-answer questions. What should you do first?
options: Map each question group to a part of the text
Read the whole passage slowly, word by word
Learn every glossary word before reading
kahoot.explain: Avval uchala savol guruhiga 2 daqiqa ko'z yugurtirib, har biri matnning qaysi qismiga tegishli ekanini belgilaymiz (xarita usuli).

kahoot.q: Limit: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS. Which answer gets 0 marks, even if its meaning is right?
kahoot.explain: Artikl 'a' ham so'z sanaladi: 'a public library' — 3 so'z, chegara buziladi va javob 0 ball oladi.

kahoot.q: What is the key difference between FALSE and NOT GIVEN?
options: FALSE: the text says the opposite
FALSE: the idea is not in the text
NOT GIVEN: the words are changed
NOT GIVEN: the topic is too hard
kahoot.explain: FALSE uchun matnda qarama-qarshi isbot gap bor; isbot gap umuman bo'lmasa — NOT GIVEN.

kahoot.q: Text: 'Both teachers and students use the new app.' Statement: 'Only students use the new app.' Answer?
options: TRUE – the students do use the app
NOT GIVEN – the app is not named
TRUE – the text says the app is new
kahoot.explain: 'Only' kabi cheklovchi so'z matndagi 'both' ga zid — javob FALSE.

kahoot.q: Text: 'Fewer than half of the users are over 40.' Statement: 'Most users are over 40.' Answer?
options: FALSE – less than half is not most
NOT GIVEN – no exact number is given
kahoot.explain: 'Fewer than half' (yarmidan kami) va 'most' (ko'pchilik) bir-biriga zid — FALSE.

kahoot.q: Text: 'The festival is popular with local families.' Statement: 'The festival was started by a local family.' Answer?
options: NOT GIVEN – its founder is not mentioned
FALSE – families only visit the festival
TRUE – the festival is very popular
kahoot.explain: 'Local families' so'zlari matnda bor, lekin festivalni kim boshlagani haqida gap yo'q — NOT GIVEN.

kahoot.q: The notes are headed 'Funding of the project'. Which part of the passage should you read?
options: The part about money for the project
The first and the last paragraphs only
The part with the most difficult words
kahoot.explain: Notes sarlavhasi kerakli xatboshini ko'rsatadi: 'funding' — pul, moliyalashtirish haqidagi qism.

kahoot.q: Notes: 'Several ___ were built near the river.' What kind of word is needed?
kahoot.explain: 'Several' dan keyin va 'were' oldidan ko'plikdagi ot keladi (masalan, factories).

kahoot.q: Short answer: 'Where did the team first test the robot?' Which answer fits the question?
kahoot.explain: 'Where' joy so'raydi; vaqt, odamlar yoki sabab bu savolga javob bo'lmaydi.

kahoot.q: Question: 'What did the students build?' Text: 'The students built a small wooden bridge.' Limit: TWO WORDS. Best answer?
kahoot.explain: Savoldagi fe'l ('built') takrorlanmaydi; 'a wooden bridge' va 'small wooden bridge' — 3 so'z, chegaradan oshadi. To'g'ri javob — 2 so'zli 'wooden bridge'.

kahoot.q: Limit: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER. Which answer is acceptable?
kahoot.explain: Raqam alohida hisoblanadi: '250 students' — raqam + bitta so'z; qolganlarida so'z uchta.

kahoot.q: The passage spells 'colour'. You write 'color' in your answer. Is it accepted?
options: No – you must copy every letter
Yes – but you lose half a mark
kahoot.explain: IELTS'da britancha va amerikacha imlo ikkalasi ham qabul qilinadi; faqat bitta ishda bir xil imlodan foydalaning.

kahoot.q: An 'amateur' photographer is someone who…
options: takes photos as a hobby, not a job
kahoot.explain: amateur — havaskor: ishni pul uchun emas, qiziqish uchun qiladigan odam.

kahoot.q: 'Anonymous' comments are written by people who…
kahoot.explain: anonymous — ismi oshkor etilmagan, noma'lum muallif.

kahoot.q: Complete: 'A free lunch is a good ___ for staff to arrive on time.'
kahoot.explain: incentive — rag'bat: odamni biror ishni qilishga undaydigan sabab.

kahoot.q: 'Superficial' learning is learning that is…
kahoot.explain: superficial — yuzaki: chuqur emas, faqat ustki qismini qamragan.

kahoot.q: Complete: 'The club hopes to ___ fifty new volunteers this year.'
kahoot.explain: recruit — (a'zo, ko'ngilli, xodim) jalb qilmoq, yollamoq.

kahoot.q: Complete: 'With so many emails, it is hard to ___ which ones I have answered.'
kahoot.explain: keep track of — hisobini yuritmoq, kuzatib bormoq: qaysi xatlarga javob berganimni kuzatib borish qiyin.

kahoot.q: Complete: 'The school changed its rules ___ complaints from parents.'
kahoot.explain: in response to — javoban: ota-onalarning shikoyatlariga javoban qoidalar o'zgartirildi.

kahoot.q: Doctors found 'a correlation between' exercise and good sleep. This means…
options: exercise has no effect on sleep
the doctors studied it at night
kahoot.explain: a correlation between — ikki narsa o'rtasidagi bog'liqlik; bu biri ikkinchisiga albatta sabab bo'ladi degani emas.

intro: Section 4 — bitta ma'ruzachi akademik mavzuda gapiradi (ma'ruza, taqdimot). Oraliq tanaffus yo'q, shuning uchun tayyorlanish vaqtida 10 savolning HAMMASINI ko'rib chiqish kerak. Ma'ruzachi faqat fakt emas, fikr va maslahat ham beradi.

6.0 darajasida Section 4 ko'pincha ikki xil completion turidan iborat: gap (sentence) yoki summary completion va flow chart. Ikkalasida ham asosiy ish — bo'shliq GRAMMATIKASI: "a ___ or a video" — birlikdagi ot; "of little interest to a large ___" — ot; "earn money from ___" — ot yoki -ing.

Flow chart — jarayon bosqichlari, strelkalar bilan. Ma'ruzachi bosqichlarni signal so'zlar bilan ajratadi: "First of all", "Then", "Remember", "Once you've written...", "And another thing", "Finally". Signal so'zni eshitsangiz, keyingi qutiga o'ting.

Paraphrase: savoldagi so'z audioda boshqacha keladi. "Include ___ from people involved" = "put in quotations from people who are part of the story"; "check the accuracy of" = "make sure that ... are correct". Kalit so'zni emas, MA'NONI kuting.

TUZOQ: ma'ruzachi bir nechta mos keladigan so'zni aytadi. "Write a report ... take a photo ... make a video" — gapda "video" allaqachon bor, "a ___" — birlikdagi ot: photo. Workbook'da "web log" (1997) va "we blog" (1999) — savoldagi yilga qarang.

So'z chegarasi: Student's Book'da Q1–5 — ONE OR TWO WORDS, Q6–10 — ONE WORD ONLY. "quotations from people" — faqat "quotations". Imtihonda kitobda berilgan har ikki imlo ham qabul qilinadi (organisation / organization), lekin xato imlo — 0 ball.
Transfer: ko'plik -s, imlo va so'z soni. Flow chart'da kitob "quotes/quotations" ikkalasini qabul qiladi — lekin ikki variantni birga yozmang.
formulas: check the accuracy = make sure ... correct
presentation: Section 4 da tanaffus yo'q. Qachon o'qiyman?
Faqat boshidagi tayyorlanish vaqtida. Shuning uchun 1–10 ni bir yo'la ko'rib chiqing va so'z turini qalam bilan yozib qo'ying.
Flow chart'da qutilar tartibi o'zgarishi mumkinmi?
Deyarli yo'q: flow chart jarayon tartibida, audio ham shu tartibda.
Bo'shliqni o'tkazib yubordim. Nima qilaman?
Keyingi qutiga o'ting. Signal so'z eshitilsa, demak oldingi bosqich tugagan. Oxirida bo'sh qolganiga taxminiy so'z turini yozing.
Eshitgan so'zim bo'shliqqa grammatik mos kelmayapti.
Ehtimol noto'g'ri so'zni ushladingiz yoki ko'plik/birlik farq qiladi. Kitob maslahati: iloji bo'lsa eshitgan so'zingizni yozing.
"ONE WORD ONLY" da "a pyramid" deb yozsam-chi?
Artikl ham so'z hisoblanadi: "a" gapda allaqachon bor, faqat "pyramid".
Ma'ruzachi fikr bildirsa, bu ham javobmi?
Ha, Section 4 da ko'pincha shunday: "I think the main cause..." — fikr ham savol bo'lishi mumkin.
notes: 5.0 da sentence completion va flow chart'ni alohida o'rgangan edik. Endi ular bitta Section 4 ma'ruzasida, tanaffussiz ketma-ket keladi — asosiy ko'nikma: 10 bo'shliqni oldindan tayyorlash.
Tekshiruvda har javobdan keyin skriptdagi gapni ekranga chiqaring va signal so'zni boshqa rang bilan ko'rsating.
Kuchli o'quvchilarga: Workbook audiosini 1.25 tezlikda tinglash yoki Jony Academy skriptini o'quvchining o'zi sinfga o'qib berishi.

Grammatika bo'limidagi SB/WB misollari (Tushuntirish kartasidagi tuzoq, paraphrase, so'z chegarasi va imlo misollari, savol-javobdagi ONE WORD ONLY savoli, Tipik xatolar jadvali) shu darsdagi SB va WB javoblarining o'zi. Tushuntirish va Tipik xatolar kartalari proyektor rejimida ham ko'rinadi — grammatika bo'limini tinglashlardan oldin proyektorga chiqarmang. Doskadagi 10 daqiqalik tushuntirishda strategiyani umumiy misol bilan bering, masalan: ONE WORD ONLY — "Take a ___ with you", eshitiladi "a warm jacket" → jacket; tuzoq — "Lunch is in the hall, and dinner is in the garden", savol "Dinner is served in the ___" → garden. SB/WB misolini esa o'sha savolni tekshirganda ko'rsating — aks holda WB imtihon rejimi va uning normativi (10 dan 8) ma'nosini yo'qotadi. Lug'at jadvali ham (headline, quotation, figures, source, local, advertising va ularning misollari) SB va Jony javoblarini ochadi — uni tinglashlardan keyin oching.

"any figures you quote are correct" — raqamlar
Birinchi nom so'ralgan; keyingi nom — tuzoq

Har o'quvchi o'zi kuzatadigan bitta blog, kanal yoki sahifa haqida 3 gap aytadi, har gapda bitta yangi so'z.
