class_ex.title: Bo'shliq turini oldindan aytish (SB, 2- va 4-mashq)
class_ex.instr: Tinglashdan oldin: har bo'shliqqa qanday so'z kerak — ot/fe'l/sifat, birlik yoki ko'plik?
items: 1 — "a news story, a ___ or a video"
2 — "of little interest to a large ___"
3 — "used to write a ___"
4 — "more likely to be a ___ rather than national"
5 — "earn money from ___"
6 — "in the shape of a ___"
7 — "Include ___ from people involved"
8 — "Check the accuracy of your ___"
9 — "Don't write a ___"
10 — "write an attractive ___"
why: "a ___ or a video" — video ga o'xshash narsa: artikl "a" — birlik.
"a large ___" — katta nima? Ko'p odamlar yoki tashkilot.
"write a ___" — yoziladigan narsa: xat, maqola.
"a ___ rather than national or international news" — mavzu turi.
"from ___" — daromad manbasi.
"the shape of a ___" — geometrik shakl.
"from people involved" — odamlardan olinadigan narsa, ko'plik.
"your ___" — tekshiriladigan narsalar: raqamlar, faktlar.
"a ___" — maqolaning qismi.
"an attractive ___" — maqola ustida ishlashning oxirgi bosqichida yoziladigan qism (flow chart'da "Finally").
class_ex.note: "a" / "an" artikli — birlik belgisi. 10-savolda "an" "attractive" ga tegishli, javobning o'zi haqida hech narsa demaydi.

class_ex.title: Signal so'zlar: flow chart'ning qaysi qutisi?
class_ex.instr: Ustoz gapni o'qiydi. O'quvchilar: bu yangi bosqichmi, qaysi bosqich va qaysi so'z signal berdi?
items: "First of all, you need to choose a topic you really care about."
"Once you've written your article, go over it again."
"And another thing to bear in mind: people online stop reading quickly."
"Then ask a friend to read your draft."
"Finally, read the whole text aloud one last time."
why: "First of all" — flow chart'ning birinchi qutisi.
"Once you've..." — oldingi bosqich tugaganini bildiradi.
"Another thing" — qo'shimcha qadam yoki maslahat.
"Then" — ketma-ketlik.
"Finally" — oxirgi quti. Bu so'zni eshitsangiz, oldingi bo'shliqlarga qaytmang.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 1: Laughter
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda so'rang va javob bering; har javob 2–3 gap: javob + sabab/misol (because, for example, to be honest).
items: What usually makes you laugh?
Do you enjoy watching funny videos online?
Do you like spending time with people who make you laugh?
Do you think laughing is good for our health?
answers: Well, mostly my friends, to be honest. We have a group chat where someone is always posting silly jokes, and my younger brother's impressions of our neighbours make me burst out laughing every single time.
Yes, quite a lot, although I try not to overdo it. I usually watch short comedy clips after I finish my homework because they help me relax, but I've noticed they can easily eat up a whole hour.
Definitely. My best friend Sardor has a great sense of humour, which makes even a boring bus journey enjoyable. If I'm in a bad mood, he's the first person I call.
Absolutely. I've read that laughing reduces stress and even helps you sleep better. For example, after a tough exam, watching a comedy with my family always makes me feel much lighter.
why: 'to be honest' diskurs belgisi, 'where' bilan relative clause va 'burst out laughing' kam uchraydigan iborasi.
'although' bilan cheklov, 'because' bilan sabab, present perfect ('I've noticed') va 'eat up' frazali fe'li.
'a great sense of humour' kollokatsiyasi, 'which makes...' relative clause va 1-tur shart gap (If I'm ..., he's ...).
Present perfect ('I've read'), 'For example' bilan aniq misol va solishtirma 'much lighter' — javob + sabab + misol.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 2: Interesting news online
class_ex.instr: 1 daqiqa tayyorlanish (qog'ozga 5–6 kalit so'z), keyin 1–2 daqiqa to'xtovsiz gapiring; sherigingiz vaqtni o'lchaydi va S6_CLASS bo'yicha band qo'yadi.
items: Describe a piece of news that you read or watched online and found interesting.
You should say:
what the news was about
where you saw it
how you checked whether it was true
and explain why it interested you.
answers: I'd like to talk about a story that caught my eye about two months ago. It was about a seventeen-year-old student from Namangan who had invented a pair of glasses that warns drivers when they are falling asleep. There's a small sensor inside, and if your eyes stay closed for more than two seconds, the glasses beep loudly.

I saw it on a Telegram news channel while I was scrolling through my phone on the bus. The headline was something like 'Teenager's invention could save lives', and by the evening the video had gone viral among my classmates.

To be honest, my first reaction was to take it with a pinch of salt, because many stories online turn out to be exaggerated. So I decided to fact-check it. I searched for the student's name and found the same story on two trustworthy sources: a national news website and the official page of his school, which had photos from the science competition he had won.

The main reason it interested me is that I'm keen on engineering myself. It showed me that you don't need a huge laboratory to solve a real problem. If you're curious and patient, even a school project can make a difference.
why: FC: cue card tartibida — nima → qayerda → qanday tekshirdi → nega qiziq; 'To be honest', 'So', 'The main reason' bilan bog'langan, taxminan 1:50 gapiriladi.
LR: box iboralari (caught my eye, headline, gone viral, take it with a pinch of salt, fact-check, trustworthy sources) o'z joyida; 'scrolling through my phone', 'keen on' tabiiy.
GRA: past perfect ('had invented', 'had won'), past continuous ('was scrolling'), relative clause (who/which), 1-tur shart gap (if your eyes stay closed ... beep).
Nega Band 7 emas: fikrlar oddiy, idioma va nozik ma'noli iboralar cheklangan — Band 6–6.5 uchun namunaviy daraja.
box: to go viral — internetda tez tarqalib ketmoq
breaking news — endigina kelgan shoshilinch yangilik
to fact-check — faktlarni tekshirib ko'rmoq
a trustworthy source — ishonchli manba
to catch my eye — e'tiborimni tortmoq
a headline — sarlavha
to spread misinformation — noto'g'ri ma'lumot tarqatmoq
to take something with a pinch of salt — biror narsaga shubha bilan qaramoq
class_ex.note: Namuna — Jony Academy original matni (yangilik to'qima). Ustoz o'qiydi (taxminan 1:50); o'quvchilar box iboralarini eshitganda qo'l ko'taradi.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 3: Citizen journalism and fake news
class_ex.instr: Ustoz savol beradi, 2–3 o'quvchi javob beradi: fikr → sabab → misol → qarama-qarshi fikr yoki xulosa (har javob 30–40 soniya).
items: Why are blogs and social media becoming more popular than newspapers?
Should ordinary people be allowed to report the news?
What can be done to stop the spread of fake news?
answers: I think the main reason is convenience. Most people, especially the young, carry a phone everywhere, so they can read the news for free the moment it happens, whereas a newspaper only comes out once a day. Social media is also interactive, because readers can comment and share their own opinions. On the other hand, this speed has a cost: posts are rarely checked as carefully as newspaper articles.

Yes, I believe they should, because ordinary people are often in the right place at the right time. For example, when there's a flood or a road accident, a passer-by with a phone can film it long before journalists arrive. However, citizen reporters aren't trained, so their reports may be one-sided. In my view, their videos are most useful when professional journalists check them before they are published.

Well, I don't think it can be stopped completely, but it can certainly be reduced. Firstly, schools could teach media literacy, so that teenagers learn how to check a source before sharing anything. Secondly, social media companies should label posts that have been shown to be false. Finally, each of us has a responsibility: if we aren't sure a story is true, the best option is simply not to share it.
why: Strategiya: fikr (convenience) → sabab (phone, free, instant) → 'whereas' bilan solishtirish → 'On the other hand' qarama-qarshi fikr.
Fikr → sabab → misol (flood, road accident) → 'However' bilan cheklov → 'In my view' xulosa; dars lug'ati (in the right place at the right time) qayta ishlatiladi.
Takliflar Firstly / Secondly / Finally bilan tartiblangan; passive ('can be reduced', 'have been shown'), 'so that' maqsad ergash gapi va shart gap bor.

listenings.title: Student's Book, Track 15: Amateur journalism (Q1–5)
intro: Ma'ruzachi havaskor jurnalistika haqida gapiradi: nima uchun u o'sib bormoqda va odamlar nima haqida yozadi. Tinglashdan oldin Q1–10 ning hammasini ko'rib chiqing (Section 4 da tanaffus yo'q).
Ko'rsatma: Write ONE OR TWO WORDS for each answer. Savollar sahifasi quyida rasm sifatida.

tasks.title: Questions 1–5
tasks.type: Complete the sentences below. Write ONE OR TWO WORDS for each answer.
tasks.instr: Gap tartibi = ma'ruza tartibi. Bo'shliq grammatikasini oldindan belgilang.
items: 1 Ordinary people can provide a news story, a ___ or a video when no professional journalist is present.
2 Amateur journalists often report on subjects which would be of little interest to a large ___.
3 In the past, someone who wanted to express an opinion used to write a ___, while now they write a blog.
4 An amateur journalist's subject is more likely to be a ___ rather than national or international news.
5 Amateur news websites, such as Ohmynews in South Korea, earn money from ___.
why: "They can take a photo with a digital camera or use their mobile phone to make a video film". Tuzoq: "write a report" — bu "news story" ga to'g'ri keladi, u gapda allaqachon bor.
"Things which a big organisation might not be interested in". "Of little interest to" = "might not be interested in"; "large" = "big".
"One of the few ways of doing this was to send a letter to a newspaper". "Express an opinion" = "make your opinions known"; "blog" gapda bor.
"Amateur journalists often write about something which is a local issue". Keyin misollar: maktab, shahardagi tirbandlik.
"They can attract advertising and get income from this". "Earn money" = "get income".
tasks.note: 1-savol — darsning asosiy namunasi: audioda uchta mos so'z (report, photo, video) bor, bo'shliqqa grammatika va gapdagi so'zlar faqat bittasini qoldiradi.

tasks.title: Questions 6–10 — How to write an article
tasks.type: Complete the flow chart below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.
tasks.instr: Bosqichlar audio tartibida. Har qutida kalit g'oyani paraphrase bilan kuting.
why: "The best model is really shaped like a pyramid". "In the shape of" = "shaped like".
"A really good technique for doing that is to put in quotations from people who are part of the story". "Include" = "put in"; "people involved" = "people who are part of the story".
"Make sure that any figures you quote are correct". "Check the accuracy" = "make sure ... correct". Misol: Tanyaning bolalari soni.
"Don't put in a conclusion — just let your article end without it".
"Finally, you need to write a headline — something eye-catching". "Attractive" = "eye-catching".
tasks.note: 8-savolda "facts" yozganlarga skriptni ko'rsating: ma'ruzachi "figures" deydi va raqam misolini keltiradi (two children, not one or three).
rows: Put the main facts at the beginning to attract attention.
Use a model in the shape of a (6) to build up details.
Rewrite, making sure paragraphs are short.

listenings.title: Workbook, Track 5: Blogs and blogging (Q1–10)
listenings.qtype: Summary completion + Flow-chart completion — imtihon rejimi
intro: Mutaxassis bloglar va blog yuritish haqida ma'ruza qiladi. Avval Workbook 1-mashqini bajaring: Q6–10 dan qaysi uchtasiga ot kerak?
Keyin imtihondagidek: tayyorlanish vaqti, audio BIR MARTA, 10 savol. Q1–5 — ONE OR TWO WORDS, Q6–10 — ONE WORD ONLY.

tasks.title: 1-mashq: qaysi uchta bo'shliqqa ot kerak?
tasks.type: Og'zaki
tasks.instr: Tinglashdan oldin Q6–10 ni ko'zdan kechiring.
items: Which three questions (6–10) need a noun to fill the gap?
why: 6 "the ___ of your posts" — ot; 7 "a record of ___ and links" — ko'plikdagi ot; 9 "the ___ relating to the post" — ot. 8 "to ___ a post" — fe'l; 10 "say ___" — bu yerga aytiladigan so'z yoki ibora keladi: gap tuzilishidan uning ot ekanini oldindan aytib bo'lmaydi. Shuning uchun Workbook kaliti — 6, 7, 9 (10-savol haqida batafsil — Q6–10 tekshiruvida; tinglashdan oldin javobni aytmang).

tasks.title: Questions 1–5 — Blogs and the history of blogging
tasks.type: Complete the summary below. Write ONE OR TWO WORDS for each answer.
tasks.instr: Summary ma'ruzaning birinchi yarmiga tegishli. Yillar (1994, 1999) — langar.
items: 1 Blogs are usually not ___ because they have interactive elements...
2 ...which may lead to friendships or even ___ relationships between people.
3 The first 'blog' was probably created in 1994 by a student and he called it his '___'.
4 Similar websites were then created and these included both links and ___.
5 In 1999, someone changed the term used for these websites by creating the phrase '___'.
why: "Most blogs are not monologues, because they allow readers to make their own comments". "Interactive elements" = o'quvchi izohlari.
"Perhaps making friends or even doing business with each other". "Friendships" summary'da bor.
"His site was called Justin's Home Page". Tuzoq: "he later called it Links From The Underground" — keyingi nom.
"With links to other websites and forums for people to contribute their personal opinions".
"In 1999, a blogger called Peter Merholz jokingly broke this word up into 'we blog'". Tuzoq: "web log" — 1997, Jorn Barger.
tasks.note: 5-savolda "web log" yozganlar ko'p bo'ladi. Summary'dagi yilni (1999) ko'rsating va "changed the term" — mavjud atamani o'zgartirish ekanini tushuntiring.

tasks.title: Questions 6–10 — Blogging workflow: advice
tasks.type: Complete the flow chart below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.
tasks.instr: Ma'ruzaning ikkinchi yarmi: "OK, now let's move on to how to run a blog". Bosqichlarni signal so'zlar bilan kuzating.
why: "First of all, you need to decide on the frequency of your blog posts". Keyin misollar: "several a day ... once a week".
"Open a file for storing the sources of your information and the links". "Keep a record of" = "storing".
"Announce it by sending links to it on social networking sites". "Outstanding" = "particularly good ... really proud of".
"Then check your blog statistics to see how many people are reading".

"Give them a proper reply rather than just saying thanks". "Don't simply say" = "rather than just saying". 1-mashqqa izoh: "thanks" grammatik jihatdan ot (ko'plikda), lekin tinglashdan oldin "say ___" dan faqat "aytiladigan so'z yoki ibora" kutiladi — shuning uchun Workbook kaliti 6, 7, 9; o'quvchilarga shuni tushuntiring.
rows: Decide what the (6) of your posts will be.
Do some reading before starting a post.
As you compose the post, keep a record of (7) and links.
After creating the post, add some tags to it to improve searchability.
Use social networking sites to (8) a post you think is outstanding.
Look at the (9) relating to the post.
Don't simply say (10) to people who have responded to your post.
Go on to other blogs and leave comments.

listenings.title: Jony Academy mashqi: Checking a news story before you share it
intro: Ma'ruza: onlayn yolg'on xabarlar va ularni tekshirish usuli. 45 soniya tayyorlanish; ma'ruza BIR MARTA.
Ko'rsatma: Q1–5 — ONE OR TWO WORDS; Q6–10 — ONE WORD ONLY.
transcript: [Ustoz uchun] Ustoz tabiiy tezlikda, BIR MARTA o'qiydi.
[Ustoz uchun] Savollarni doskaga yoki varaqqa yozing (Q1–5 gaplari va Q6–10 flow chart qutilari) — tinglashdan oldin.

LECTURER: Good morning, everyone. Today I'm going to talk about false information online — what people often call 'fake news'. In the first part I'll look at why it spreads so easily, and in the second part I'll give you a simple method for checking a story before you share it.

LECTURER: Let's start with a little history. False stories are nothing new. For centuries, rumours were passed from person to person, and later they appeared in printed leaflets and newspapers. What has changed is speed. Today, a false story on social media can reach millions of people in a single afternoon — long before anyone publishes a correction.

LECTURER: So why do people share these stories? You might expect the main reason to be that people want to trick others. In fact, research suggests that most people who share false information believe it is true. What matters is how a story makes us feel. Stories that cause strong emotions — especially anger or surprise — are shared far more often than calm, factual reports.

LECTURER: We are also much more likely to trust a story if it's passed on by a friend. And the effect is even stronger when it comes from a family member — even if that person has no idea where the story originally came from.

LECTURER: Pictures are another problem. A photograph can be completely genuine, but it may have been taken years earlier, or in a different country, and then presented as today's news. Many people assume that a photo is proof. It isn't.

LECTURER: Now, you might think that young people are better at spotting false stories, because they've grown up with the internet. Actually, studies of university students have found that many of them struggle to tell the difference between news and advertising — especially when an advert has been designed to look like an ordinary article.

LECTURER: So, how can you protect yourself? Here's a method I recommend. The first step is simply to stop. Don't share anything immediately, however exciting it seems. That pause is the most important part of the whole process.
LECTURER: Next, look at the source. Who actually published this story? If you don't recognise the website, find its 'About' page and see who runs it.
LECTURER: Then read beyond the headline. Headlines are written to attract clicks, and sometimes the article itself says something quite different — or much less dramatic.
LECTURER: After that, check the date. Old stories are often shared again as if they were new, particularly after a disaster or during an election.

LECTURER: The next step is to search for the same story on other websites. If something really important has happened, several reliable news organisations will be reporting it. If you can only find it in one place, be suspicious.

LECTURER: And finally, if the story includes a photo, do a reverse image search. This shows you where else the picture has appeared online, and when it was first published. If the story passes all these checks, then by all means share it. If it doesn't — the best thing you can do is nothing at all.

tasks.title: Questions 1–5
tasks.type: Complete the sentences below. Write ONE OR TWO WORDS for each answer.
tasks.instr: Bo'shliq turini oldindan belgilang. Birinchi eshitgan mos so'zni darhol yozmang.
items: 1 A false story on social media can reach millions of people in a single ___.
2 Stories that cause strong ___ are shared more often than factual reports.
3 A story is trusted most when it is passed on by a ___.
4 A genuine photo may be misleading if it was taken years earlier or in a different ___.
5 Many university students find it hard to tell the difference between news and ___.
why: "A false story on social media can reach millions of people in a single afternoon". Tuzoq: "for centuries" — o'tmish haqida.
"Stories that cause strong emotions — especially anger or surprise — are shared far more often". "Anger" va "surprise" — misollar, bo'shliqqa umumiy so'z kerak.
"The effect is even stronger when it comes from a family member". Tuzoq: "a friend" birinchi eshitiladi, lekin savolda "most" — eng kuchli ta'sir.
"It may have been taken years earlier, or in a different country".
"Many of them struggle to tell the difference between news and advertising". Tuzoq: "young people are better" — ma'ruzachi buni rad etadi.
tasks.note: 3-savol — asosiy tuzoq: "friend" va "family member" ikkalasi ham eshitiladi. Savoldagi "most" ni doiraga oling.

tasks.title: Questions 6–10 — How to check a news story
tasks.type: Complete the flow chart below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.
tasks.instr: Signal so'zlar: The first step, Next, Then, After that, The next step, And finally.
why: "Next, look at the source. Who actually published this story?"
"Then read beyond the headline". "Read more than" = "read beyond".
"After that, check the date. Old stories are often shared again as if they were new".
"Search for the same story on other websites". Ko'plik -s — "other" dan keyin.
"Do a reverse image search". Bitta so'z: "search".
rows: Stop — don't share the story immediately.
Look at the (6) — who published the story?
Check the (8) to make sure the story is not old.
Look for the same story on other (9).
For photos, do a reverse image (10).
Share the story only if it passes all the checks.

Birinchi vazifa — shadowing: Student's Book Track 16 ni (maqola yozish bosqichlari) ikki marta tinglang, keyin skriptsiz 8 bosqichni o'z so'zlaringiz bilan ayting va ovozli xabar qilib guruhga yuboring. Signal so'zlarni (first, then, remember, finally) albatta ishlating.

kahoot.q: Section 4 has no pause in the middle. When should you read all ten questions?
kahoot.explain: Section 4 da oraliq tanaffus yo'q — 10 savolning hammasini boshidagi tayyorlanish vaqtida ko'rib chiqing.

kahoot.q: 'Each member receives a ___ at the first meeting.' What kind of word fits the gap?
kahoot.explain: "a" artikli — birlikdagi sanaladigan ot belgisi.

kahoot.q: ONE WORD ONLY. Gap: 'Bring a ___ to every lecture.' You hear 'a small notebook'. What do you write?
kahoot.explain: "a" gapda bor, "small" esa ortiqcha — ONE WORD ONLY da faqat "notebook" yoziladi.

kahoot.q: ONE OR TWO WORDS. Which answer stays within the word limit?
kahoot.explain: Chiziqcha bilan yozilgan so'z (part-time) bitta so'z sanaladi; artikl ham so'z, qo'shilsa 3 so'z bo'ladi.

kahoot.q: In a flow-chart task, the speaker says 'Once that's done, ...'. What does this usually signal?
options: The talk is about to end
kahoot.explain: "Once that's done" — oldingi bosqich tugadi, keyingi qutiga o'ting.

kahoot.q: Flow chart, boxes 6–10: box 8 is still empty, but you hear 'Finally, ...'. What is the best thing to do?
options: Move on to the last box
Wait for box 8 to be repeated
Write the next word you hear in 8
kahoot.explain: Audio qaytarilmaydi: oxirgi qutiga o'ting, bo'sh qolgan 8 ga oxirida taxminiy javob yozing.

kahoot.q: Are flow-chart answers usually heard in the same order as the boxes?
options: Yes, in the order of the boxes
kahoot.explain: Flow chart jarayon tartibida tuziladi — audio ham shu tartibda boradi.

kahoot.q: Gap: 'The festival was funded by ___.' Which words in a talk are most likely to lead to the answer?
kahoot.explain: "was funded by" = "the money came from" — ma'no bir xil, so'zlar boshqa.

kahoot.q: Gap: 'Members get a free ___ every month.' You hear: 'Members get free tickets, and a free magazine every month.' What do you write?
kahoot.explain: "a free ___ every month" — birlikdagi ot va "every month": magazine; "tickets" — tuzoq.

kahoot.q: In Section 4, can a question test the speaker's opinion, not just a fact?
options: Only in the first half of the talk
kahoot.explain: Section 4 da ma'ruzachining fikri va maslahati ham savol bo'lishi mumkin ("I think...", "I'd recommend...").

kahoot.q: You hear 'Collect your certificates at the front desk.' Gap: 'Collect your ___ at the front desk.' You write 'certificate'. Is it correct?
options: Yes — the meaning is the same
No — it must start with a capital
kahoot.explain: Eshitilgan shakl ko'plikda — "-s" tushib qolsa, javob noto'g'ri.

kahoot.q: You write 'color' instead of the British spelling 'colour'. How is it marked?
options: Wrong — only British spelling is accepted
Correct, but it loses half a mark
Wrong — it is a spelling mistake
kahoot.explain: IELTS'da Britaniya va Amerika imlosi ikkalasi ham qabul qilinadi; faqat imlo xatosi 0 ball.

kahoot.q: 'News reports must be accurate.' What does 'accurate' mean?
kahoot.explain: accurate — aniq, xatosiz: hamma tafsiloti to'g'ri.

kahoot.q: 'Anyone can contribute ideas to the class blog.' Which verb is closest in meaning to 'contribute'?
kahoot.explain: contribute — hissa qo'shmoq: o'z fikri yoki g'oyasini qo'shmoq.

kahoot.q: A profitable blog is one that ...
options: makes more money than it costs
kahoot.explain: profitable — foyda keltiradigan: daromadi xarajatidan ko'p.

kahoot.q: The posts appear in chronological order. How are they arranged?
kahoot.explain: chronological — vaqt tartibida: avval eng eskisi, keyin yangilari.

kahoot.q: Complete: 'Short paragraphs help to ___ the reader's interest.'
kahoot.explain: hold someone's interest — qiziqishini ushlab turmoq: o'quvchi o'qishni to'xtatmaydi.

kahoot.q: 'Make a study plan and stick to it.' What does 'stick to it' mean?
kahoot.explain: stick to (a plan/schedule) — rejaga qat'iy amal qilmoq, uni o'zgartirmaslik.

kahoot.q: 'This guidebook is bang up to date.' What does this mean?
options: It was written a long time ago
It is full of spelling mistakes
It is too heavy to carry
kahoot.explain: bang up to date — eng so'nggi ma'lumotga ega, mutlaqo zamonaviy.

kahoot.sub: the right place at the right time
kahoot.q: 'She was in the right place at the right time.' What does this suggest?
options: She was lucky to be there
kahoot.explain: be in the right place at the right time — omad: kerakli payt kerakli joyda bo'lish.

lessons.title: Mock test 1: Unit 1–4 dan keyin — natijalar tahlili (imtihon alohida 150 daqiqalik sessiyada)
lessons.grammar_topic: Mockdan keyingi tahlil darsi: imtihonning o'zi dars sonidan tashqaridagi alohida 150 daqiqalik sessiyada (JonyOS → Imtihonlar → Mock testlar, qat'iy rejim, faqat kompyuter; Listening ~30, Reading 60, Writing 60 daqiqa); bu darsda natija savol turlari bo'yicha Unit 1–4 ga bog'lab tahlil qilinadi, Writing AI izohi 4 mezon bo'yicha ko'rib chiqiladi va ikki haftalik reja yoziladi; Speaking — alohida yuzma-yuz intervyu (11–14 daqiqa, S6_FULL bo'yicha; filial imkon bersa, boshqa kuni examiner bilan)
lessons.vocab_topic: Xom ball va band, yetti xato sababi, savol turi bo'yicha naqsh, unitga qaytish, Writing mezonlari, ikki haftalik reja
lessons.book_ref: JonyOS mock bazasi: JonyOS → Imtihonlar → Mock testlar (qat'iy rejim, faqat kompyuter). Mock — dars sonidan tashqaridagi alohida 150 daqiqalik sessiya: Listening ~30, Reading 60, Writing 60 daqiqa; Listening yozuvi bo'lmasa, skriptni examiner ovoz chiqarib o'qiydi. Examiner javoblar varaqasi har savol bo'yicha o'quvchining javobi, to'g'ri javob va mavzu belgisini ko'rsatadi; Listening va Reading bandi rasmiy xom ball — band jadvali bo'yicha avtomatik qo'yiladi. Writing'ni JonyOS AI examiner 4 IELTS mezoni bo'yicha baholaydi; examiner 48 soat ichida tekshiradi yoki o'zgartiradi, keyin natija e'lon qilinadi. Speaking mock kartochkalari A/B/C — Jony Academy original materiali (Part 1 mavzulari: Work or studies, Weather, Music, Mobile phones).
objectives: Mock sessiyasini tartib bilan o'tkazish (alohida kun, JonyOS → Imtihonlar → Mock testlar, qat'iy rejim): xona va ekran tayyorligi, qoidalar, Listening, tugatgan o'quvchi bilan ishlash.
Mock (Listening ~30 + Reading 60 + Writing 60 = 150 daqiqa) dars sonidan tashqaridagi alohida sessiya ekanini, bu 120 daqiqalik dars esa faqat natijalar tahlili ekanini bilish.
O'z natijasini o'qish: xom ball, band va qaysi bo'lim o'rtachani pastga tortgani.
Har xato javobni yetti sababdan bittasiga ajratish.
Xatolarni savol turi bo'yicha guruhlab, Unit 1–4 dagi qaysi darsga qaytish kerakligini aniqlash.
Maqsad bilan solishtirish (kamida 5.5: Listening 18+, Reading 19+ (40 dan)) va ikki haftalik aniq reja yozish.
Writing natijasini o'qish: AI examiner 4 mezon bo'yicha qo'ygan ballar, inglizcha izoh va xatolar ro'yxati; eng past mezonni topish va 5 ta xatoni tuzatish.
Speaking mock tartibini bilish va o'z bandini 4 mezon bo'yicha tushunish.
materials: Mock sessiyasi uchun: chop etilgan ism ro'yxati — kim qaysi kompyuterda o'tirgani va kim tugatgani belgilanadi.
Mock sessiyasi uchun: sessiyani o'tkazuvchi examiner ekranida Listening skripti (yozuv bo'lmasa o'qiladi) — o'quvchiga ko'rsatilmaydi.
Mock sessiyasi uchun: har stolda zaxira qog'oz va qalam — Listening paytida ism, raqam va sanalar qoralama qilinadi.

Mock sessiyasi uchun: doskada xona qoidalari (telefon sumkada, imtihon to'liq ekranda, ekrandan chiqish tizimda sanaladi) va qolgan vaqt. Tahlil darsi uchun: doskada Listening va Reading xom ball — band jadvallari (2-mashq).
Tahlil darsi: har o'quvchiga "Yetti sabab" jadvali va "Savol turi → Unit" xaritasi (quyidagi 3-mashq jadvali) chop etilgan holda.
Tahlil darsi: har o'quvchiga "Ikki haftalik reja" varaqasi — 6 qator, oxirida ustoz imzosi uchun joy.

Tahlil darsi: har o'quvchi o'z examiner javoblar varaqasini o'z ekranida (kompyuterda) yoki chop etilgan shaxsiy nusxada ko'radi. Proyektorda faqat to'g'ri javoblar va guruh statistikasi (qaysi savolda nechta xato) ko'rsatiladi — shaxsiy natijalar proyektorga chiqarilmaydi.
Tahlil darsi: har o'quvchining examiner tasdiqlagan Writing natijasi — 4 mezon bo'yicha ball, inglizcha izoh va grammatika/lug'at xatolari ro'yxati (o'z ekranida yoki chop etilgan nusxada).
Speaking intervyusi uchun (filial imkon bersa, boshqa kuni examiner bilan): Speaking kartochkalari A/B/C (faqat examinerda), bayonnoma varaqasi, telefon diktofoni, intervyu jadvali.
timeline: Kirish: bugun — tahlil darsi

Mock alohida 150 daqiqalik sessiyada o'tgan (JonyOS → Imtihonlar → Mock testlar); bugun faqat natija va tahlil. Mock — o'lchov, jazo emas. Ballar ovoz chiqarib aytilmaydi, har kim o'z varaqasi bilan ishlaydi.
Natijani ochish
Har o'quvchi Listening va Reading xom ball va bandini, Writing bandini daftariga yozadi va maqsad bilan solishtiradi (kamida 5.5: Listening 18+, Reading 19+ (40 dan)).
Xom ball — band jadvali
Doskada ikkala jadval; jadval chegarasida bitta savol yarim bandni o'zgartirishi ko'rsatiladi (2-mashq).
Yetti sabab
Har sababga bitta tanish misol (1-mashq); sabablar jadvali tarqatiladi.
Javoblar varaqasi: Listening

Har kim o'z varaqasini savol-savol o'qiydi, har xatoga sabab raqami va Section turi yoziladi. Proyektorda faqat to'g'ri javoblar va guruh statistikasi; eng ko'p xato qilingan 3–4 savol uchun ustoz skriptdan faqat tegishli bitta gapni ko'rsatadi (bu gaplarni darsdan oldin examinerdan olib tayyorlab qo'ying).
Javoblar varaqasi: Reading
Passage bo'yicha ketma-ket; har xatoga sabab raqami va savol turi yoziladi.
Savol turi → Unit xaritasi
Har tur va har sabab necha marta chiqqani sanaladi; xatolar savol turi bo'yicha guruhlanadi va Unit 1–4 dagi qaysi darsga qaytish kerakligi topiladi (3-mashq).
Ikki haftalik reja
Har kim eng katta ikki naqsh bo'yicha 6 qatorli reja yozadi; juftlik o'qib tekshiradi.
Writing feedback
AI examiner natijasi: 4 mezon bo'yicha ball, inglizcha izoh, grammatika va lug'at xatolari; eng past mezon, 5 ta tuzatish va bitta odat (4-mashq).
SPEAKING — Mock: tartib, kartochkalar va band

3' format va vaqt (S6_MOCK_PROCEDURE) → 3' 4 mezon va band jadvali (S6_FULL, S6_MOCK_BAND) → 2' intervyu jadvali e'lon qilinadi → 2' ixtiyoriy 2 o'quvchi bilan Part 1 dan 2 savol (namoyish) Intervyuning o'zi — filial imkon bersa, boshqa kuni examiner bilan (5–8-mashq).
Xulosa va vazifa

4-mashqdagi Writing odati reja varag'ining ostiga yoziladi; reja ustozga ko'rsatiladi va imzolanadi; xatolar daftari, yangi material va Writing xatboshisi uyda bajariladi. Har o'quvchi Speaking intervyu slotini daftariga yozadi.

intro: Bu — Mock 1 dan keyingi TAHLIL darsi. Imtihonning o'zi dars sonidan tashqaridagi alohida sessiyada o'tadi; bu 120 daqiqada natijalar savol-savol va savol turi bo'yicha tahlil qilinadi, Writing izohi ko'rib chiqiladi va ikki haftalik reja yoziladi. Yangi mavzu yo'q — Unit 1–4 da o'rganilgan savol turlari kombinatsiyalarining imtihon sharoitidagi natijasi tahlil qilinadi.

Mock sessiyasi (dars sonidan tashqarida, alohida kun): examiner JonyOS → Imtihonlar → Mock testlar bo'limidan guruh uchun mockni ochadi, o'quvchilar qat'iy rejimda (faqat kompyuter, to'liq ekran) ishlaydi: Listening ~30, Reading 60, Writing 60 daqiqa — jami 150 daqiqa, bitta o'tirishda. Speaking — filial imkon bersa, boshqa kuni examiner bilan: har o'quvchiga 11–14 daqiqa, 4 mezon bo'yicha; imkon bo'lmasa, bu mockda Speaking yo'q.

Sessiyada Listening yozuvi bo'lmasa, skriptni EXAMINER ovoz chiqarib o'qiydi: bir marta, bir tekis tezlikda (taxminan 150 so'z/daqiqa), rollarni ovoz bilan farqlab. Skript faqat examiner ekranida turadi.

Natija ikki raqam: XOM BALL (40 dan nechta) va BAND. Listening va Reading jadvallari bir xil emas: 26 ta to'g'ri javob Listeningda 6.5, Academic Readingda 6.0. Jadval chegarasida bitta savol yarim bandni o'zgartiradi (Listening 29 ta = 6.5, 30 ta = 7.0) — bo'sh javob qoldirmang.

Yetti sabab: 1) eshitmadim / topa olmadim; 2) eshitdim, lekin xato yozdim (imlo, ko'plik, raqam); 3) vaqt yetmadi; 4) savol turini noto'g'ri tushundim (so'z limiti, NOT GIVEN va FALSE farqi, TWO letters); 5) taxmin qildim; 6) bilardim, lekin javobni o'zgartirdim; 7) savoldagi so'zni yoki uning paraphrase'ini tanimadim (javob joyi oldimda edi, lekin sinonimni bilmadim) — davosi: paraphrase juftligini daftarga yozish va unit lug'atini takrorlash.

6.0 kursida tahlil SAVOL TURI bo'yicha olib boriladi. Har xatoning yonida savol turi yoziladi va "Savol turi → Unit" xaritasidan qaysi darsga qaytish kerakligi topiladi. Masalan, Matching headings da 3 ta xato — Unit 2 (3-dars) strategiyasi takrorlanadi va shu turdagi YANGI passage'lar ishlanadi (darsdagi Practice'larning javoblari o'quvchiga allaqachon ma'lum).
Kombinatsiya xatosini alohida belgilang: agar bir passage'da ikkinchi savol turiga vaqt yetmagan bo'lsa (3-sabab), muammo tur emas — xarita usuli va vaqt taqsimoti.

Maqsad: kamida 5.5: Listening 18+, Reading 19+ (40 dan). Maqsaddan past bo'lim — ikki haftalik rejaning birinchi qatori. Writing uchun raqamli maqsad qo'yilmaydi: Task 1 kursda 19–20-darslarda o'tiladi, shuning uchun bu mockdagi Writing bali — diagnostika (eng past mezon aniqlanadi).

WRITING natijasi: JonyOS AI examiner Writing'ni 4 IELTS mezoni bo'yicha baholaydi — Task Achievement (Task 1) / Task Response (Task 2), Coherence and Cohesion, Lexical Resource, Grammatical Range and Accuracy; Task 2 ikki barobar hisoblanadi. U inglizcha examiner izohi va grammatika/lug'at xatolari ro'yxatini beradi. Examiner 48 soat ichida bahoni tekshiradi yoki o'zgartiradi, shundan keyin natija e'lon qilinadi. Guruh ustozining vazifasi — tahlil darsida shu tasdiqlangan natija bilan ishlash. Har mezonga faqat butun ball qo'yiladi; .5 faqat o'rtacha — Writing bandida chiqadi.

Sessiya qoidasi: telefon sumkada, stolda emas. Qat'iy rejimda imtihon to'liq ekranda ishlanadi; qoidabuzarlik (boshqa varaq, oyna yoki ilovaga o'tish, to'liq ekrandan chiqish, brauzer kengaytmasi yoki ekran rasmini olishga urinish) tizimda sanaladi: 2 marta ogohlantirish beriladi, 3-chiqishda o'quvchi imtihondan chetlatiladi (chegarani examiner o'zgartirishi mumkin). Savol bo'lsa qo'l ko'tariladi.

SPEAKING (filial imkon bersa, boshqa kuni examiner bilan; imkon bo'lmasa, bu mockda Speaking yo'q): Speaking ham mockning bir qismi, lekin kompyuterda emas: har o'quvchi bilan ALOHIDA, yuzma-yuz 11–14 daqiqa (Part 1, Part 2, Part 3). Intervyu telefon diktofoniga yoziladi (moderatsiya uchun); baho S6_FULL bo'yicha 4 mezonga qo'yiladi, umumiy band S6_MOCK_BAND jadvalidan olinadi.

Asosiy yo'l — mock haftasida alohida jadval: har o'quvchiga 15 daqiqalik slot (dars oldidan yoki keyin), administrator jadvalni guruh chatiga yuboradi. Zaxira (faqat 1–3 o'quvchi: kasal yoki kelmagan) — 10, 12, 14, 16-darslarning 'Practice 1' bosqichida: sinf 15 daqiqa mustaqil vaqtli ishlaydi, ustoz bitta o'quvchini qo'shni stolda tekshiradi. Zaxira intervyuni ham imkon qadar examiner o'tkazadi; ustoz o'tkazsa, diktofon yozuvini examiner ko'rib chiqadi va bandni tasdiqlaydi.
formulas: Bo'sh reja ishlamaydi; uyda 3 daqiqa zaxira bilan ishlanadi
Writing: eng past mezon + 5 ta tuzatish
Writing bandini ko'taradigan bitta aniq odat
presentation: To'liq mock bitta darsga sig'adimi?

Yo'q. Mock — dars sonidan tashqaridagi alohida 150 daqiqalik sessiya (JonyOS → Imtihonlar → Mock testlar, qat'iy rejim, kompyuterda): Listening ~30, Reading 60, Writing 60 daqiqa. Speaking — filial imkon bersa, boshqa kuni examiner bilan (har o'quvchiga 11–14 daqiqa, 4 mezon). Bu 120 daqiqalik dars — faqat natijalar tahlili.
Mock nega kerak, darslar yetmaydimi?
Darsda har tur alohida ishlanadi; mockda hammasi aralash va vaqt bilan. Kombinatsiya ko'nikmasi faqat shu yerda o'lchanadi.
Ballim past chiqdi. Nima qilaman?

Avval sabablarni sanang. 2-sabab (imlo, raqam) eng tez tuzaladi — undan boshlang. 7-sabab (paraphrase'ni tanimadim) ham ko'p uchraydi, lekin u lug'at bilan sekin tuzaladi — uni rejaga doimiy qator qilib qo'ying.
Xatolarim har xil turlarda. Qayerdan boshlayman?
Eng ko'p xato bo'lgan ikki turdan. Xaritadan ularning darsini toping.
Listening skriptini keyin berasizmi?

To'liq skript berilmaydi — tahlil javoblar varaqasi orqali. Lekin guruhda eng ko'p xato qilingan 3–4 savol uchun ustoz skriptdan faqat tegishli bitta gapni ekranda ko'rsatadi: shunda 1-sabab (eshitmadim) bilan 7-sabab (paraphrase'ni tanimadim) ajraladi.
Vaqt yetmadi — bu qaysi sabab?
3-sabab. Davosi — xarita usuli va vaqt qoidasi (Unit 1): imtihonda har passage 20 daqiqa (javoblarni kiritish bilan); uyda mashqda 17 daqiqa — 3 daqiqa zaxira bilan.
Writingni ham tahlil qilamizmi?

Ha, bugun 20 daqiqa (4-mashq). Writing'ni JonyOS AI examiner 4 IELTS mezoni bo'yicha baholaydi (TA/TR, CC, LR, GRA; Task 2 ikki barobar), inglizcha izoh va grammatika/lug'at xatolari ro'yxatini beradi; examiner 48 soat ichida tekshiradi yoki o'zgartiradi, keyin natija e'lon qilinadi. Task 1 kursda 19–20-darslarda o'tiladi — hozirgi Task 1 bali diagnostika. Speaking ham alohida baholanadi — alohida intervyuda (filial imkon bersa, boshqa kuni examiner bilan) S6_FULL bo'yicha 4 mezonga butun band (5–8-mashq). Umumiy band — to'rt bo'lim o'rtachasi.
notes: Maktab qarori: mock imtihoni — dars sonidan tashqaridagi ALOHIDA 150 daqiqalik sessiya (JonyOS → Imtihonlar → Mock testlar, qat'iy rejim, faqat kompyuter): Listening ~30, Reading 60, Writing 60 daqiqa. Speaking — filial imkon bersa, boshqa kuni examiner bilan (har o'quvchiga 11–14 daqiqa, 4 mezon). Writing natijasi examiner tekshirgandan keyin (48 soat ichida) chiqadi, shuning uchun bu 120 daqiqalik tahlil darsini natijalar e'lon qilingandan KEYIN o'tkazing.
Natijalarni ochishdan oldin o'quvchilarga eslating: mock — o'lchov, jazo emas. Maqsad — keyingi ikki haftada qaysi darsga qaytishni bilish.
Tahlil qismida ustoz ham guruh bo'yicha umumiy naqshni yozib oladi: agar guruhning yarmi bitta turda xato qilgan bo'lsa, o'sha unit keyingi haftada sinfda qayta ko'riladi.
Bu kurs o'rtasidagi mock: natija Unit 5–8 ni boshlashdan oldin qaysi turlarni mustahkamlash kerakligini ko'rsatadi.

Sessiya kuni tartibi (dars timeline'iga kirmaydi): kompyuterlar tekshiriladi, mock JonyOS → Imtihonlar → Mock testlar bo'limidan ochiladi, ism ro'yxati va zaxira qog'oz tarqatiladi; telefon sumkaga, qat'iy rejim qoidalari ovoz chiqarib aytiladi. Listening skriptini (yozuv bo'lmasa) ikki marta o'qimang va tezlashtirmang. Reading va Writing paytida xona kuzatiladi, mazmun bo'yicha yordam berilmaydi (texnik savolga — beriladi), qolgan vaqt doskaga yozib boriladi.

Speaking intervyusi: slotlar ro'yxatini mock haftasidan oldin administratorga bering, u jadvalni guruh chatiga yuboradi; har intervyu telefon diktofoniga yoziladi. Kartochkalar A/B/C faqat examinerda — ularni almashtirib ishlating va chiqqan o'quvchidan savollarni boshqalarga aytmaslikni so'rang. Zaxira slot (10, 12, 14, 16-darslar, 'Practice 1') faqat 1–3 o'quvchi uchun. Bularning hammasi filial Speaking'ni o'tkaza olsa amal qiladi (examiner bilan, boshqa kuni).
mistakes: Har xatoga sabab va savol turi
Aniq dars, aniq miqdor, aniq kun
Noto'g'ri javob uchun jarima yo'q; bo'sh javob — kafolatlangan nol
Davosi boshqa: xarita va vaqt taqsimoti

class_ex.title: 1-mashq: Bu xato qaysi sababdan?
class_ex.instr: Ustoz xato javobni o'qiydi, o'quvchi yetti sababdan bittasini raqami bilan aytadi va "demak nima qilish kerak" deydi.

To'g'ri javob "two weeks", o'quvchi "two week" yozgan.

Savolda "the scheme was costly", matnda "the project required a large budget"; o'quvchi NOT GIVEN belgilagan (to'g'risi TRUE) va "costly bilan large budget bir xil ekanini bilmadim" deydi.

Ko'plik -s — javoblarni tekshirish vaqtida qarab chiqiladi (qog'ozda — transfer vaqti, kompyuterda — oxirgi tekshiruv daqiqalari).
Xarita usuli va vaqt (Unit 1 Reading): imtihonda har passage 20 daqiqa (javoblarni kiritish bilan); uyda mashqda 17 daqiqa — 3 daqiqa zaxira bilan.
So'z limiti: uch so'z — 0 ball.
Qarshi isbot gap bo'lmasa — NOT GIVEN.
TWO letters — ikkita harf, ikkalasi ham to'g'ri bo'lishi kerak (Unit 2).
Birinchi javobni isbotsiz o'zgartirmang.
Section 4 da tayyorlanish vaqtida savollarni oldindan o'qish (Unit 4 Listening).
costly = required a large budget. Paraphrase juftligini daftarga yozing va unit lug'atini takrorlang.

class_ex.title: 4-mashq: Writing — AI examiner izohi bo'yicha tahlil
class_ex.instr: Har o'quvchi examiner tasdiqlagan Writing natijasini ochadi: 4 mezon bo'yicha ball, inglizcha examiner izohi va grammatika/lug'at xatolari ro'yxati. Besh qadamni daftarda bajaring. Namuna (Madina) "Javobni ko'rsat" tugmasi ostida — ko'chirmang, o'z natijangiz bilan ishlang.
items: 1-qadam. Task 1 va Task 2 uchun 4 mezon bo'yicha ballaringizni yozing: Task Achievement (Task 1) / Task Response (Task 2), Coherence and Cohesion, Lexical Resource, Grammatical Range and Accuracy.
2-qadam. Eng past mezonni belgilang. Task 2 ikki barobar hisoblanishini eslang: qaysi task'dagi past ball Writing bandini ko'proq tushirgan?
3-qadam. Inglizcha izohdan eng muhim BITTA gapni toping va o'zbekchaga o'giring: examiner nimani so'rayapti?
4-qadam. Xatolar ro'yxatidan 5 ta xatoni tanlang: to'g'ri shaklini yozing va turini belgilang (grammatika yoki lug'at).
5-qadam. Eng past mezon uchun keyingi ikki haftada bajariladigan BITTA aniq odatni yozing.
answers: Madina. Task 1: TA 5, CC 6, LR 5, GRA 6. Task 2: TR 6, CC 6, LR 5, GRA 6.

Eng past ball — 5: Task 1 da TA va LR, Task 2 da LR. LR ikkala task'da past, Task 2 esa ikki barobar og'ir — shuning uchun Writing bandini eng ko'p Task 2 dagi LR 5 pastga tortgan; asosiy ish — LR. Task 1 dagi TA 5 — diagnostika (Task 1 19–20-darslarda o'tiladi).

"You rely on a narrow range of vocabulary and repeat key words such as 'problem' and 'important'." → So'z boyligingiz tor: "problem" va "important" so'zlarini qayta-qayta ishlatasiz — sinonim va paraphrase kerak (LR).

"a lot of informations" → "a lot of information" (grammatika); "make a crime" → "commit a crime" (lug'at); "The number of students have increased" → "The number of students has increased" (grammatika); "despite of the cost" → "despite the cost" (grammatika); "economical growth" → "economic growth" (lug'at).
Essay rejasida har body uchun 3 ta asosiy so'z va ularning sinonimini oldindan yozaman (problem → issue, challenge; important → significant, crucial) va har xatboshidan keyin takrorni tekshiraman.
why: Har mezonga faqat BUTUN ball qo'yiladi (masalan 5 yoki 6); .5 faqat o'rtacha — Writing bandida chiqadi.
Task 2 ikki barobar hisoblanadi: Task 2 dagi 1 ball farq Writing bandiga Task 1 dagiga qaraganda ko'proq ta'sir qiladi.
Izoh inglizcha — tushunmagan so'zni ustozdan so'rang. Izohdan bitta aniq harakat chiqishi kerak.
Tuzatilgan xato — keyingi ishda takrorlanmaydigan xato. Grammatika xatolari GRA ga, so'z tanlash, birikma va so'z yasalishi xatolari LR ga tegishli.
Odat kichik va aniq bo'lsin: "lug'atni boyitaman" emas, "har body uchun 3 ta sinonimni oldindan yozaman". Bu odat ikki haftalik reja varag'ining ostiga Writing qatori qilib yoziladi.
class_ex.note: Writing'ni JonyOS AI examiner 4 mezon bo'yicha baholaydi (Task 2 ikki barobar hisoblanadi), inglizcha izoh va xatolar ro'yxatini beradi; examiner 48 soat ichida tekshiradi yoki o'zgartiradi, natija shundan keyin e'lon qilinadi. Bu darsda faqat tasdiqlangan natija bilan ishlanadi. Task 2 5.0 kursida o'tilgan, Task 1 esa 6.0 da 19–20-darslarda o'tiladi — shuning uchun Task 1 bali DIAGNOSTIKA, asosiy e'tibor Task 2 ga. Ballni sinfda ovoz chiqarib aytmang.

Juda ravon; takror yoki o'z-o'zini tuzatish kam; fikrni izchil va mos rivojlantiradi.
Keng lug'at, ma'no nozikliklari aniq; kam uchraydigan iboralar mahorat bilan, ba'zan kichik noaniqlik.

Gapni davom ettiradi, lekin takror, sekinlashish va o'z-o'zini tuzatish ko'p; oddiy gap ravon, murakkab fikr qiyin; bir xil bog'lovchilarni ortiqcha ishlatadi.

class_ex.title: 8-mashq: SPEAKING — Mock kartochkalari A/B/C (faqat examiner)
class_ex.instr: Examiner kartochkani tasodifiy tanlaydi; savollar oldindan oshkor qilinmaydi.
items: Kartochka A / B / C — examiner tasodifiy tanlaydi
Part 1 (4–5 daqiqa): Work or studies + yana 1 ta tanish mavzu
Part 2 (3–4 daqiqa): kartochka, 1 daqiqa tayyorlanish, 1–2 daqiqa gapirish
Part 3 (4–5 daqiqa): Part 2 mavzusi bo'yicha umumiy muhokama
answers: KARTOCHKA A — Part 1. Work or studies: Do you work or are you a student? / What do you like about your studies? / What would you like to do after you finish your studies? Weather: What's the weather usually like where you live? / What kind of weather do you like best? / Does the weather ever change your mood?

KARTOCHKA A — Part 2. Describe a person who helped you when you were in a new or difficult situation. You should say: who this person is, when it happened, how they helped you, and explain why you still remember it. Follow-up: Do you still keep in touch with this person?

KARTOCHKA A — Part 3. Why is it important to help newcomers in a community? / Do people help strangers less than they did in the past? / What qualities does a good helper need? / Should helping others be taught at school?

KARTOCHKA B — Part 1. Work or studies: Do you work or are you a student? / What do you like about your studies? / What would you like to do after you finish your studies? Music: What kind of music do you like? / Do you listen to music while you study? / Did you learn to play an instrument as a child?

KARTOCHKA B — Part 2. Describe a meal that you enjoyed eating with family or friends. You should say: where you had it, who you were with, what you ate, and explain why you enjoyed it. Follow-up: Do you often eat together with your family?

KARTOCHKA B — Part 3. Why do fewer families eat together nowadays? / Is fast food a threat to traditional dishes such as plov? / Should children learn to cook at school? / How does food help to keep traditions alive?

KARTOCHKA C — Part 1. Work or studies: Do you work or are you a student? / What do you like about your studies? / What would you like to do after you finish your studies? Mobile phones: How often do you use your phone? / What do you mainly use it for? / At what age should children have their own phone?

KARTOCHKA C — Part 2. Describe something useful that you learned from the internet. You should say: what it was, how you found it, how you learned it, and explain why it was useful. Follow-up: Have you used this skill recently?

KARTOCHKA C — Part 3. Can online learning replace classroom learning? / Why do some people believe everything they read online? / How can students avoid being distracted by their phones? / Will libraries still be needed in the future?
why: Part 1 da javob 1 gap bo'lsa — 'Why?' yoki 'Can you give an example?' bilan kengaytiring; boshqa yordam bermang.
Part 2 da tayyorlanish va gapirishni taymer bilan o'lchang; 2:00 da muloyim to'xtating, keyin 1 ta follow-up savol.
Part 3 da fikrni chuqurlashtiring: 'Why do you think so?', 'Is that always true?'; mavzudan tashqariga chiqmang.
Kartochkalarni bir guruhda almashtirib ishlating (A, B, C, A ...), toki keyingi o'quvchi savollarni oldindan eshitmasin.
O'quvchi chiqqach 1–2 daqiqada S6_FULL bo'yicha 4 mezonga butun band qo'ying va S6_MOCK_BAND dan umumiy bandni jurnalga yozing.
class_ex.note: Mavzular: IELTS Speaking Part 1–3 umumiy turlari; kartochka matni — Jony Academy original materiali. Proyektorga faqat items (tartib) chiqadi.

homework_intro: Mock sessiyasida to'liq imtihonni topshirdingiz, bugun sinfda javoblar varaqasini savol-savol o'qidik va Writing izohini ko'rdik. Uyda xuddi shu ishni HAMMA xato bo'yicha oxirigacha qilasiz.

Birinchi vazifa — xatolar daftari: har xato uchun oltita ustun — savol raqami, sizning javobingiz, to'g'ri javob, savol turi, sabab raqami (1–7) va qaytiladigan dars. Oxirida har sabab va har tur necha marta chiqqanini sanang.
Ikkinchi vazifa — ikki haftalik reja: eng katta ikki naqsh bo'yicha 6 qator; har qatorda qaysi dars, qancha mashq, qaysi kun va kim tekshiradi.

Uchinchi vazifa — eng zaif savol turi bo'yicha YANGI material: Reading uchun 30-Day Reading Challenge'dagi shu turdagi hali ishlanmagan passage, Listening uchun JonyOS mock bazasidagi mos Section (raqamini ustoz beradi). Vaqt bilan ishlang, har javob yonida isbot gap bo'lsin. Darsdagi Practice'larni qayta ishlamang — ularning javoblari sizga allaqachon ma'lum.
To'rtinchi vazifa — Writing: AI izohi bo'yicha Task 2 dagi eng past mezon uchun Task 2 dan bitta body xatboshini qayta yozing; xatolar ro'yxatidan yana 5 ta xatoni tuzating.

Beshinchi vazifa — Speaking intervyusi: administrator mock haftasidagi jadvalni guruh chatiga yuboradi — o'z 15 daqiqalik slotingizga 5 daqiqa oldin keling; tayyorgarlik uchun uchta Part 2 turini (a person / a place / an event) uyda ovozli yozib yuboring.

homework.title: Xatolar daftari: sabab + savol turi + dars
homework.instr: Har xato: savol raqami — javobim — to'g'ri javob — savol turi — sabab (1–7) — qaytiladigan dars. Oxirida sanash.

lessons.title: Unit 5 Reading — Passage 2: Matching information + Matching features + Summary completion
lessons.grammar_topic: Uch savol turi bitta passage'da: Matching information + Matching features + Summary completion (Passage 2)
lessons.vocab_topic: Unit 5 (The world in our hands) — qayta tiklanadigan energiya, iqlim o'zgarishi, tabiatni asrash
lessons.book_ref: Complete IELTS Bands 5–6.5: Student's Book, Unit 5, 50–52-betlar (Reading Section 2); Workbook, Unit 5, 32–33-betlar. Practice 1–3 — Jony Academy matnlari; Speaking — Jony Academy original materiali (Part 1 mavzusi: Good view).
objectives: Passage 2 da uch savol turi kelganda ishlash tartibini tanlash: avval tartibli tur (summary), keyin ismlar (matching features), oxirida matching information.
Matching information savolidagi birinchi so'zlardan ma'lumot TURINI aniqlash (estimate, comparison, suggestion, description) va xatboshidan aynan shu turdagi gapni topish.
Matching features uchun matndagi barcha ism va tashkilotlarni 2 daqiqada doiraga olib, har birining yoniga 2–3 so'zli izoh yozish.
Tuzoqni tanish: bitta xatboshida ikki tashkilot yoki bir xil raqam (2020) tilga olinsa, fikr aynan kimniki ekanini tekshirish.
Summary sarlavhasidan kerakli xatboshini topish va javobni so'z chegarasi (NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS) hamda so'z turiga mos ko'chirish.
Speaking: The world in our hands bo'yicha IELTS Part 1–3 savollariga Band 6 darajasida javob berish (javob + sabab + misol) va 4 mezon bo'yicha sherikni baholash.
materials: Student's Book, Unit 5, 50–52-betlar ("Out of Africa: solar energy from the Sahara") — sinfda birga ishlanadi.
Workbook, Unit 5, 32–33-betlar ("Russia's boreal forests and wild grasses could combat climate change") — mustaqil mashq.
Practice 1–3 matnlari chop etilgan varaqlar (har o'quvchiga) — pastdagi Reading bo'limidan.
Rangli qalamlar: ism/tashkilotlar — doira, matching information kalit g'oyasi — to'lqinli chiziq.
Doskada uch ustun: "Summary → qaysi xatbosh?", "Ismlar → qaysi xatboshilar?", "Information → ma'lumot turi".
Part 2 kartochkasi (har juftlikka chop etilgan), taymer, S6_CLASS rubrikasi varaqasi.

intro: Passage 2 da 6.0 darajasida ko'pincha uch savol turi birga keladi. Student's Book'dagi Sahara matnida: 1–5 Matching information (qaysi xatboshida?), 6–9 Matching features (qaysi tashkilot?), 10–13 Summary completion (matndan ikki so'zgacha). Workbook'da ham aynan shu uchlik.

Muammo: uch turning ikkitasi NEVER guruhida — matching information va matching features savollari matn tartibida kelmaydi. Faqat summary odatda (USUALLY) tartibli va bitta-ikkita xatboshiga tegishli. Shuning uchun navbatni o'zgartiramiz.

TAVSIYA ETILGAN TARTIB: 1) sarlavha va kichik sarlavha — 30 soniya; 2) SUMMARY — sarlavhasi ("Concentrating Solar Power") kerakli xatboshini ko'rsatadi, uni o'qib 4 javobni yozasiz; 3) MATCHING FEATURES — matndagi barcha ism/tashkilotlarni doiraga olasiz (bu matnda ular ro'yxatda matn tartibida berilgan — ko'pincha shunday, lekin har doim emas) va gaplarni solishtirasiz; 4) MATCHING INFORMATION — endi matn tanish, eng oxirida ishlanadi.

Matching features: ro'yxatdagi variantlar ko'pincha savollardan ko'p (7 ta tashkilot — 4 ta savol). Ro'yxat ko'pincha (har doim emas) matn tartibida beriladi — 30 soniyada tekshiring; tartib mos kelsa, xarita tuzish ancha tezlashadi. Har ism yoniga 2–3 so'z yozing: "Abengoa — building 2 plants", "e-Parliament — start small".

Matching information: savolning boshidagi so'zlar ma'lumot TURINI aytadi — "estimates of" (raqam, hisob), "a comparison of" (ikki narsa solishtiriladi), "a suggestion for" (maslahat), "a mention of" (qisqa eslatma), "a short description of" (tasvir). Xatboshining asosiy g'oyasini emas, ichidagi bitta detalni qidirasiz (5.0 dagi headings bilan farqini eslang).

Uch tur bir-biriga yordam beradi: summary uchun o'qigan xatboshi, ismlar uchun chizgan xaritangiz — matching information uchun tayyor bilim. Oxirida 1–5 savollarning ko'pchiligini xotiradan joylashtirasiz, faqat tekshirish uchun qaytib o'qiysiz.
Vaqt: Passage 2 ga 20 daqiqa. Taxminan: summary — 5, matching features — 6, matching information — 7, tekshiruv — 2 daqiqa.
formulas: E ikki marta? NB ruxsat beradi
presentation: Nega 1–5 ni oxirida ishlaymiz?
Chunki ular tartibsiz va butun matnni qamraydi. Summary va ismlardan keyin matn allaqachon tanish bo'ladi.
Ro'yxatda 7 ta tashkilot, savol 4 ta. Qolganlari nima?
Ortiqcha variantlar — tuzoq. Ular matnda bor, lekin hech bir gapga mos kelmaydi.
Bitta xatboshida ikki tashkilot bor. Qanday ajrataman?
Fe'lga va egaga qarang: kim quryapti, kim qonun qabul qilgan, kim hisoblagan? Gap aynan kimga tegishli?
"NB You may use any letter more than once" nima degani?
Bitta xatbosh (masalan, E) ikki savolga javob bo'lishi mumkin. Ikki marta chiqsa, xato deb o'ylamang.
Summary'dagi so'z matndagidan boshqacha.
Normal: summary paraphrase qiladi ("situated in" = "building ... in"). Javob esa matndagi so'z, aynan o'sha shaklda.
Summary javobi uch-to'rt so'z chiqdi.
Chegarani buzmang: kerakli ot odatda bitta so'z ("depressions"), ortiqcha sifat va artikl tashlanadi.
notes: 5.0 da matching information (25-dars), matching features (26-dars) va summary (14-dars) alohida o'rganilgan. Bugungi yangilik — uchalasini bitta passage'da, to'g'ri NAVBAT bilan yechish.
Tekshiruvda har javob uchun o'quvchidan ikki narsa so'rang: "isbot gap qaysi?" va "savoldagi qaysi so'z matnda qanday aytilgan?"
Kuchli o'quvchilarga: SB matnidagi 7 tashkilotning har biri haqida bir gapli izohni xotiradan aytish; zaif o'quvchilarga — faqat ism va xatboshi harfi.

class_ex.title: Ma'lumot turini aniqlash (SB, 3-mashq)
class_ex.instr: Matnni ochmasdan, SB 1–5 savollarining kalit so'zini tagiga chizing va xatboshida qanday gap qidirish kerakligini ayting.
items: 1 a mention of systems which could not be used
2 estimates of the quantity of power the Sahara could produce
3 a suggestion for how to convince organisations about the Sahara's potential
4 a short description of the Sahara at present
5 a comparison of the costs of two different energy sources
answers: maslahat: "if it can be shown ... they will..."
Saharaning hozirgi holati: harorat, quruq, bo'sh
why: "Could not be used" — salbiy: "would not be suitable", "cannot" kabi so'zlarni qidiring.
"Estimates" — ko'plik: bir nechta hisob-kitob va raqam bo'lishi kerak.
"Suggestion" — kimdir nima qilish kerakligini aytadi; "convince" = ishontirish, isbot ko'rsatish.
"At present" — tarix yoki kelajak emas, hozirgi tasvir.
"Comparison" — qiyosiy daraja (cheaper, more expensive) va ikkita manba nomi.
class_ex.note: Uchinchi mashq savollari ("Hamma harf kerakmi?" — yo'q; "Bitta harf ikki marta?" — ha) ni ham og'zaki so'rang.

class_ex.title: Tashkilotlar xaritasi (SB, 5-mashq)
class_ex.instr: SB matnini tez ko'zdan kechiring va ro'yxatdagi har tashkilot qaysi xatboshida tilga olinganini yozing.
items: A Exploration Architecture
B DESERTEC
C ABB Power Technologies
D Aerospace Centre
E Abengoa
F The European Parliament
G e-Parliament
why: Michael Pawlyn — Exploration Architecture direktori; Sahara Forest Project haqida.
Gerry Wolff boshqaradigan konsorsium — $59 billion hisobi.
Gunnar Asplund — kabellar va narx haqida.
Germaniyaning Aerospace Centre — infratuzilmani almashtirish narxi.
Sevilyadagi kompaniya — Jazoir va Marokashda stansiya qurmoqda.
Yevropa Parlamenti — 2020 yilgacha 20% maqsadi haqidagi qonun.
Nicholas Dunlop — "Lego method".
class_ex.note: Bu matnda ro'yxat tartibi matn tartibi bilan bir xil ekanini ko'rsating: B, D, E, E, F, F, G — o'sib boradi. Imtihonda ro'yxat ko'pincha (har doim emas) shunday beriladi — 30 soniyada tekshiring; mos kelsa, bu tezlik beradi. SB 52-betdagi Exam advice "they are listed in the order they appear in the passage" deydi — bu matnda shunday, lekin har bir yangi testda tartibni o'zingiz tekshiring.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 1: Good view
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda so'rang va javob bering; har javob 2–3 gap: javob + sabab/misol (because, for example, to be honest).
items: Is there a good view from your window at home?
Do you prefer views of the city or of nature?
Where is the best view in your hometown?
Would you pay more for a hotel room with a good view?
answers: Not really, to be honest. We live on the second floor, so all I can see is the yard and the building opposite. In spring, though, the apricot trees in the yard are in bloom, which looks lovely.

Definitely views of nature. City views can be impressive at night, but mountains or a river make me feel calm. For example, whenever I visit my grandparents in the village, I spend hours just looking at the hills.
I'd say it's the top of the TV tower, because from there you can see the whole of Tashkent. I went up there last year, and on a clear day you could even see the mountains in the distance.
It depends on the price. If the difference were small, I would definitely pay more, because waking up to a sea or mountain view makes a holiday special. But I wouldn't spend a fortune on it.
why: Javob + sabab (so all I can see...) va relative clause (which looks lovely) — oddiy savolga ham kengaytirilgan javob.
Solishtirish (City views can be impressive..., but...) va aniq misol (For example, whenever I visit...) — FC va LR uchun ball.
Past simple (I went) va 'could even see' bilan aniq detal — zamonlar to'g'ri, javob shaxsiy tajribaga bog'langan.
2nd conditional (If the difference were small, I would...) va 'spend a fortune' iborasi — GRA va LR uchun murakkab tuzilma.
class_ex.note: Mavzu: IELTS Speaking Part 1 to'plami (Good view). Namuna javoblar — Jony Academy original matni.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 2: A natural place I enjoyed
class_ex.instr: 1 daqiqa tayyorlanish (qog'ozga 5–6 kalit so'z), keyin 1–2 daqiqa to'xtovsiz gapiring; sherigingiz vaqtni o'lchaydi va S6_CLASS bo'yicha band qo'yadi.
items: Describe a natural place (for example a mountain, lake or forest) that you visited and enjoyed.
You should say:
where it is
when you went there
what you did there
and explain why you liked it.
class_ex.answers: I'd like to talk about Charvak Reservoir, which is a huge lake in the mountains about eighty kilometres from Tashkent. I went there last August with my family, just after my exams had finished. We stayed in a small guest house for three days, and to be honest, it was exactly what I needed to get away from it all. In the mornings we went hiking on the hills around the lake, and in the afternoons we swam and took a boat trip. The water was surprisingly cold, but incredibly clear and blue. In the evenings we had barbecues and watched the sun go down behind the mountains. There are a few reasons why I liked it so much. First of all, the scenery is breathtaking; the turquoise water and the mountains look like a postcard. Secondly, it felt calm and peaceful compared with the noise of the city, and I hardly used my phone at all. However, I also noticed some plastic bottles on the beach, which made me realise that people should take better care of such places. If I have the chance, I would love to go back next summer, maybe with my friends this time.
why: Kartochkaning 4 bandi tartib bilan yoritilgan (qayer → qachon → nima qildi → nega yoqdi) — FC: izchil tuzilma.
Mavzu iboralari (to get away from it all, the scenery is breathtaking, look like a postcard, take better care of) — LR: 'less common' lug'at.
Past perfect (my exams had finished), relative clause (which is / which made me realise), shart gap (If I have the chance, I would love to) — GRA: turli tuzilmalar.
Diskurs belgilari (First of all, Secondly, However) va oxirgi gapda kelajak rejasi — monolog tabiiy yakunlangan; ekologiya mavzusiga ko'prik (Part 3 ga o'tish).
box: breathtaking scenery — hayratlanarli manzara
unspoilt — buzilmagan, tabiiy holicha qolgan (joy)
off the beaten track — odam kam boradigan, chekka (joy)
to get away from it all — hamma narsadan uzoqlashib dam olmoq
carbon footprint — uglerod izi (inson faoliyati chiqaradigan CO2 miqdori)
renewable energy — qayta tiklanadigan energiya
to raise awareness — xabardorlikni oshirmoq
it's high time that... — ...vaqti allaqachon keldi
class_ex.note: Cue card va namuna monolog — Jony Academy original materiali (Unit 5 mavzusi: The world in our hands). Namunadagi joy — Chorvoq suv ombori; o'quvchi o'zi borgan joyni tanlaydi (Chimyon, Zomin, Arslonbob va h.k.).

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 3: Energy and the environment
class_ex.instr: Ustoz savol beradi, 2–3 o'quvchi javob beradi: fikr → sabab → misol → qarama-qarshi fikr yoki xulosa (40–60 soniya).
items: Is renewable energy such as solar power the answer to climate change?
Who should be most responsible for protecting the environment — governments, companies or individuals?
Why do many people not change their habits even though they know about climate change?
How can young people help to protect nature?
answers: I think it is a very important part of the answer, but not the whole answer. Solar and wind power produce almost no emissions, and in sunny countries like Uzbekistan solar panels make a lot of sense. For example, several large solar plants have been built here in recent years. However, we also need to use less energy in general, because even clean energy cannot solve the problem if our consumption keeps growing.

In my opinion, governments should take the lead, because only they can pass laws that apply to everyone. For instance, they can tax pollution or support public transport. Companies come next, since big factories produce far more waste than a single person. That said, individuals still matter, as millions of small choices add up. So I would say it is a shared responsibility, but the biggest changes have to start at the top.

I'd say the main reason is that climate change feels far away. People can't see the effects in their daily lives, so it is easy to ignore them. Another reason is convenience: driving a car is simply faster and more comfortable than taking a bus. On top of that, many people think their own actions are too small to make a difference. Unless change becomes cheap and easy, most people will probably keep their old habits.

There are quite a few things young people can do. First, they can change small habits, like carrying a reusable bottle or walking instead of asking parents for a lift. Secondly, they are very active on social media, so they can raise awareness much faster than older generations. For example, some students in Tashkent organise clean-up days in parks and post the results online. In my view, it's high time that schools supported such projects more actively.
why: 'Muhim, lekin to'liq javob emas' — muvozanatli pozitsiya; present perfect passive (have been built) va However bilan qarama-qarshi fikr.
Javobgarlarni tartib bilan baholash (take the lead → come next → That said) va xulosa gapi — Band 6–7 FC: fikr aniq rivojlangan.
Sabablarni ketma-ket qo'shish (the main reason, Another reason, On top of that) va 'Unless...' bilan xulosa — murakkab grammatika.
Amaliy takliflar + aniq misol, box iboralari (raise awareness, it's high time that + past simple) ishlatilgan — LR va GRA uchun ball.
class_ex.note: Part 3 savollari jamiyat darajasida: 'I' emas, 'people / governments / young people' haqida gapiriladi; har javob 60–90 so'z.

readings.title: Practice 1: Power from the sea
readings.qtype: Matching information (1–5) + Matching features (6–9) + Summary completion (10–13)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 2 darajasi); ismlar o'quv maqsadida to'qilgan
text: A  When the world's first offshore wind farm was switched on off the coast of Denmark in 1991, it consisted of just eleven small turbines, and many engineers regarded it as an expensive experiment. Three decades later, wind farms at sea supply a significant share of the electricity used in several northern European countries, and the largest turbines now stand taller than most city office buildings. A single turn of their enormous blades can produce enough electricity to run an ordinary home for many hours.

B  The main attraction of building at sea is the wind itself. Out on the open water there are no hills, trees or buildings to slow the air down, so winds are both stronger and more constant than on land. In addition, turbines placed far from the coast are rarely seen or heard by anyone, which removes one of the most common objections to wind power. 'On land, the biggest obstacle is usually not engineering but neighbours,' says Marta Lind, an engineer who has worked on several North Sea projects. 'At sea, the difficulties are technical, and technical problems can be solved.'

C  Those difficulties are considerable. Most offshore turbines stand on foundations made of steel or concrete and fixed to the seabed, which is only practical in water less than about fifty metres deep. For deeper seas, engineers have developed floating turbines. Instead of resting on the bottom, each turbine is mounted on a large platform that is partly filled with water to keep it stable, and the platform is held in position by cables attached to heavy anchors on the seabed. The electricity then travels to the shore through cables buried beneath the sea floor.

D  Environmental groups have generally welcomed offshore wind, but not without reservations. Seabirds can be killed by the blades, and the noise of hammering foundations into the seabed may disturb whales and dolphins. Marine biologist Tomas Reyes, however, points to an unexpected benefit. 'Within a few years the foundations are covered in mussels and seaweed, and fish gather around them,' he explains. 'In effect, a wind farm can become an artificial reef.' He adds that because fishing boats usually stay out of these areas, some fish populations have a chance to recover.

E  Not everyone sees that as good news. Fishing communities complain that wind farms close traditional fishing grounds and that they are rarely consulted before a site is chosen. Peter Holm, who represents a group of small fishing businesses, says the turbines themselves are not the problem. 'We are not against clean energy,' he says. 'We simply want to be involved from the start, instead of being told about a project when all the decisions have already been made.'

F  Cost has long been the main argument against offshore wind. Building and maintaining machines in salt water and storms is far more expensive than doing so on land. Yet prices have fallen sharply over the past decade as turbines have grown larger and construction methods have improved. Government adviser Sara Novak believes the industry has reached a turning point. 'Ten years ago, electricity from offshore wind cost much more than power from gas,' she says. 'In many places today the difference has almost disappeared.'

G  The greatest remaining challenge may be what happens when the wind drops or suddenly becomes much stronger. Existing electricity networks were designed for power stations that produce a steady supply, and they cannot always absorb sudden surges from the sea. Engineers are therefore testing ways of storing surplus energy, for example by using it to produce hydrogen, which can be kept and burned later. Marta Lind is optimistic. In her view, within twenty years the question will not be whether offshore wind can meet a country's needs, but how quickly the networks can be rebuilt to carry it.

the size of the first wind farm
consisted of just eleven small turbines
keeping extra energy for later use
storing surplus energy ... which can be kept and burned later
fish gather around them ... a chance to recover

readings.title: Practice 2: Bringing back the beaver
readings.qtype: Matching information (1–5) + Matching features (6–9) + Summary completion (10–13)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 2 darajasi); ismlar o'quv maqsadida to'qilgan
text: A  Beavers were once common in rivers across Europe and northern Asia. Over the centuries, however, they were hunted in huge numbers, partly for their thick fur and partly for a strong-smelling substance they produce, which was used in medicines and perfumes. By the early twentieth century only small groups survived in a few isolated areas. Since then, protection and reintroduction programmes have been remarkably successful, and the number of beavers in Europe is now thought to be well over a million. In Britain, where the animal had disappeared several hundred years earlier, the first officially approved release into the wild did not take place until the early twenty-first century.

B  Few animals change their surroundings as dramatically as beavers do. Using their powerful teeth, they cut down young trees and use the branches, together with stones and mud, to build dams across streams. Water collects behind each dam and forms a pond. In the middle of this pond the beavers construct their home, known as a lodge. Its entrances are always underwater, which makes it very difficult for predators such as wolves to get inside.

C  For people living downstream, these dams can bring real benefits. During heavy rain, the ponds hold back large quantities of water and release it slowly over several days, reducing the risk of sudden floods. 'A series of beaver dams works rather like a sponge,' explains hydrologist Emma Clarke. 'It will not prevent every flood, but it can reduce the peak flow that reaches the towns further down the valley, and that is often where the most expensive damage happens.' Beaver ponds also trap soil and pollution, so the water that leaves them tends to be cleaner.

D  The ponds are equally valuable for wildlife. Dead trees standing in the water attract insects and woodpeckers, while the still, shallow edges are ideal for frogs, dragonflies and water birds. Ecologist James Ward has studied several sites where beavers were released. 'Within five years, the variety of species at some of them had increased dramatically,' he says. 'The ponds act as nurseries, where young fish and frogs can grow without being carried away by fast-moving water.'

E  Not everyone is pleased to see the animals return, however. Farmers complain that dams can flood valuable fields and block drainage ditches, and that beavers sometimes damage fruit trees. In some regions, landowners can now receive compensation for these losses. Farmer Tom Baxter, whose land lies beside a river where beavers have settled, accepts that they have a place in the countryside. 'My problem is the paperwork,' he says. 'When a dam floods my field, I need permission to remove it within days, not months.'

F  Managing these conflicts is now a major part of conservation work. In several countries, beavers that cause serious problems can be caught and moved to more suitable rivers, and in some places simple pipes are fitted through dams to keep water at a safe level. Other measures are even more basic: wire fences can be placed around individual trees that owners want to protect, and some landowners simply accept a small amount of damage as the price of a healthier river. Conservation officer Nadia Rossi believes that the most effective tool is knowledge. 'Many of the fears people have come from stories rather than facts,' she says. 'When landowners understand how beavers behave, they are far more willing to share the river with them.'

readings.title: Practice 3 (uyga): Gardens on the roof
readings.qtype: Matching information (1–5) + Matching features (6–9) + Summary completion (10–13)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 2 darajasi), uy vazifasi; ismlar o'quv maqsadida to'qilgan
text: A  Covering a roof with plants is not a new idea. In Scandinavia, farmhouses have been built with roofs of grass and earth for centuries, because the thick layer helped to keep homes warm through long winters. The modern green roof, however, is a much more technical product. It was developed largely in Germany in the second half of the twentieth century, and today green roofs can be seen on offices, schools, shopping centres and even bus shelters in cities around the world.

B  A modern green roof is built in layers. At the bottom is a waterproof membrane that stops water from entering the building. Above this lies a root barrier, which prevents plant roots from growing into the roof and damaging it. Next comes a drainage layer that allows extra water to run away, and on top of that a growing medium, which is much lighter than ordinary garden soil. Most roofs are planted with low-growing species such as sedum, which can survive long periods of dry weather and need very little care.

C  One of the main reasons cities are interested in green roofs is rain. In a typical city, most surfaces are hard, so rainwater runs straight into the drains, which can quickly become overloaded during a storm. A green roof acts differently: the plants and growing medium absorb a large part of the rain and release it slowly, partly through evaporation. 'We used to think of drains and roofs as completely separate problems,' says urban planner Leila Haddad. 'In fact, every roof is part of a city's water system, and it should be planned that way.'

D  Green roofs also affect temperature. Cities are usually several degrees warmer than the surrounding countryside, especially at night, because concrete and asphalt store heat. Plants cool the air around them, and the layers of a green roof protect the building below from the summer sun. Building engineer Oliver Grant points out, however, that the benefit is not spread evenly. 'The rooms directly under the roof gain the most,' he says. 'In a tall building, people on the lower floors may notice very little difference.'

E  For wildlife, a green roof can be a small island in a desert of concrete. Bees, butterflies and beetles quickly find these spaces, and some birds use them for feeding and even nesting. Ecologist Ana Sousa warns that not all green roofs are equally useful. 'A roof covered with a single type of plant looks neat, but it offers food for very few species,' she explains. 'If we want real variety, we need different plants, some deeper soil and even a few stones or pieces of dead wood.'

F  Despite these advantages, green roofs remain relatively uncommon. They cost more to install than conventional roofs, and a roof full of wet soil is heavy, so many older buildings would need to be strengthened before one could be added. Property developer Ben Carter admits that price is the main obstacle. 'Most builders know green roofs are a good idea,' he says. 'But when a client compares the first bill, the ordinary roof usually wins, even if the green one saves money over thirty years.'

G  To change this situation, a number of cities now require green roofs on certain types of new building, while others offer grants or lower taxes to owners who install them. Some also allow developers to build slightly larger buildings if they include a planted roof. Supporters hope that these measures will make green roofs as ordinary as solar panels, turning thousands of empty grey surfaces into living spaces.

items: 6 The benefits of green roofs are not equal for every part of a building.
7 A roof planted with only one type of plant has limited value for wildlife.
8 The initial cost of green roofs discourages many clients.
9 Roofs should be considered part of a city's water management.
why: Grant: "The rooms directly under the roof gain the most ... people on the lower floors may notice very little difference".
Sousa: "A roof covered with a single type of plant ... offers food for very few species".
Carter: "When a client compares the first bill, the ordinary roof usually wins".
Haddad: "Every roof is part of a city's water system, and it should be planned that way".

tasks.type: Summary completion — NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage
tasks.instr: Sarlavha — "The layers of a green roof".
why: "At the bottom is a waterproof membrane". Bo'shliqdan keyin "layer" bor — sifat kerak.
"A root barrier, which prevents plant roots from growing into the roof".
"A growing medium, which is much lighter than ordinary garden soil". "Than" dan oldin qiyosiy sifat.
"Can survive long periods of dry weather".
head: The layers of a green roof
rows: At the bottom there is a (10) layer that keeps water out of the building, and above it a barrier that stops (11) from damaging the roof.
Next comes a drainage layer, then a growing medium which is (12) than ordinary soil. Plants such as sedum are chosen because they can survive long periods of (13).
