kahoot.q: Which of these question types usually follows the order of the passage?
kahoot.explain: Summary odatda matn tartibida va bitta-ikkita xatboshiga tegishli, shuning uchun uni birinchi ishlaymiz.

kahoot.q: Why is it often best to answer the matching information questions last?
options: You know the passage well by then
They are always the easiest ones
Their answers are always in paragraph A
They are worth more marks than others
kahoot.explain: Summary va ismlar xaritasidan keyin matn tanish bo'ladi, tartibsiz detallarni topish tezlashadi.

kahoot.q: A summary has a title. How does the title help you?
options: It shows which part of the text to read
It gives you the answer to one gap
It tells you how many words to write
It lists the names you need to find
kahoot.explain: Summary sarlavhasi matnning qaysi qismi (odatda bir-ikki xatbosh) haqida ekanini ko'rsatadi — faqat o'sha qismni diqqat bilan o'qiymiz.

kahoot.q: Summary: 'The panels sit on strong ___ frames.' Text: 'The panels are placed on strong metal frames.' Answer?
kahoot.explain: 'Strong' va 'frames' gapda allaqachon bor — takrorlansa javob noto'g'ri, faqat 'metal' yoziladi.

kahoot.q: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS. Text: 'The city bought a fleet of small electric buses.' Gap: 'The city now uses ___.' Best answer?
kahoot.explain: 'Electric buses' — ikki so'z; qolgan variantlar uch-to'rt so'z va chegarani buzadi (0 ball).

kahoot.q: What do matching information questions usually ask you to find?
options: one small detail inside a paragraph
the main idea of every paragraph
the title of the whole passage
the first sentence of a paragraph
kahoot.explain: Matching information — headings emas: xatboshining asosiy g'oyasi emas, ichidagi bitta detal (raqam, maslahat, taqqoslash) qidiriladi.

kahoot.q: Information: 'a suggestion for saving energy'. Which sentence from a text matches this type?
options: 'Energy use rose by five per cent last year.'
'Most homes here use gas for heating.'
kahoot.explain: 'Suggestion' — maslahat: kimdir nima qilish kerakligini aytadi ('should').

kahoot.q: Information: 'an estimate of future costs'. Which sentence from a text matches this type?
options: 'The new bridge may cost about $2 million.'
'The old bridge cost $2 million to build in 1990.'
'The bridge is cheaper than the old tunnel.'
'The bridge should be repaired every year.'
kahoot.explain: 'Estimate' — taxminiy hisob: kelajak ('may cost') va taxminiy raqam ('about'); o'tgan fakt yoki taqqoslash emas.

kahoot.q: The instructions say 'NB You may use any letter more than once.' What does this mean?
options: One paragraph may answer two questions
Every paragraph must be used once
You may write two letters per answer
The answers follow the paragraph order
kahoot.explain: Bitta xatbosh ikki savolga javob bo'lishi mumkin — harf ikki marta chiqsa, faqat shu sababli javobni o'zgartirmang.

kahoot.q: Text: 'The council rejected the plan and was criticised by Green Action.' Statement: 'They opposed the plan.' Who?
kahoot.explain: Fe'lga va egaga qarang: rejani rad etgan ('rejected') — council; Green Action rejani emas, council'ni tanqid qilgan ('criticised').

kahoot.q: In matching features, what is true about the list of names?
options: It is often, not always, in text order
It is always in alphabetical order
It always follows the question order
It never matches the order of the passage
kahoot.explain: Ro'yxat ko'pincha matn tartibida beriladi, lekin har doim emas — 30 soniyada tekshirib, keyin xarita tuzing.

kahoot.q: Seven names are listed, but there are only four statements. What does this mean?
options: Some names will not be used
Every name is used at least once
Two names go with each statement
The extra names are not in the text
kahoot.explain: Ortiqcha variantlar tuzoq: ular matnda bor, lekin hech bir gapga mos kelmaydi.

kahoot.q: Choose the best verb: 'The government plans to ___ carbon emissions by 30% by 2035.'
kahoot.explain: 'Cut / reduce emissions' — chiqindi gazlarni kamaytirmoq; to'g'ri birikma.

kahoot.q: Which of these is a renewable source of energy?
kahoot.explain: Shamol tugamaydigan manba — qayta tiklanadigan energiya; ko'mir, gaz va neft — qazilma yoqilg'i (fossil fuels).

kahoot.q: 'One drawback of the plan is its high cost.' Here 'drawback' means ...
kahoot.explain: 'Drawback' = kamchilik, noqulay tomon (disadvantage).

kahoot.q: A government subsidy for solar panels is ...
options: money that helps pay for them
a report that criticises their use
kahoot.explain: 'Subsidy' — davlatning moliyaviy yordami: narxning bir qismini davlat to'laydi.

kahoot.q: 'At first, many engineers were sceptical about the idea.' This means they ...
kahoot.explain: 'Sceptical' — shubha bilan qaraydigan, ishonqiramaydigan: g'oya ishlashiga shubha qilishgan.

kahoot.q: 'Low-lying coastal towns are vulnerable to flooding.' 'Vulnerable to' means ...
kahoot.explain: 'Vulnerable to' — ...ga qarshi zaif, osongina zarar ko'radigan.

kahoot.q: 'The company plants trees to offset its emissions.' Here 'offset' means ...
kahoot.explain: 'Offset' (fe'l) — o'rnini qoplamoq, muvozanatlamoq: daraxtlar chiqindi gazning bir qismini qoplaydi.

kahoot.q: If damage to the environment is irreversible, it ...
kahoot.explain: 'Irreversible' — qaytarib bo'lmaydigan: avvalgi holatga qaytarib bo'lmaydi.

lessons.title: Unit 5 Listening — Section 1: Note completion + Table completion
lessons.grammar_topic: Section 1 kombinatsiyasi: Note completion + Table completion (so'z chegarasi har guruhda boshqa)
lessons.vocab_topic: Unit 5 (The world in our hands) — eko-sayohat, ko'ngillilar tashkiloti, tabiatni asrash loyihalari
lessons.book_ref: Complete IELTS Bands 5–6.5: Student's Book, Unit 5, 48–49-betlar (Listening Section 1, CD1 Track 19–20); Workbook, Unit 5, 30-bet (Listening Section 1, Track 6). Oxirgi mashq — Jony Academy skripti; Speaking — Jony Academy original materiali (Part 1 mavzusi: Fishing).
objectives: Bitta Section 1 da ikki guruhning so'z chegarasi har xil ekanini tayyorlanish vaqtida belgilash (TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER → ONE OR TWO WORDS → ONE WORD).
Qisqa yozilgan notes'dagi bo'shliqqa qanday ma'lumot kerakligini oldingi va keyingi so'zdan aniqlash (£ → raqam; "for advance payments" → ot).
Jadvalni qator bo'yicha tinglash: ustun sarlavhalari (type / accommodation / advantage) har qatorda qaysi ma'lumot kelishini aytadi.
Tuzatish va chalg'ituvchi ma'lumotni tanish: "originally ... but actually", "over 300 groups ... 150,000 members".
Raqamlarni son bilan (1,750; 130,000) va ot ko'pligini (cyclists, fences) to'g'ri yozish.
Speaking: Volunteering for nature bo'yicha IELTS Part 1–3 savollariga Band 6 darajasida javob berish (javob + sabab + misol) va 4 mezon bo'yicha sherikni baholash.
materials: Student's Book, Unit 5, 48–49-betlar — savollar sahifasi (quyida rasm), CD1 Track 19 va 20 audiosi.
Workbook, Unit 5, 30-bet — savollar sahifasi va Track 6 audiosi (imtihon rejimi, bir marta).

Recording script rasmlari — ustozda; tekshiruvdan keyin ekranga chiqariladi. Uy vazifasi uchun guruhga faqat ikkitasi yuboriladi: SB Track 20 skripti (shadowing uchun) va WB Track 6 ning 2-qismi skripti (diktant topshirilgandan keyin).

Jony Academy skripti ("Green Weekend") — ustoz o'qiydi, ikkinchi rolni kuchli o'quvchi yoki ikkinchi ustoz o'qishi mumkin. Audio yo'q: taxminan 150 so'z/daqiqa tezlikda o'qing va rollarni ovoz bilan farqlang. Rolni o'qigan o'quvchi savollarni yechmaydi — tahlilda unga skriptdan tuzoqlarni (tuzatilgan son, o'zgargan kun, uchta raqam, eski qoida) topib, sinfga tushuntirishni topshiring.
Kolonka yoki quloqchin; doskada uch ramka: "TWO WORDS + NUMBER", "ONE OR TWO WORDS", "ONE WORD".
Part 2 kartochkasi (har juftlikka chop etilgan), taymer, S6_CLASS rubrikasi varaqasi.

intro: Section 1 — kundalik suhbat (sayohat agentligi, ko'ngillilar tashkiloti, ro'yxatdan o'tish). 6.0 darajasida bu yerda ko'pincha ikki xil "completion" keladi: avval notes (qisqa yozuvlar), keyin table (jadval). Ikkalasi ham bo'shliq to'ldirish, lekin o'qish usuli boshqa.

ENG MUHIM FARQ — so'z chegarasi. Student's Book'da Q1–6: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER, Q7–10: ONE OR TWO WORDS. Workbook'da Q1–6: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER, Q7–10: ONE WORD. Har guruh ko'rsatmasini alohida o'qing va ramkaga oling — ikkinchi guruhda ko'pchilik birinchisining qoidasi bilan yozib, ball yo'qotadi.

NOTES: gaplar to'liq emas ("Will pay up to £ ___", "Needs quote for ___ during holiday"). Bo'shliq atrofidagi so'z turi aytadi: £ dan keyin — raqam; "for" dan keyin — ot; "a ___" — birlikdagi ot. Notes'da bor so'zni (£, "on plane") javobga qo'shmang.

TABLE: avval jadval sarlavhasi va ustun nomlarini o'qing (type of holiday / accommodation / advantage). Suhbat odatda QATOR bo'yicha boradi: bitta joy haqida uchala ustun, keyin keyingi joy. Qatordagi tayyor katakchalar ("watching animals", "village house") — qayerda turganingizni bildiruvchi "belgi".

TUZOQLAR: 1) tuzatish — "I originally planned three weeks, but actually two would be better" → oxirgi javob; 2) yaqin raqamlar — "over 300 groups and around 150,000 members" → jadvalda "300 ___" — demak "groups"; 3) o'xshash ma'noli ibora — audioda avval "salaried people" (boshqa loyihalar haqida), keyin "very few, if any, paid staff"; notes'dagi "do not have any" ga ikkinchisi mos, javob — "paid staff".
Transfer: raqam — son bilan va vergul bilan (1,750; 130,000); ko'plik -s (cyclists, fences); imlo (vegetarian, insurance). Nom bosh harf bilan (City Farms, Action).
formulas: Table: ustun va qator nomlarini o'qing
presentation: Notes'da "£" bor. Men ham yozamanmi?
Yo'q. Faqat raqam: 1,750. Belgi allaqachon berilgan.
"ONE OR TWO WORDS" va "ONE WORD" farqi katta-mi?
Ha. "local family" birinchisida to'g'ri, ikkinchisida xato bo'ladi. Har guruh ko'rsatmasini qayta o'qing.
Jadvalda qatorlar tartibi buzilishi mumkinmi?
Odatda yo'q: agent joylarni jadval tartibida aytadi. Lekin bitta qator ichida ustunlar aralash kelishi mumkin.
Raqam jadvalda allaqachon bor (300 ___). Nima yozaman?
Raqamdan keyingi otni: "300 groups". 150,000 — boshqa narsa (a'zolar) soni.
Gapiruvchi o'z fikrini o'zgartirdi.
Oxirgi, tasdiqlangan javobni yozing: "originally ... but actually" dan keyingisi.
Q6 bilan Q7 orasida pauza bo'ladimi?
Student's Book'da ha — ikki alohida track. Workbook'da pauza bor; shu vaqtda jadval ustunlarini o'qing.
notes: 5.0 da note completion (5-dars) va table completion (16-dars) alohida o'rganilgan. Bugun ular bitta section'da ketma-ket keladi va har birining so'z chegarasi boshqa — asosiy ko'nikma shu.
Tekshiruvda har javobdan keyin skriptdagi gapni ekranga chiqaring; tuzatish va chalg'ituvchi raqamni boshqa rang bilan belgilang.
Kuchli o'quvchilarga: Workbook audiosini skriptsiz ikkinchi marta tinglab, har tashkilot haqida bitta qo'shimcha faktni yozish (branches soni, members soni).

how: CORE — sayohat bron qilish va ko'ngillilar ishi so'zlari; STRONG — tabiatni asrash; SUPER — Section 1 suhbatidagi iboralar.
Har o'quvchi o'zi uchun eko-sayohat "buyurtmasi"ni 4 gapda aytadi: qancha muddat, qancha pul, qanday talablar.

class_ex.title: Bo'shliq turini bashorat qilish (SB, 2- va 4-mashq)
class_ex.instr: Audioni tinglashdan oldin SB Q1–10 dagi har bo'shliqqa qanday ma'lumot kerakligini ayting.
items: 1 Length of holiday: ___
2 Will pay up to £ ___
3 Told him about ___ for advance payments
4 Needs quote for ___ during holiday
5 Requires ___ on plane
6 Must check if he needs a ___
7 accommodation: house in a ___
8 type of holiday: live with a ___
9 type of holiday: working in a ___
10 advantage: holiday location without ___
answers: ot — sayohat paytidagi xizmat (sug'urta? mashina ijarasi? gid?)
ot — parvozdagi maxsus talab (ovqat? o'rindiq? yordam?)
why: "Length" — qancha vaqt: kun, hafta, oy.
£ belgisi turibdi — faqat raqam yoziladi.
"for advance payments" — oldindan to'lov uchun beriladigan narsa.
"quote" — narx taklifi; sayohat paytida kerak bo'ladigan xizmat.
"on plane" — parvozdagi maxsus talab.
"a ___" — birlikdagi ot; sayohatdan oldin tekshiriladigan narsa.
"house in a" — uy qayerda joylashgan?
"live with a" — kim bilan yashaydi?
"working in a" — qayerda ishlaydi?
"without" — ko'pincha salbiy narsa: mashinalar, turistlar, shovqin.
class_ex.note: Bashoratlarni doskada qoldiring; tinglashdan keyin qaysilari to'g'ri chiqqanini belgilang. Q7–10 chegarasi (ONE OR TWO WORDS) Q1–6 dan farq qilishini alohida ta'kidlang.

class_ex.title: "Oxirgi javob" — tuzoq mashqi
class_ex.instr: Ustoz gapni o'qiydi. O'quvchilar javobni aytadi va tuzoqni ko'rsatadi.
items: "We booked ten nights at first, but in the end we only stayed a week." — Length of stay?
"Rooms cost from 40 dollars, but I'd rather not spend more than 65 a night." — Maximum price?
"There are 12 branches and about 9,000 members in 400 teams." — Table: 400 ___
"You'll paint walls, but most of the time you'll be building bridges over streams." — Main activity: building ___
"There are no shops nearby, which some people don't like, but the best thing is that there's no traffic at all." — Advantage: a place without ___ (ONE WORD)
why: "At first ... but in the end" — tuzatishdan keyingi javob.
40 — eng past narx; savol eng ko'p to'lovni so'raydi.
400 raqamidan keyin kelgan ot — "teams". 9,000 — a'zolar soni, tuzoq.
"Most of the time" — asosiy faoliyat. "Walls" — qo'shimcha.
"Advantage" — afzallik: "the best thing" signal. Do'kon yo'qligi "some people don't like" — kamchilik, tuzoq.
class_ex.note: 5-gap SB Q10 ga tayyorgarlik: jadval ustuni (advantage) qaysi "without" kerakligini ko'rsatadi.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 1: Fishing
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda so'rang va javob bering; har javob 2–3 gap: javob + sabab/misol (because, for example, to be honest).
items: Have you ever been fishing?
Is fishing popular in your country?
Why do you think some people enjoy fishing?
Would you like to try fishing in the future?
answers: Yes, a couple of times. My uncle took me fishing on the Chirchik River when I was about twelve, and although I didn't catch anything, I really enjoyed the peaceful atmosphere early in the morning.

Actually, it's quite popular, especially among older men. On summer weekends you can see lots of people fishing by rivers and lakes outside Tashkent, and some of them spend the whole day there with their friends.
I think it's mainly because it helps them switch off. Fishing forces you to slow down and be patient, which is quite rare in our busy lives. Besides, it's a good excuse to spend a day in nature.
To be honest, I'd like to give it another try. If my uncle invites me again this summer, I'll definitely go, but this time I'm going to take my own fishing rod and hopefully catch something!
why: Present perfect savoliga "a couple of times" bilan javob, so'ng past simple hikoya va "although" bilan qarama-qarshi gap — Band 6–6.5 belgisi.
"Actually" diskurs belgisi, "especially among" aniqlashtirish va "you can see... some of them..." — umumiy fikrdan misolga o'tish.
"Switch off" (dam olmoq) — less common ibora; relative clause (which is quite rare) va "Besides" bilan ikkinchi sabab.
Shartli gap (If my uncle invites..., I'll...) va reja (I'm going to) — kelajak shakllarini farqlash GRA mezonida ball beradi.
class_ex.note: Mavzu: IELTS Speaking Part 1 to'plami (Fishing). Namunalar — Jony Academy original matni. Javob 1 gapdan iborat bo'lsa, sherik "Why?" deb so'rasin.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 2: Helping the environment or volunteering
class_ex.instr: 1 daqiqa tayyorlanish (qog'ozga 5–6 kalit so'z), keyin 1–2 daqiqa to'xtovsiz gapiring; sherigingiz vaqtni o'lchaydi va S6_CLASS bo'yicha band qo'yadi.
items: Describe a time when you helped to protect the environment or did some volunteer work.
You should say:
what you did
who you did it with
how long it took
and explain how you felt about it.
class_ex.answers: I'd like to talk about a time when I helped to clean up the bank of a small river near our mahalla in Samarkand. It happened last April, during a spring hashar, which is a traditional day when neighbours work together for free. The idea came from our mahalla committee. They had noticed that people were leaving plastic bottles and bags along the river, so they asked everyone to lend a hand. I went with my father, my younger brother and about thirty neighbours, including several of my classmates. What we did was quite simple but tiring. First, we picked up litter and filled more than forty large bags. After that, we planted around twenty young trees along the path, and some older men repaired a wooden bench. The whole thing took about five hours, from eight in the morning until lunchtime, and at the end our neighbours served plov for everyone. As for how I felt, I was exhausted but really proud. It was a rewarding experience, because I could see the result immediately. I also felt that I was giving something back to the place where I grew up. Now, whenever I walk past those trees, I feel that I've made a small difference, so it was well worth it.
why: FC: kartochkadagi 4 band tartib bilan yoritilgan, o'tishlar aniq (What we did was..., The whole thing took..., As for how I felt...) — tinglovchi adashmaydi.
LR: box iboralari o'z joyida — lend a hand, picked up litter, a rewarding experience, giving something back, made a difference, well worth it; "hashar" qisqa izoh bilan berilgan.
GRA: zamonlar xilma-xil — past simple (we planted), past perfect + past continuous (had noticed that people were leaving), present perfect (I've made).
GRA: murakkab gaplar — relative clause (which is a traditional day, the place where I grew up) va "whenever" bilan gap.
box: to give something back — (jamiyatga, yurtga) yaxshilik bilan javob qaytarmoq
to lend a hand — yordam qo'lini cho'zmoq, ko'maklashmoq
a worthwhile cause — arziydigan, foydali maqsad (xayrli ish)
to make a difference — sezilarli o'zgarish yasamoq, foyda keltirmoq
to pick up litter — axlat (chiqindi) terib olmoq
eco-friendly — tabiatga zarar bermaydigan, ekologik toza
a rewarding experience — qoniqish beradigan, foydali tajriba
it was well worth it — bunga to'liq arzirdi
class_ex.note: Namuna — Jony Academy original monologi (212 so'z, Band 6–6.5; g'oya: mahalla hasharida daryo bo'yini tozalash va daraxt ekish). Avval o'quvchilar gapiradi, namuna faqat 3' bosqichda o'qiladi.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 3: Volunteering and eco-tourism
class_ex.instr: Ustoz savol beradi, 2–3 o'quvchi javob beradi. Har javob: fikr → sabab → misol → qarama-qarshi fikr yoki xulosa.
items: Why do some people do volunteer work without being paid?
Is eco-tourism good for local communities?
Should schools make community service compulsory?
answers: I think the main reason is that helping others gives people a sense of purpose. For example, many students volunteer at charity events or help elderly neighbours because it makes them feel useful. Another reason is practical: volunteering is a good way to gain experience and improve your CV. On the other hand, some people simply want to give something back to their community, which is a kind of motivation that money can't buy.

In most cases, yes, because it brings money directly to local families. For instance, in mountain villages near Zaamin, tourists stay in guest houses, buy homemade food and hire local guides. It also encourages people to protect nature, since a clean environment is exactly what attracts visitors. However, if too many tourists come, eco-tourism can damage the very places it is supposed to protect, so the number of visitors needs to be controlled.

Personally, I think a small amount of compulsory service is a good idea. Many teenagers would never try volunteering on their own, but once they do, they often discover that it's a rewarding experience. It also teaches responsibility and teamwork. That said, if it becomes just another duty with lots of paperwork, students might lose interest. So the best solution would be to let students choose their own project, for example tree planting or tutoring younger children.
why: Fikr (the main reason is) → misol (For example) → ikkinchi sabab (Another reason is practical) → boshqa nuqtai nazar (On the other hand) — to'liq Part 3 tuzilmasi.
Ikki tomonni ko'rish: foyda (brings money, encourages people to protect nature) va xavf (However, if too many tourists come...) — "the very places" kabi ta'kidlovchi ibora LR ga ball beradi.
"Personally" → sabab → "That said" bilan cheklov → murosali yechim (the best solution would be to...) — Band 7 ga yaqin strategiya.
class_ex.note: Part 3 da "I" emas, "people / teenagers / local communities" haqida gapiriladi. Javob 2 gapdan qisqa bo'lsa: "Why do you think so?" deb chuqurlashtiring.

tasks.title: Questions 1–6 — Notes
tasks.type: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER
tasks.instr: Notes tartibi = suhbat tartibi. £ va "on plane" kabi berilgan so'zlarni takrorlamang.
why: "I originally planned to go for three weeks, but I think actually two would be better". Tuzoq: "a week, a month" (agent savoli) va "three weeks".

"I may need to see if you'll need a visa for some of the places". Millat (Russian) — bu savol uchun sabab, javob emas.

listenings.title: Jony Academy: Green Weekend — volunteer registration (Q1–10)
intro: Dilnoza shahar "Green Weekend" tadbiriga guruhini ro'yxatdan o'tkazish uchun qo'ng'iroq qiladi.
Chegaralar: Q1–5 — NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER; Q6–10 — ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER. Tinglashdan oldin 40 soniya savollarni o'qing.
transcript: [Ustoz uchun] Ustoz skriptni BIR MARTA, tabiiy tezlikda o'qiydi (ikki rol: ORGANISER va DILNOZA).
ORGANISER: Good morning, Green Weekend office. How can I help you?
DILNOZA: Hello. I'd like to register a group of volunteers for this weekend, please.
ORGANISER: Of course. Can I have your name?
DILNOZA: Yes, it's Dilnoza Karimova. That's K-A-R-I-M-O-V-A.
ORGANISER: K-A-R-I-M-O-V-A. Thank you. And how many people are in your group?
DILNOZA: Well, there were eight of us, but two of my friends have exams on Saturday, so it'll be six.

ORGANISER: Six, fine. Now, everyone meets on Saturday morning. Usually we meet at the main entrance of the park, but it's being repaired at the moment, so this time we're meeting in the car park next to the sports centre.
DILNOZA: Next to the sports centre. OK. Do we need to bring anything? Gloves?
ORGANISER: No, we provide gloves and rubbish bags for everyone. But please bring strong boots, because the river bank can be very muddy. And a water bottle, of course.
DILNOZA: Boots and a water bottle. And when do I need to confirm the names?
ORGANISER: Registration closes on Thursday. I know the website says Friday, but that's a mistake — we need the list a day earlier to order the equipment.
DILNOZA: Thursday, then. Could you tell me what activities there are?

ORGANISER: Sure. There are four. The biggest one is the river clean-up on the north bank. People expect to find leaves and branches, but most of what we pull out of the water is plastic — bottles, bags, that sort of thing.
DILNOZA: That's sad. What else?

ORGANISER: Then there's tree planting. That happens on the grass near the bridge — not the old footbridge, the new road bridge. Last year we planted two hundred trees, and our long-term aim is five hundred, but this weekend we've got 150 young trees ready.
DILNOZA: 150. My younger brother might like that. Is there anything for children?
ORGANISER: Yes, the bird box workshop in the community centre. It used to be for children over six, but the tools are quite sharp, so now it's only for children over eight.
DILNOZA: He's nine, so that's perfect. And the fourth activity?

ORGANISER: The litter survey in the town centre. Volunteers count and record the rubbish they find in each street, and all the results go to the local council, so they can decide where to put new bins.
DILNOZA: The council. Great. I think my group will choose the river.
ORGANISER: Wonderful. I'll email you a map this afternoon.

tasks.title: Questions 1–5 — Registration notes
tasks.type: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER
tasks.instr: Harflangan ism, tuzatilgan raqam va o'zgartirilgan joy/kunlarga e'tibor bering.

"There were eight of us, but ... it'll be six". Tuzoq: 8.
"This time we're meeting in the car park next to the sports centre". Tuzoq: "main entrance of the park" — ta'mirda.
"Please bring strong boots". Tuzoq: "gloves" — tashkilotchilar beradi. "Water bottle" notes'da bor.
"Registration closes on Thursday. I know the website says Friday, but that's a mistake".
head: Green Weekend — volunteer registration

tasks.title: Questions 6–10 — Activities
tasks.type: ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER
tasks.instr: Jadval qator bo'yicha eshitiladi. Har qatorda ikki-uch raqam yoki joy aytiladi — savolga mosini tanlang.
why: "Most of what we pull out of the water is plastic". Tuzoq: "leaves and branches" — odamlar kutadigan narsa.
"On the grass near the bridge — not the old footbridge, the new road bridge". ONE WORD — "bridge" ("road bridge" ikki so'z).
"This weekend we've got 150 young trees ready". Tuzoq: 200 (o'tgan yil) va 500 (uzoq maqsad).
"Now it's only for children over eight". Tuzoq: "used to be for children over six"; 9 — ukasining yoshi.
"All the results go to the local council". "Local" jadvalda bor.

kahoot.q: In a Section 1 test, Questions 1–6 say 'NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER' and Questions 7–10 say 'ONE WORD ONLY'. What should you do?
options: Use the first limit for all
kahoot.explain: Har guruhning ko'rsatmasi alohida: ikkinchi guruhda birinchisining qoidasi bilan yozilsa, ball yo'qoladi.

kahoot.q: ONE WORD ONLY. Notes: 'Bring a waterproof ___'. You hear: 'Please bring a waterproof jacket.' What do you write?
kahoot.explain: "Waterproof" notes'da bor — faqat yetishmayotgan so'z yoziladi; ikki so'z ONE WORD chegarasidan oshadi.

kahoot.q: Notes: 'Deposit: £ ___'. You hear: 'a deposit of two hundred and forty pounds'. What do you write?
kahoot.explain: "Two hundred and forty" = 240; £ belgisi notes'da bor, shuning uchun faqat raqam yoziladi.

kahoot.q: You hear: 'fourteen thousand five hundred volunteers'. Which number do you write?
kahoot.explain: Fourteen thousand = 14,000, five hundred = 500; jami 14,500 — minglik vergul bilan yoziladi.

kahoot.q: 'We first planned the trip for Monday, but actually Wednesday suits us better.' Which day do you write?
kahoot.explain: "First ... but actually" — tuzatish signali; oxirgi, tasdiqlangan javob yoziladi.

kahoot.q: Table cell: '60 ___'. You hear: 'We have about 60 guides and 2,000 visitors a week.' What do you write?
kahoot.explain: 60 raqami jadvalda bor — undan keyin kelgan ot yoziladi; 2,000 boshqa narsaning (tashrifchilar) soni.

kahoot.q: In a Section 1 table completion task, how does the conversation usually move?
options: Row by row, in question order
Column by column, right to left
In a random order each time
From the last row to the first
kahoot.explain: Suhbat savollar tartibida boradi: gapiruvchi odatda bitta joy (qator) haqida hammasini aytadi, keyin keyingi qatorga o'tadi.

kahoot.q: Why should you read the cells that are already filled in (e.g. 'campsite') before you listen?
options: They help you follow the recording
They are the answers you must copy
They show the spelling of answers
They tell you each row's word limit
kahoot.explain: Tayyor kataklar "belgi" vazifasini bajaradi: ularni eshitsangiz, qaysi qatorda turganingizni bilasiz.

kahoot.q: ONE OR TWO WORDS. Table: 'volunteers build ___ for birds'. You hear: 'we build nest boxes for birds'. What do you write?
kahoot.explain: Audioda ko'plik (boxes) — -s tushib qolsa, javob xato; "for birds" jadvalda bor, takrorlanmaydi.

kahoot.q: 'Visitors expect the main problem to be noise, but in fact it's light from the hotels.' Main problem: ___
kahoot.explain: "Expect ... but in fact" — kutilgan narsa tuzoq, haqiqiy javob "in fact" dan keyin keladi.

kahoot.q: Notes: 'Free guided walk for ___ and their dogs'. What kind of word is most likely needed?
kahoot.explain: "For ___ and their dogs" — kimlar uchun? "Their" odamlarni ko'rsatadi, demak ko'plikdagi ot kerak (owners, families); yurish bepul — narx emas.

kahoot.q: The notes say 'costs nothing'. Which phrase in the recording means the same?
kahoot.explain: "Costs nothing" = "free"; arzon yoki yarim narx bo'lsa ham, baribir pul to'lanadi.

kahoot.q: Travel agent: 'I'll give you a quote for the car hire.' What is a 'quote' here?
options: the price they will charge you
a famous line from a book
a receipt for money you have paid
a list of rules for drivers
kahoot.explain: Quote — narx taklifi (smeta): kompaniya xizmat qancha turishini oldindan aytib beradi.

kahoot.q: Which phrase is closest in meaning to 'accommodation'?
kahoot.explain: Accommodation — turar joy: mehmonxona, hostel yoki oila uyi.

kahoot.q: Someone who works in 'wildlife conservation'…
options: hunts wild animals for their meat
catches wild animals to sell to zoos
kahoot.explain: Conservation — tabiatni muhofaza qilish: hayvonlarni va ular yashaydigan joyni asrash.

kahoot.q: A 'sustainable' holiday is one that…
options: does little harm to the environment
costs less than any other trip
lasts for a very long time
is only possible for very rich people
kahoot.explain: Sustainable — barqaror: tabiatga va mahalliy aholiga zarar yetkazmaydigan.

kahoot.q: An 'unspoilt' island is…
options: still natural and not built on
full of hotels, shops and tourists
kahoot.explain: Unspoilt — buzilmagan: tabiati asl holida, qurilish va turizm uni hali o'zgartirmagan.

kahoot.q: 'They booked the trip at short notice.' This means they booked it…
options: only a short time before leaving
several months before the departure date
kahoot.explain: At short notice — qisqa muddatda: jo'nashga oz vaqt qolganda.

kahoot.q: 'Bear in mind that the island has no shops.' Which verb is closest in meaning?
kahoot.explain: Bear in mind — yodda tutmoq, hisobga olmoq (= remember).

kahoot.q: If an activity is 'right up your street', it is…
options: exactly the kind of thing you like
on the road right outside your house
too difficult for you to try
kahoot.explain: Right up your street — aynan sizbop, didingizga mos (so'zma-so'z "ko'cha" ma'nosida emas).

intro: Bu darsda bitta Passage 1 da UCH savol turi keladi: chizma (diagram labelling), TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN va flow chart. Uch tur — uch xil o'qish usuli, shuning uchun boshlashdan oldin 1–2 daqiqa xarita tuzish shart.

Chizma va flow chart — "mahalliy" savollar: ular matnning bitta yoki ikki-uch xatboshisiga tegishli. Sarlavhani o'qing: "Layout of typical supermarket" — do'kon ichidagi joylar tasvirlangan xatboshilar; "In-store bread production process" — faqat non haqidagi bitta xatbosh. Butun matnni qayta o'qish shart emas.
T/F/NG — "tarqoq" savollar: ular butun matn bo'ylab tartib bilan keladi. Har savoldan kalit so'zni belgilang (ism, noyob so'z: greeters, bakeries, right-handed, decoy) va matndan skanerlab toping.

Chizmada javoblar matn tartibida KELMASLIGI mumkin — chizmadagi joylashuv bo'yicha raqamlanadi. Berilgan yorliqlar (pharmacy, milk, WAY IN) sizga yo'l ko'rsatadi: ular matnda qayerda tilga olingan bo'lsa, yonidagi bo'shliq javobi ham o'sha yerda.

Flow chart esa jarayon — bosqichlar deyarli har doim matn tartibida boradi. Strelkalar "keyin nima bo'ldi?" degan savolga javob beradi. Bo'shliq atrofidagi so'zlardan so'z turini aniqlang: "is sent ___ and other items" — ko'plikdagi ot.
So'z chegarasi har guruhda boshqacha bo'lishi mumkin: SB da chizma — NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS, flow chart — NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS. Har guruh ko'rsatmasini alohida o'qing va chegarani doiraga oling.
Tavsiya etilgan tartib: 1) uchala ko'rsatma va sarlavhalar (1–2 daqiqa); 2) chizma; 3) T/F/NG; 4) flow chart. Qiyin savolda 2 daqiqadan ortiq to'xtamang — belgilab, keyingisiga o'ting.
formulas: Layout of typical supermarket; milk, pharmacy
presentation: Qaysi guruhdan boshlayman?
Odatda raqam tartibida. Lekin chizma va flow chart'ning qaysi xatboshiga tegishli ekanini boshidayoq belgilab qo'ying — T/F/NG ni o'qiyotganda o'sha joylarga ham ko'zingiz tushadi.
Chizmadagi javoblar ham tartibdami?
Har doim emas. Chizma joylashuv bo'yicha raqamlanadi. Berilgan yorliqlarni matndan topib, atrofini o'qing.
Flow chart'dagi javoblar-chi?
Deyarli har doim tartibda — jarayon matnda qanday tasvirlangan bo'lsa, shunday.
Savoldagi solishtirish matnda yo'q bo'lsa?
"Wider range than...", "easier to persuade than..." — agar matn bu ikki narsani solishtirmasa, javob NOT GIVEN.
"is said to cut shoplifting" va "increase sales" — bir xilmi?
Yo'q. O'g'irlikni kamaytirish va savdoni oshirish — boshqa-boshqa da'vo. Savdo haqida gap yo'q — NOT GIVEN.
Javobni o'z so'zim bilan yozsam bo'ladimi?
Yo'q. Chizma va flow chart'ga faqat matndagi so'z, aynan o'sha shaklda yoziladi.
notes: Bu darsning yangiligi — bitta passage'da UCH tur. 5.0 da chizma (7-dars) va flow chart (4-dars) alohida o'rganilgan; endi ularni T/F/NG bilan bitta 20 daqiqada birga yechamiz.
Har javobdan keyin ikki savol bering: "isbot qaysi gapda?" va "savoldagi qaysi so'z matnda qanday aytilgan?"
Kuchli o'quvchilarga: SB matnini o'qimasdan, faqat uch sarlavha va yorliqlarga qarab, qaysi savol qaysi xatboshida ekanini 2 daqiqada taxmin qilish, keyin tekshirish.

Eslatma: 30-Day Reading Challenge'dagi Day 7 va Day 10 — aynan shu darsdagi SB va WB matnlari. Ularni uyga bermang, boshqa "Day" lardan foydalaning. Day 1 (L07) va Day 25 (L01) ham oldin ishlatilgan — kitobdagi qolgan flow chart topshiriqlari faqat shu kunlarda. Shuning uchun uyga yangi passage — Day 28 (T/F/NG + qisqa javob) beriladi, chizma va flow chart esa Practice 3 da mashq qilinadi.

class_ex.title: Do'kon so'zlari (SB, 1-mashq asosida)
class_ex.instr: Har so'zni ta'rif bilan moslang. Keyin har so'z bilan bitta gap ayting.
items: 1 aisle
2 bargain
3 own-label product
4 promotion
5 retailer
6 purchase
why: Aisle — javonlar orasidagi uzun, tor yo'lak.
Bargain — haqiqiy qiymatidan arzonroq sotilayotgan narsa.
Own-label — ishlab chiqaruvchi emas, do'konning o'z nomi yozilgan mahsulot.
Promotion — mahsulotni reklama qilish uchun tadbir yoki aksiya.
Retailer — xalqqa mol sotadigan odam, do'kon yoki kompaniya.
Purchase — siz sotib olgan narsa (ot) yoki sotib olish (fe'l).
box: A a product with the shop's name on it
B a person or company that sells goods to the public
C a long, narrow space between shelves
D something that you buy
E something sold for less than its real value
F activities to advertise something
class_ex.note: SB matnida bu so'zlarning hammasi uchraydi — o'qishdan oldin mashq qilish skanerlashni tezlashtiradi.

class_ex.title: Bo'shliq turini oldindan aytish (SB, Q1–4 va Q11–13)
class_ex.instr: Javob bermasdan, har bo'shliqqa qanday so'z kerakligini va qaysi xatboshidan qidirishni ayting.
items: 1 — "'decompression zone' for ___, not sales"
2 — "'chill zone' for ___, such as magazines, books, DVDs"
3 — "counters selling ___ situated opposite entrance"
4 — "___ often placed in central areas of aisles"
11 — "The supermarket is sent ___ and other items"
12 — "Shoppers' ___ are stimulated"
13 — "bread and ___"
why: "not sales" bilan qarshilantirilgan — savdodan boshqa maqsad; 1-xatbosh (kirish joyi).
"such as magazines, books" — ular misol, bo'shliq esa umumiy nom; 2-xatbosh.
"selling" dan keyin mahsulot; "opposite entrance" — kirishdan to'g'ri yurganda birinchi keladigan bo'lim, 2-xatbosh (chill zone bilan bir xatboshida).
"often placed" — ko'plik; "aisles" so'zi 3-xatboshda.
"and other items" — ko'plik ot; non haqidagi xatbosh (flow chart sarlavhasi).
"are stimulated" — ko'plikdagi fe'l, demak ot ham ko'plikda.
"bread and ___" — nondan boshqa oziq-ovqat turi.
class_ex.note: Doskada har javob yoniga xatboshi raqamini yozing — bu "xarita" bo'ladi.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 1: Coins
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda so'rang va javob bering; har javob 2–3 gap: javob + sabab/misol (because, for example, to be honest).
items: Do you often use coins?
Did you collect coins when you were a child?
Do you think coins will disappear in the future?
What do you usually do with small change?
answers: Not very often, to be honest. Most shops in my town accept cards or QR payments now, so I only use coins when I buy bread at the little shop near our house or pay a driver in cash.

Yes, I did, for a couple of years. My grandfather had kept some old Soviet coins, and he gave them to me when I was about eight. Since then I've added a few foreign ones that relatives brought back from their trips.

I think they probably will, at least in big cities. More and more people pay with their phones, so coins are becoming less useful. However, older people in villages still rely on cash, so it might take a few decades.

Well, I usually drop it into a jar on my desk. When the jar is full, I either give the coins to my little sister or put them in a charity box, because carrying a pocket full of change is really annoying.
why: 'Not very often, to be honest' — tabiiy boshlanish; 'accept cards or QR payments' mavzu lug'ati va 'so' bilan sabab-natija.
Past perfect (had kept) va present perfect (I've added) bir javobda; 'that relatives brought back' — relative clause.
Taxmin darajasi aniq (probably, might); 'rely on cash' kollokatsiyasi va 'However' bilan qarama-qarshi fikr.
'drop it into a jar', 'a pocket full of change' — kam uchraydigan, lekin tabiiy iboralar; either ... or va because bilan murakkab gap.
class_ex.note: Mavzu: IELTS Speaking Part 1 to'plami (Coins) — faqat savollar olindi; namuna javoblar Jony Academy original.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 2: Something expensive
class_ex.instr: 1 daqiqa tayyorlanish (qog'ozga 5–6 kalit so'z), keyin 1–2 daqiqa to'xtovsiz gapiring; sherigingiz vaqtni o'lchaydi va S6_CLASS bo'yicha band qo'yadi.
items: Describe something expensive that you bought or would like to buy.
You should say:
what it is
where you bought it (or would buy it)
how much it cost
and explain why you wanted it.
class_ex.answers: I'd like to talk about the most expensive thing I have ever bought myself, which is a laptop. I'd been saving up for it for almost a year, putting aside the money I earned by helping my uncle in his shop during the summer holidays. I bought it last March at a large electronics market in Tashkent. Before that, I shopped around for about two weeks, comparing prices online and in several stores, because I didn't want to make an impulse buy and regret it later. In the end, I found a brand-new model that was on sale, so it cost about six million soums instead of seven. It was still a lot of money for a student, but I think it was a real bargain. As for why I wanted it, the main reason was my studies. I'm preparing for IELTS, and I wanted to practise the computer-delivered test at home. Also, our old family computer was so slow that it took ages to open a single website. Looking back, I'm really glad I didn't splash out on a new phone instead. The laptop has turned out to be excellent value for money, and I use it every single day, so it was definitely worth every penny.
why: FC: kartochka tartibi saqlangan — nima → qayerda → qancha → nega; 'Before that', 'In the end', 'As for why...', 'Looking back' bandlarni bog'laydi.

LR: box'dagi 8 iboraning hammasi tabiiy ishlatilgan (saving up for, shopped around, an impulse buy, brand-new, a bargain, splash out on, value for money, worth every penny) — Band 6+ uchun 'less common' lug'at.
GRA: zamonlar xilma-xil — past perfect continuous (I'd been saving up), past simple, present perfect (has turned out), relative clause (which is / that was), so ... that tuzilmasi.
Hajmi ~210 so'z = 1:50–2:00 gapirish; narx taxminiy va so'mda, brend nomi yo'q. Band 7 uchun yanada aniq tafsilot va idioma kerak bo'lardi.
box: to splash out on — (biror narsaga) ko'p pul sarflamoq, isrof qilmoq
a bargain — arzon va foydali xarid
value for money — narxiga arzigulik, sifat-narx mosligi
an impulse buy — o'ylamasdan, bir zumda qilingan xarid
to save up for — (biror narsa uchun) pul yig'moq
to shop around — narxlarni solishtirib, bir necha do'kon aylanmoq
brand-new — yangi, hali ishlatilmagan
it was worth every penny — har bir tiyiniga arzidi

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 3: Shopping and consumer behaviour
class_ex.instr: Ustoz savol beradi, 2–3 o'quvchi javob beradi: fikr → sabab → misol → qarama-qarshi fikr yoki xulosa (40–60 soniya).
items: How do shops encourage people to spend more money?
Is online shopping better than shopping in real shops?
Why do young people often buy things they don't really need?
Do advertisements really influence what people buy?
answers: Shops use quite a few clever techniques. For instance, supermarkets usually put essential items like bread and milk at the back, so customers have to walk past many other products to reach them. They also place sweets near the checkout, where children can easily see them. Special offers such as 'buy two, get one free' are another trick, because people feel they are saving money when, in fact, they are spending more than they planned.

It depends on what you are buying. Online shopping is clearly more convenient: you can compare prices in minutes and have things delivered to your door, which saves a lot of time. On the other hand, when you buy clothes or shoes, it is hard to judge the size and quality from a photo, and returning items can be a real nuisance. So I would say online shopping is better for electronics or books, while real shops are still better for clothes.

I think social media is the main reason. Teenagers constantly see bloggers showing off new clothes and gadgets, so they feel under pressure to keep up with their friends. Another factor is that many young people have little experience of managing money, so they find it hard to resist a special offer. For example, a friend of mine bought three phone cases in one month simply because they were cheap. Hopefully, this changes as people get older.

Yes, I believe they do, although most people would deny it. Adverts rarely tell us to buy something directly; instead, they connect a product with a feeling, such as happiness or success. If we see the same advert again and again, the product stays in our memory, and we often choose it without thinking. That said, young people today are more sceptical than their parents, because they know that many online reviews and posts are paid for.
why: Fikr → 2 aniq misol (do'kon joylashuvi, kassa yonidagi shirinlik) → xulosa; 'when, in fact,' — fikrni chuqurlashtiradi.
'It depends on...' — ikki tomonlama savolga eng xavfsiz boshlanish; On the other hand bilan qarama-qarshi fikr va aniq xulosa (while bilan solishtirish).
Sabab (social media) → ikkinchi omil (Another factor is that...) → shaxsiy misol → umid bilan xulosa; 'keep up with', 'resist a special offer' kollokatsiyalari.
'although most people would deny it' — munozarali boshlanish; first conditional (If we see...) va 'That said' bilan cheklov — Band 6.5 belgisi.
class_ex.note: Part 3 da shaxsiy tajriba emas, jamiyat darajasida (people, shops, young people) gapiriladi; har javob 40–60 soniya.

keep walking ahead, and the first thing they come to

tasks.title: Questions 1–4 — Layout of typical supermarket
tasks.type: Label the diagram. Choose NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage for each answer.
tasks.instr: Berilgan yorliqlar (WAY IN, milk, pharmacy) matnning 1–3-xatboshilarida. Har yorliqdagi kalit so'zni matndan toping: decompression zone, chill zone, "situated opposite entrance" (= "keep walking ahead"), aisles.
why: "Supermarkets do not expect to sell much here, so it tends to be used more for promotion". "Not sales" = "do not expect to sell much".
"This is intended to tempt unplanned purchases and slow customers down". "Magazines, books and DVDs" — misollar.

"People who just want to do their shopping quickly will keep walking ahead, and the first thing they come to is the fresh fruit and vegetables section". "Situated opposite entrance" = "keep walking ahead ... the first thing they come to". "fresh fruit and vegetables" — to'rt so'z, 0 ball; "fresh" siz — uch so'z. "Prepared food" — tuzoq: bu peshtaxtalar meva-sabzavot yo'lagining OXIRIDA ("Having walked to the end of the fruit-and-vegetable aisle"), kirish qarshisida emas.
"Placing popular items halfway along a section so that people have to walk all along the aisle". "Central areas" = "halfway along".
tasks.note: 3-savolda ko'p o'quvchi "prepared food" yozadi, chunki yorliqda "counters" so'zi bor va matnda "counters of prepared food" iborasi uchraydi. Yorliqning oxirini o'qitib, joyni tekshiring: "situated opposite entrance" — kirishdan to'g'ri yurganda birinchi keladigan bo'lim, ya'ni meva-sabzavot. Javob: fruit and vegetables (uch so'z; "fresh" qo'shilsa — to'rt so'z, 0 ball).
head: Place on the diagram
Label
rows: Immediately to the left of the entrance
'chill zone' for (2), such as magazines, books, DVDs
(4) often placed in central areas of aisles

tasks.title: Questions 5–10
tasks.type: TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN
tasks.instr: TRUE — matn xuddi shu ma'noni aytadi; FALSE — matn qarshisini aytadi; NOT GIVEN — matnda bu haqida ma'lumot yo'q. Kalit so'zlar: greeters, fruit and vegetables, in-store bakeries, right-handed, price, decoy.
items: The 'greeters' at Walmart increase sales.
People feel better about their shopping if they buy fruit and vegetables before they buy other food.
In-store bakeries produce a wider range of products than central bakeries.
Supermarkets find right-handed people easier to persuade than left-handed people.
The most frequent reason for leaving shops without buying something is price.
'Decoy' items are products which the store expects customers to choose.
why: "A friendly welcome is said to cut shoplifting". O'g'irlik haqida gap bor, savdo oshishi haqida — yo'q.
"Selecting these items makes people feel good, so they feel less guilty about reaching for less healthy food later on".
Matnda faqat "central bakeries ... are much more efficient" deyilgan. Mahsulot turlari soni solishtirilmaydi.
"Most people are right-handed and most people's eyes drift rightwards". Chap qo'llilar bilan solishtirish yoki "ko'ndirish osonroq" degan gap yo'q.

readings.title: Practice 1: Why shopping centres look the way they do
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn va chizma (Passage 1 darajasi)
text: Most people visit a shopping centre with a short list of things to buy, yet many leave with bags full of items they never planned to purchase. This is rarely an accident. The layout of a modern shopping centre is carefully planned by architects and retail consultants, and almost every feature is intended to keep visitors walking, looking and spending for as long as possible.

The most important decision concerns the position of the largest shops, which are known in the industry as 'anchor stores'. These are usually department stores or large supermarkets that attract customers on their own. Designers normally place one anchor store at each end of the building, so that people who want to go from one to the other must pass dozens of smaller shops on the way. This arrangement is sometimes called the 'dumbbell' layout, because the plan looks like the piece of gym equipment, with a heavy weight at both ends and a long bar in between.

The main walkway between the anchors is rarely straight. Gentle curves mean that shoppers can never see more than a few shop fronts ahead, which encourages them to keep going to find out what comes next. Benches are placed in the middle of the walkway rather than against the walls, so that people who sit down are still facing the shop windows. Some designers also use different floor materials: hard, shiny floors in the walkway keep people moving, while softer surfaces just outside shop doors invite them to slow down and look inside.

Moving between floors is also controlled. In many centres the escalators are not placed one above the other. Instead, a shopper who arrives on the first floor has to walk some distance to reach the next escalator, passing more shops as they do so. Lifts, which are needed by parents with pushchairs and people in wheelchairs, are often located near the entrances, where they are easy to find but do not interrupt the flow of shoppers.

The food court is almost always on the top floor. Hungry visitors must travel through the whole building to reach it, and after eating they tend to take the escalators back down, passing through the shopping floors once again. Toilets are frequently placed next to the food court for the same reason.

Light and sound matter too. Many shopping centres have glass roofs, because natural daylight makes people feel relaxed. However, there are very few clocks and, on the lower floors, very few windows looking outside, which makes it easy to lose track of time. Some critics argue that these techniques are manipulative, but developers reply that they simply create a comfortable place in which people want to stay. Background music is usually kept quiet and slow, since fast music tends to make people hurry, and pleasant smells from cafés and bakeries are often allowed to spread into the walkways.

developers reply that they simply create a comfortable place (qarshi ma'no)

readings.title: Practice 2: The cash machine
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn va chizma (Passage 1 darajasi)
text: Today it is hard to imagine life without cash machines, but they are a relatively recent invention. The machine usually described as the first working cash machine was opened by a bank in north London in 1967. It did not use plastic cards. Instead, customers obtained special paper vouchers from the bank, which they fed into the machine together with a personal number. The machine then gave out a fixed amount of money.

The personal number, now known as a PIN, was originally planned to be six digits long. According to a popular story, the inventor reduced it to four after his wife said that four numbers were the most she could easily remember. Four-digit PINs are still the most common today, although some countries use longer ones. In most systems, the card is blocked if the wrong PIN is entered three times in a row.

A modern cash machine looks simple from the outside, but its front panel contains several separate parts. At the top is a screen that shows instructions, and in many machines there are buttons on either side of it for choosing options. Next to the keypad is the card slot. Most keypads now have a small raised dot on the number 5, which helps blind users find the keys by touch. The cash comes out of a narrow opening called the dispenser, usually located below the keypad, while a separate slot to the side prints receipts. Many machines also have a small camera above the screen, which records each customer for security reasons.

Inside, the machine is connected to the bank's central computer. When a customer asks for money, the whole process takes only a few seconds. First, the machine reads the information stored on the card's chip or magnetic strip. The customer then enters their PIN, which is checked by the bank's central computer rather than by the machine itself. Next, the computer checks whether there is enough money in the account. If there is, it sends a message back to the machine, which counts the notes. Finally, the card is returned — in most modern machines before the cash is released, because experience showed that people often forgot their cards once they had their money.

Although cash payments are falling in many countries as more people pay by card or phone, cash machines are still used millions of times every day. Some banks have even added new functions, allowing customers to pay in cash, pay bills or top up their mobile phones. At the same time, criminals sometimes attach false devices to the card slot in order to copy card details, so banks advise customers to check the machine and to cover the keypad with their hand when typing their PIN.

readings.title: Practice 3 (uyga): How coins are made
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn va chizma (Passage 1 darajasi), uy vazifasi
text: Although more and more payments are made electronically, coins are still produced in huge numbers. National mints — the organisations that make a country's coins — produce billions every year, partly to replace old coins and partly because people keep coins at home in jars and drawers, where they are effectively lost to the economy. In some countries, producing the smallest coins actually costs more than the coins are worth.

Each coin has several parts. The side with the main design, often a portrait of a head of state or a national symbol, is called the 'obverse', or 'heads'. The other side, the 'reverse', or 'tails', usually shows the value of the coin, known as its denomination. Most coins also show the year in which they were made. Around the edge of both faces is a slightly raised ring called the rim, which protects the design from wear and allows coins to be stacked neatly. The edge itself may be smooth, or it may have a pattern of small lines known as milling.

Milling has an interesting history. In the past, coins were made of valuable metals such as silver and gold, and dishonest people used to cut small amounts of metal from the edges. The metal could then be sold, while the coin was still spent at its full value. Milled edges made this practice easy to detect, because a damaged edge would be obvious at once. In England, the scientist Isaac Newton, who worked at the Royal Mint for around thirty years, became famous for his efforts to catch people who damaged or copied coins. Today coins are made from cheaper metals, but milling is still used, partly to help blind people tell coins apart by touch.

The production process begins with long strips of metal, which are rolled until they are exactly the right thickness. Round discs called 'blanks' are then punched out of the strips, rather like a cook cutting biscuits from dough. The blanks are heated in a furnace to make the metal softer, and then washed and dried so that they shine. Next, they pass through a machine that raises the rim. Finally, each blank is placed in a press, where two dies — hard metal tools carrying the designs — strike it from both sides at the same time with enormous force. A modern press can produce several hundred coins a minute.

Finished coins are inspected, often by cameras, to find any faulty ones, which are melted down and used again. The good coins are counted by machine and packed in bags before being sent to banks. Some coins, however, are never meant to be spent. Mints also produce special coins for collectors, which are struck more slowly and handled with gloves so that they remain in perfect condition. Worn and damaged coins that return from banks are also removed from use, melted down and turned into new metal.

kahoot.explain: "Three" chartda allaqachon bor, uni takrorlamang: "three security guards" — uch so'z, "three guards" — "Three three guards" bo'lib qoladi; "security guard" da esa ko'plik -s yo'q.

kahoot.q: Text: 'The new market sells local cheese and honey.' Statement: 'The new market sells more cheese than the old one.'
options: NOT GIVEN – no comparison is made
FALSE – it sells honey as well
TRUE – the market is described as new
kahoot.explain: Matn yangi bozorni eski bozor bilan solishtirmaydi — solishtirish matnda bo'lmasa, javob NOT GIVEN.

kahoot.q: Text: 'The shop opened in 2010 and moved to a larger building in 2015.' Statement: 'The shop has always been in the same building.'
options: NOT GIVEN – its size is unknown
kahoot.explain: Matn qarshisini aytadi: do'kon 2015 da kattaroq binoga ko'chgan — demak FALSE.

kahoot.q: Text: 'The lights are kept low to save energy.' Statement: 'Keeping the lights low has cut the shop's bills.'
options: NOT GIVEN – only the aim is stated
TRUE – saving energy always cuts bills
FALSE – the lights are not low
TRUE – the lights are kept low
kahoot.explain: Matnda maqsad (to save energy) bor, natija (hisob kamaygani) yo'q — maqsad natija emas, shuning uchun NOT GIVEN.

kahoot.q: Text: 'Some shoppers say the music is too loud, but the manager says it is quiet.' Statement: 'The manager thinks the music is too loud.'
options: FALSE – the manager says it is quiet
NOT GIVEN – only shoppers give a view
TRUE – the manager hears the music
kahoot.explain: "Kim aytdi?" tuzog'i: "too loud" matnda bor, lekin uni xaridorlar aytadi; menejer qarshisini aytadi — FALSE.

kahoot.q: Where is an 'aisle' in a supermarket?
options: at the front of the checkout
on the roof of the building
kahoot.explain: aisle — do'kondagi javonlar qatori orasidagi uzun, tor yo'lak.

kahoot.q: Which sentence uses 'bargain' correctly?
options: At half price, the coat was a real bargain.
He bargained the old coat because it was cold.
The shop was a bargain of forty workers.
She paid a bargain of money for the coat.
kahoot.explain: bargain — arzon xarid, haqiqiy qiymatidan arzonga olingan narsa: "a real bargain".

kahoot.q: An 'own-label' product is…
options: sold under the shop's own name
made by a famous global brand
given away free to loyal customers
kahoot.explain: own-label — ishlab chiqaruvchi brendi emas, do'konning o'z nomi bilan sotiladigan mahsulot (ko'pincha arzonroq).

kahoot.q: A 'retailer' is a person or company that…
kahoot.explain: retailer — mahsulotni xalqqa (oxirgi xaridorga) sotadigan do'kon yoki kompaniya; ishlab chiqaruvchi emas.

kahoot.q: 'The company's turnover rose by 10% last year.' This means that…
options: its total income from sales rose
the number of people working there rose
the price of its shares rose
kahoot.explain: turnover — savdo aylanmasi: ma'lum davrdagi umumiy sotuv summasi (foyda emas).

kahoot.q: Which phrase means 'buying something you did not plan to buy'?
kahoot.explain: impulse buying — rejada yo'q narsani o'ylamasdan, to'satdan sotib olish; window shopping — faqat vitrinalarni tomosha qilish.

kahoot.q: 'She complained to the shop many times, but to no avail.' This means…
options: she got her money back at once
kahoot.explain: to no avail — natijasiz, befoyda: shikoyatlari hech narsani o'zgartirmadi.

kahoot.q: If a shop 'manipulates' its customers, it…
options: controls them in a hidden, unfair way
gives them honest advice about prices
asks them to fill in a short survey
lets them pay later without any interest
kahoot.explain: manipulate — odamlarni yashirincha, nohalol yo'l bilan boshqarmoq (masalan, musiqa yoki yorug'lik orqali).

lessons.title: Unit 6 Listening — Section 2: Matching + Diagram labelling
lessons.grammar_topic: Section 2 kombinatsiyasi: Matching (ro'yxatdan harf) + Diagram labelling
lessons.vocab_topic: Unit 6 (Making money, spending money) — bank, bank kartasi, avtomatlar

objectives: Section 2 da ikki savol turi (matching + chizma) kelganda tayyorlanish vaqtini bo'lish: matching uchun savol kalit g'oyasi, chizma uchun orientatsiya (old/orqa, yuqori/past).
Matching'da tuzoqni tanish: gapiruvchi ro'yxatdagi deyarli hamma variantni tilga oladi, lekin shartga faqat bittasi mos keladi.
Rejaning o'zgarishini bildiruvchi iboralarni eshitish: "we thought about... but decided against", "used to be", "instead".
Chizmada joylashuvni bildiruvchi so'zlarni (on the back, in the bottom right-hand corner, just above, to the left of) tez tushunish.
Javobni ONE OR TWO WORDS chegarasida, to'g'ri imlo bilan yozish.
Speaking: Money and banks bo'yicha IELTS Part 1–3 savollariga Band 6 darajasida javob berish (javob + sabab + misol) va 4 mezon bo'yicha sherikni baholash.
materials: Student's Book, Unit 6, 60–61-betlar — savollar sahifalari (quyida rasm) va CD2 Track 1–2 audiosi.
Workbook, Unit 6, 39-bet — savollar sahifasi va Track 7 audiosi (imtihon rejimi, bir marta).

Xatolar daftari va uyga vazifa

Har xato sababi: tuzoq / joylashuv / imlo / paraphrase — daftarga yoziladi. Oxirgi 2–3 daqiqada uyga vazifa tushuntiriladi (ovozli normativda haqiqiy karta emas — SB chizmasi yoki telefon). Uyga: xatolar daftari, Speaking ovozli yozuv; shadowing (SB Track 2), diktant (WB Track 7) va kartani tasvirlash normativi.

intro: Section 2 — bitta gapiruvchining kundalik mavzudagi nutqi (monolog): ekskursiya, yangi xizmatlar haqida ma'lumot, yig'ilishdagi e'lon. 6.0 darajasida u odatda ikki savol turidan iborat; bu unitda — matching (ro'yxatdan harf tanlash) va chizma (diagram labelling).

Tayyorlanish vaqtini ikkiga bo'ling. Matching uchun: har savolning kalit g'oyasini tagiga chizing ("a branch on the CAMPUS", "a FREE GIFT for NEW customers", "special interest rates for STUDENTS") va ro'yxatdagi nomlarni bir marta ovoz chiqarmay o'qing. Chizma uchun: sarlavha (DEBIT CARD), old va orqa tomon, berilgan yorliqlar va bo'shliq qaysi joyda ekanini ko'ring.

Matching tuzog'i: gapiruvchi ro'yxatdagi deyarli HAMMA nomni tilga oladi. Masalan, sport zali yangi a'zolarga sumka beradi, lekin faqat bir yillik a'zolik sotib olinsa — bu shartli sovg'a, "free gift for new customers" emas. Savoldagi shartni (new customers, students, certain customers) har doim tekshiring.

Reja o'zgarishi iboralari: "we thought about meeting on Friday ... but decided against that", "used to be", "instead", "actually". Shu iboralar bilan rad etilgan yoki eskirgan variant — tuzoq; javob — yakuniy qaror. U ko'pincha iboradan keyin keladi, lekin oldin ham aytilishi mumkin: "It'll be on Monday — we thought about Friday, but decided against that".
Matching'da ro'yxatda ortiqcha variantlar bor (6 ta harf, 4 ta savol) — ba'zi harflar umuman ishlatilmaydi. Har savolga faqat BITTA harf yoziladi.

Chizma: gapiruvchi odatda mantiqiy tartibda yuradi (old tomon → orqa tomon → yana old) va savol raqamlari audio tartibida keladi. Joylashuv so'zlarini kuting: "at the top", "halfway down on the right", "on the back", "in the bottom right-hand corner", "just above", "to the left of".
Berilgan yorliqlar — yo'l ko'rsatkich. "Cardholder's name" eshitilsa, yaqinida 8 yoki 9 javobi bor. Bitta bo'shliqni o'tkazib yuborsangiz — to'xtamang, keyingi yorliqni kuting.
formulas: CAMPUS, FREE GIFT for NEW, STUDENTS
presentation: Gapiruvchi uchta bankni aytdi. Qaysi birini yozaman?
Savoldagi shartga to'liq mos kelganini. Masalan, "near the station" — ikki do'kon; "inside the station" — faqat bittasi.
Ro'yxatdagi harf ikki marta ishlatiladimi?
Bu savolda — yo'q, "Choose FOUR answers". Ba'zi Section 3 matching savollarida harf takrorlanishi mumkin — ko'rsatmani o'qing.
"Toilets" eshitdim, ro'yxatda "restrooms" bor.
Bu paraphrase: toilets (BrE) = restrooms (AmE). Ro'yxat deyarli har doim boshqa so'z bilan yoziladi.
Chizmada qaysi bo'shliqdan boshlayman?
Eng kichik raqamdan. Audio savol raqamlari tartibida keladi, chizmadagi joylashuv tartibida emas.
"Wooden" chizmada bor. Javobga yozamanmi?
Yo'q. Yorliqda bor so'zni takrorlamang: "wooden ___" → faqat "door", "wooden door" emas.
Matching va chizma orasida pauza bo'ladimi?
Section 2 da ko'pincha qisqa pauza bor. Shu paytda chizmaga qayting va birinchi bo'shliqni toping.
notes: 5.0 da matching (21-dars) va chizma (8-dars) alohida o'rganilgan. Endi ular bitta Section 2 da ketma-ket keladi — asosiy ko'nikma: birinchi qismdan ikkinchisiga vaqtida o'tish.
Tekshiruvda har javobdan keyin skriptdan aynan o'sha gapni ekranga chiqaring va tuzoq gapni boshqa rang bilan ko'rsating.
Kuchli o'quvchilarga: Track 1 da har bank uchun BARCHA aytilgan ma'lumotni jadvalga yozish (filial, sovg'a, foiz, to'lov) — keyin savollarga javob berish.
mistakes: SB Q2: shartli sovg'a beradigan bankni yozish
Yangi mijozga shartsiz sovg'a beradigan bank
Kalit: D — International Union. A (Evergreen) — laptop faqat £5,000 balans 9 oy saqlansa; yangi mijozga sovg'a emas
SB Q3: eng yuqori foiz beradigan bankni yozish
Aynan TALABALARGA maxsus foiz beradigan bank
Kalit: C — Great Western. F (Northern Star) — eng yuqori foiz omonatchilar uchun, talabalar uchun emas
SB Q5: yorliqdagi so'zni javobga yozish
Kalit: picture. "Hologram" va "moving" yorliqda bor — takrorlanmaydi
WB Q1: rad etilgan joyni yozish ("we thought about ...")
Kalit: D — entrance hall. B (in front of the building) — "we thought about ... but decided against that"
WB Q10: bo'shliq ma'nosini tekshirmay raqam yozish
Kalit: 10 / ten products. 495 — mashina sig'imi, buyurtma chegarasi emas

how: CORE — bank va hisob so'zlari (SB 1-mashq so'zlari shu yerda); STRONG — karta va avtomat qismlari; SUPER — suhbatdagi iboralar.
Juftlikda: har o'quvchi o'z bankini (yoki orzudagi bankni) 4 ta so'z bilan tasvirlaydi: branch, interest rate, charges, in credit.
core: I opened a bank account last week.
Check your balance before you pay.
There is a branch near the university.
I pay my phone bill by direct debit.
This bank offers a high interest rate.
Bu bank yuqori foiz stavkasini taklif qiladi.
She keeps her savings in a separate account.
Some banks have no charges for students.
Ba'zi banklarda talabalar uchun xizmat haqi yo'q.
Check the expiry date on your card.
strong: The magnetic strip is on the back of the card.
Insert the card with the chip facing up.
A hologram makes a card hard to copy.
There is a vending machine in the corridor.
The museum has been completely refurbished.
super: Charges are the same across the board.
Try not to go into the red this month.
Bu oy minusga tushmaslikka harakat qiling.
In the end, we decided against buying a new car.
Oxir-oqibat yangi mashina sotib olishdan voz kechdik.

class_ex.title: Joylashuv iboralari — namunaviy karta bilan
class_ex.instr: Ustoz doskaga namunaviy talaba guvohnomasini (student ID card) chizadi va qismlarini inglizcha yozadi. OLD tomon: tepada — college name; o'ngda, o'rtada — photo; chapda yuqoridan pastga — student number, course name, student's name; pastki o'ng burchakda — stamp. ORQA tomon: bir chetidan ikkinchi chetigacha — barcode. Ustoz joylashuvni aytadi, o'quvchilar chizmadagi o'sha joyni ko'rsatadi va u yerda nima borligini aytadi. SB dagi debit card chizmasi bu mashqda ishlatilmaydi — uning bo'shliqlari Track 2 savollari. Haqiqiy bank kartalari ishlatilmaydi.
items: "On the front, at the top."
"Halfway down on the right."
"On the back — a row of thin black lines going from one side to the other."
"In the bottom right-hand corner."
"Just above the student's name."
"Above the course name, on the left."
why: "At the top" — yuqori qism.
"Halfway down" — o'rtasida; "on the right" — o'ngda.
"From one side to the other" — bir chetidan ikkinchi chetigacha, butun kenglik bo'ylab.
"Bottom right-hand corner" — pastki o'ng burchak.
"Just above" — darhol ustida.
"Above ..., on the left" — chap tomonda, kurs nomi ustida.
class_ex.note: Mashqdan keyin juftlikda: bir o'quvchi joyni aytadi, sherigi ko'rsatadi — rollar almashadi.

class_ex.title: "Oxirgi qaror qaysi?" — tuzoq mashqi
class_ex.instr: Ustoz gapni o'qiydi. O'quvchilar javobni va tuzoqni aytadi.
items: "We thought about holding the concert in the park, but decided against that — it'll be in the town hall." — Where?
"The first-aid room used to be on the ground floor, but now it's next to the gym." — Where now?
"The Rose Café and Café Blue are both near the museum, but only Mario's is actually inside the museum building." — In the museum?
"The bookshop gives a free bag to new customers who spend more than £50." — A free gift for ALL new customers?
"The hall can seat 200 people, but each student can bring a maximum of three guests." — How many guests per student?
why: "Decided against" — birinchi variant (park) bekor qilindi; javob undan keyin keladi.
"Used to be" — o'tmishdagi joy, tuzoq; javob "but now" dan keyin.
"Near" ≠ "inside": ikki kafe muzey yaqinida, binoning ichida esa faqat Mario's.
Sovg'a shartli (£50 dan ortiq xarid) — har bir yangi mijozga berilmaydi.
200 — zal sig'imi (joylar soni), bitta talabaga ruxsat etilgan mehmonlar soni emas.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 1: Saving money
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda so'rang va javob bering; har javob 2–3 gap: javob + sabab/misol (because, for example, to be honest).
items: Do you prefer to save money or spend it?
How did you learn to manage money?
Do you use cash or cards more often?
Is it easy for young people to save money nowadays?
answers: To be honest, I'm more of a saver. I usually put some of my pocket money aside every week, because I like knowing that I have something for emergencies, although I do spend a bit on snacks with friends.
Mostly from my mum, actually. When I was about twelve, she started giving me a weekly allowance and asked me to write down everything I bought, which taught me to think twice before spending.
These days I use my card much more often. Contactless payment is quicker, and most shops in Tashkent accept it now. I only carry cash for the bazaar or for taxis in smaller towns.

Not really, I'd say. There are so many temptations, like new phones and online shopping, that it's hard to resist them. On the other hand, banking apps make it easier to track your spending if you use them properly.
why: 'To be honest' diskurs belgisi, 'to put money aside' iborasi, 'because' sabab va 'although' bilan qarama-qarshi detal.
Past simple hikoya, 'which taught me to...' relative clause va 'to think twice' idiomatik iborasi.
Solishtirma 'much more often', box iborasi 'contactless payment' va aniq misol (bazaar, taxis).
'so many ... that' tuzilmasi, 'On the other hand' bilan ikkinchi fikr va 'if' shart gapi.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 2: Saving money for something special
class_ex.instr: 1 daqiqa tayyorlanish (qog'ozga 5–6 kalit so'z), keyin 1–2 daqiqa to'xtovsiz gapiring; sherigingiz vaqtni o'lchaydi va S6_CLASS bo'yicha band qo'yadi.
items: Describe a time when you saved money for something special.
You should say:
what you saved for
how long it took
how you saved the money
and explain how you felt when you finally got it.
answers: I'd like to talk about the time I saved up for my first laptop, which I bought last summer when I was fifteen. I needed it for my IELTS preparation and online lessons, because sharing the family computer with my two brothers was really inconvenient.
It took me about eight months. The laptop cost around six million soums, and my parents agreed to pay half if I could find the rest myself.

So I made a plan. First of all, my father helped me open a bank account, and every week I put most of my pocket money aside instead of spending it on snacks and games. I also earned some extra money by helping my uncle in his shop on Saturdays. I wrote a simple budget in a notebook and tried hard to stick to it, which wasn't always easy when my friends went to the cinema without me.

When I finally had enough, I went to the shop with my dad and paid for it myself. Honestly, I felt incredibly proud, and I've been much more careful with money ever since. If I hadn't saved for it on my own, I don't think I would value it so much today.
why: FC: kartochka tartibida — nima → qancha vaqt → qanday → his-tuyg'u; First of all / also / When I finally bilan bog'langan, 2 daqiqaga yetadi.
LR: box iboralari (pocket money, to put money aside, to open a bank account, to stick to a budget) va 'to save up for', 'incredibly proud' kollokatsiyalari o'z joyida.
GRA: relative clause (which I bought, which wasn't always easy), present perfect ('I've been ... ever since'), aralash shart gap (If I hadn't saved ..., I wouldn't value ...), gerund (by helping).
Nega Band 7 emas: fikrlar oddiy va ketma-ket, idioma kam — Band 6–6.5 uchun namunaviy daraja.
box: pocket money — cho'ntak puli (ota-ona beradigan xarajat puli)
to put money aside — pulni chetga qo'yib yig'moq
to live within your means — topganiga yarasha yashamoq
to be in debt — qarzda bo'lmoq
contactless payment — kontaktsiz to'lov (kartani tekkizib to'lash)
to open a bank account — bankda hisob ochmoq
to stick to a budget — byudjetga qat'iy amal qilmoq
to make ends meet — kun ko'rmoq, tirikchilikni eplamoq
class_ex.note: Namunani ustoz o'qiydi (taxminan 1:50); o'quvchilar box iboralarini eshitganda qo'l ko'taradi. Mavzu: standart IELTS Part 2 kartochkasi; savollar va namuna — Jony Academy original materiali.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 3: Money, banks and a cashless society
class_ex.instr: Ustoz savol beradi, 2–3 o'quvchi javob beradi: fikr → sabab → misol → qarama-qarshi fikr yoki xulosa (har javob 30–40 soniya).
items: Should schools teach children how to manage money?
Will we live in a completely cashless society in the future? Is that a good thing?
Why do some people get into debt?
answers: Yes, I strongly believe they should. Many young people leave school without knowing how to stick to a budget or how interest on a loan works, so they make expensive mistakes later. For example, a simple course could show students how to plan their spending for a month. Of course, parents also play a role, but not every family talks about money openly, so schools can fill that gap.

I think we're moving in that direction, especially in big cities where contactless payment and mobile apps are already very common. It's certainly convenient and safer than carrying cash around. However, I'm not sure it's entirely a good thing. Older people and those in rural areas might find it difficult, and if the banking system goes down, people could be left without any way to pay. So I'd prefer cash to remain as a backup.

There are several reasons. Some people simply don't live within their means: they buy things they can't afford, often on credit, because they want to keep up with their friends. Others get into debt for reasons beyond their control, such as losing a job or facing unexpected medical bills. Another factor is that borrowing has become very easy, as many apps offer instant loans, so people don't always think about how they'll pay the money back.
why: Strategiya: aniq fikr (strongly believe) → sabab → misol (a simple course) → 'Of course ... but' qarama-qarshi fikr → xulosa (fill that gap).
Bashorat savoli: hozirgi tendensiya (we're moving in that direction) → afzallik → 'However' bilan kamchilik → 'might / could' ehtimol fe'llari → shaxsiy xulosa.
Sabablar ro'yxati: Some people ... / Others ... / Another factor is ...; box iborasi 'live within their means', present perfect (has become) va 'beyond their control' iborasi.

class_ex.title: Speaking rubrikasi — IELTS band 5–7 (4 mezon)
head: Mezon
Band 5
Band 6 (kurs maqsadi)
Band 7
Sherik tekshiradi
rows: Ko'p to'xtaydi va takrorlaydi; faqat and, but, because.
Uzoq gapiradi, ba'zan to'xtab o'zini tuzatadi; firstly, also, however bor, lekin mexanik.
Zo'riqishsiz gapiradi; on the other hand, as a result, what I mean is tabiiy ishlatiladi.
Part 2 da 1:40–2:00 gapirdimi? Necha marta uzoq to'xtadi?
Mavzu so'zlari yetarli, 1–2 'less common' ibora; so'z topolmasa boshqacha aytadi.
Idioma va kollokatsiyalar (to settle in, a sense of belonging) o'z joyida.
Oddiy + murakkab gaplar (because, which, if, when); xatolar bor, lekin ma'no aniq.
Turli tuzilmalar (present perfect, conditional, passive) asosan xatosiz.
Kamida 2 ta murakkab gap bo'ldimi? Zamon to'g'rimi?
Umuman tushunarli; ayrim tovush/urg'u xatolari (th, w/v, so'z urg'usi).
Oson tushuniladi; urg'u va intonatsiya ma'noni ta'kidlaydi.

why: "Only one – Finley's – actually has an office inside one of the university buildings". Tuzoq: Great Western va Moneysafe — "branches near the university".

"With International Union, you'll get a phone when you open your first account". Tuzoq: Evergreen laptopi — faqat £5,000 dan ortiq balans 9 oy saqlansa; Moneysafe va Northern Star — "if you put money on deposit".

"Great Western will lend money at a lower percentage than normal to people registered on higher education courses". Tuzoq: Northern Star — "the highest rate of interest to savers", talabalarga maxsus emas.

"Moneysafe actually say that if you're in credit, your account won't cost a thing". "Certain customers" = hisobida puli borlar. Tuzoq: Evergreen, Finley's, Northern Star — "charge the same across the board".

listenings.title: Jony Academy mashqi: Greenfield Supermarket — new services
intro: Supermarket menejeri xaridorlarga yangi xizmatlar joylashuvini va o'z-o'ziga xizmat ko'rsatish kassasini tushuntiradi.
Tayyorlanish: 30 soniya Q1–4 (kalit g'oya), 30 soniya chizma (Q5–10). Ko'rsatma: ONE OR TWO WORDS for each answer.
transcript: [Ustoz uchun] Ustoz skriptni oddiy tezlikda (taxminan 150 so'z/daqiqa) BIR MARTA o'qiydi.

MANAGER: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for coming to this short talk. As you know, Greenfield Supermarket has just been redesigned, so I'd like to explain where you can find some of our new services, and then show you how our self-service checkouts work.

MANAGER: Let's start with returns. If something you've bought is faulty, you might expect to take it back to the checkout where you paid. Please don't — the checkout staff are very busy. Instead, go to the customer service desk, which is just on your right as you come in. They'll give you a refund or a replacement.

MANAGER: Now, online orders. Until last month, you collected these from a counter by the main entrance, but that area was getting far too crowded. So now there's a collection point in the car park, next to the trolley shelter. You can drive right up to it, and a member of staff will put the bags in your car.

MANAGER: A lot of you have asked about photo printing. We did think about putting the photo machines in the café, so people could have a coffee while they wait, but there simply wasn't enough space. So you'll find them on the first floor, next to the pharmacy.

MANAGER: And finally, recycling. The bottle machines used to be in the car park, but people told us they didn't like carrying bags of bottles across it in the rain. So we've moved them to just inside the main entrance. You put your empty plastic bottles in, and you get a voucher to spend in the store.

MANAGER: Right, now let's look at the self-service checkouts. If you look at the picture on the screen here... The first thing you'll see is the large touch screen. Before you start scanning, you need to choose your language — we have English, Uzbek and Russian — because all the instructions after that will appear in the language you pick. Some people press 'Start' straight away, but please choose the language first.

MANAGER: Below the screen is the scanner. It's a flat glass surface with a red line across it, and it reads the barcodes on your items. You don't need to press anything — just hold the barcode over the glass until you hear a beep.

MANAGER: When an item has been scanned, you put it in the bagging area on the right. Underneath the bags there are scales, which check the weight of everything you put down. If the weight doesn't match the item you've scanned, the machine will stop and ask you to wait for help. So please don't put your handbag or your coat in the bagging area!

MANAGER: When you've finished, you pay. On the right, below the scanner, there's the card reader. As well as bank cards, it also accepts phones, so if you have a payment app, you can simply hold your phone over it. It doesn't take watches yet, although we're hoping to add that next year.
MANAGER: If you prefer cash, coins go in the small tray at the bottom, and notes go in the long slot on the left, just under the scanner. Your change will come out of the same tray as your coins.

MANAGER: Last of all, you'll notice a light on top of each machine. While you're scanning, it stays green. If there's a problem, or if you're buying something that needs an age check, it turns yellow, and one of our assistants will come over straight away. Don't worry if it flashes red for a second when the machine starts up — that's just the system checking itself.
MANAGER: Right, if you'd like to try one now, please follow me to the checkout area.
