homework_intro: Bugun Section 2 da ikki savol turini ketma-ket yechdik: avval matching, keyin chizma. Eng ko'p ball ikki joyda yo'qoladi — matching tuzog'ida va chizmada yorliqdagi so'zni takrorlashda.

Birinchi vazifa — shadowing: ustoz guruhga SB Track 2 audiosini va skript rasmini yuboradi. Student's Book Track 2 (debit card) ni skript bilan 2 marta tinglang, keyin gapiruvchi bilan birga (bir soniya orqada) ovoz chiqarib takrorlang. Joylashuv iboralarini (halfway down, on the back, bottom right-hand corner, just above) alohida daftarga yozing.

Ikkinchi vazifa — diktant: ustoz guruhga WB Track 7 audiosini yuboradi. Uning oxirgi qismini (staff room drinks machine) tinglab, 5 ta gapni so'zma-so'z yozing va daftaringiz rasmini ustoz belgilagan muddatgacha guruhga yuboring; muddat tugagach ustoz skript rasmini yuboradi — solishtiring va xatolarni qizil bilan belgilang.

Uchinchi vazifa — ovozli normativ: Student's Book dagi debit card chizmasini (yoki o'z telefoningizni) ingliz tilida 6 gap bilan tasvirlang — har gapda bitta joylashuv iborasi bo'lsin. Haqiqiy bank kartangizni tasvirlamang: karta raqami, amal qilish muddati va CVV kodini hech qachon aytmang va yozmang. Ovozli xabarni guruhga yuboring.
Speaking vazifasi — bugungi Part 2 kartochkasini uyda ovozli yozib yuboring (1 daqiqa tayyorlanish, 2 daqiqa gapirish).

kahoot.q: A matching task has 4 questions and 6 options (A–F); no letter is used twice. What is true?
options: Two of the options are not used
Every option is used at least once
The last two options are always wrong
kahoot.explain: 4 savolga 6 variant — ikkita harf ortiqcha, ular odatda audioda tuzoq sifatida eshitiladi.

kahoot.q: You hear: 'We considered the library for the party, but in the end we chose the sports hall.' Where will the party be?
kahoot.explain: 'In the end we chose' — oxirgi qaror; birinchi aytilgan kutubxona tuzoq.

kahoot.q: You hear: 'The gift shop used to be on the ground floor, but now it's at the top of the building.' Where is it now?
kahoot.explain: 'Used to be' — o'tmishdagi joy (tuzoq); 'but now' dan keyingi ma'lumot — javob.

kahoot.q: Question: 'discounts for STUDENTS'. You hear: 'The gym gives 20% off to anyone who joins before May.' Is the gym the answer?
options: No – it isn't just for students
Yes – it gives a discount of 20%
Yes – students often join in May
No – 20% is too small a discount
kahoot.explain: Chegirma may oyidan oldin a'zo bo'lgan har kimga beriladi, talabalarga maxsus emas — savoldagi 'talabalar uchun' shartiga mos kelmaydi.

kahoot.q: When can you use the same letter for two questions in a matching task?
options: Only if the instructions say so
Always in Section 2 of the test
Never in any IELTS matching task
kahoot.explain: Harf takrorlanishi mumkin bo'lsa, ko'rsatmada 'You may use any letter more than once' deyiladi; aks holda har harf bir marta.

kahoot.q: An option in the box says 'information desk'. What might the speaker say instead?
options: where you pay for all your shopping
where the staff go to have lunch
where you can leave your coat and bags
kahoot.explain: Ro'yxatdagi variant audioda boshqa so'zlar bilan aytiladi: information desk — savollarga javob beradigan joy.

kahoot.q: In a diagram-labelling task, in what order do the answers come in the recording?
options: From left to right on the picture
From top to bottom on the picture
kahoot.explain: Audio savol raqamlari tartibida yuradi; chizmadagi joylashuv tartibi boshqacha bo'lishi mumkin.

kahoot.q: You have 30 seconds before a diagram task. What should you look at first?
options: The title and the labels already given
The number of words in the recording
The colours used in the picture
The longest answer you might need
kahoot.explain: Sarlavha va berilgan yorliqlar orientatsiya beradi: qaysi tomon, qayerga qarash va bo'shliqqa qanday ma'lumot kerakligi.

kahoot.q: Label: 'metal ___ on the side'. You hear: 'There's a metal handle on the side.' ONE WORD ONLY. What do you write?
kahoot.explain: 'Metal' yorliqda bor — takrorlanmaydi; bo'shliqqa faqat yangi so'z yoziladi: handle.

kahoot.q: ONE OR TWO WORDS. The speaker says 'the bus station'. What should you write?
kahoot.explain: 'The bus station' — uch so'z, chegarani buzadi; artiklsiz 'bus station' — ikki so'z.

kahoot.q: You hear: 'The clock is just above the notice board.' Where is the clock?
options: A little above the notice board
A little below the notice board
kahoot.explain: 'Just above' — darhol ustida, juda yaqin; 'below' — ostida, 'high above' — ancha yuqorida.

kahoot.q: You hear the right word but spell it wrongly on the answer sheet. What happens?
kahoot.explain: Listening'da noto'g'ri imlo bilan yozilgan javob xato hisoblanadi — ball berilmaydi.

kahoot.q: 'Your account is in credit' means…
options: it has a new credit card
kahoot.explain: In credit — hisobda pul bor (minusda emas).

kahoot.q: An overdraft allows you to…
options: spend more money than you have
earn more interest on your savings
kahoot.explain: Overdraft — hisobdagi puldan ko'proq sarflash imkoni (bankdan qisqa muddatli qarz).

kahoot.q: If you pay your phone bill by direct debit, …
options: it is taken from your account automatically
you pay it in cash at the phone shop each month
you post a cheque to the phone company
a friend pays it for you every month
kahoot.explain: Direct debit — hisobdan avtomatik to'lov: pul har oy hisobingizdan o'zi yechiladi.

kahoot.q: 'There is a branch of my bank near the station.' Here 'branch' means…
kahoot.explain: Branch — bankning filiali (mahalliy bo'limi).

kahoot.q: If you go into the red, you…
kahoot.explain: Go into the red — minusga tushmoq: hisobdagidan ko'p sarflab, bankka qarzdor bo'lmoq.

kahoot.q: 'The bank charges are pretty steep.' This means the charges are…
kahoot.explain: Pretty steep (so'zlashuv) — ancha baland, qimmat.

kahoot.q: 'We decided against taking the bus.' This means we…
options: waited a long time for it
kahoot.explain: Decide against — biror narsadan voz kechmoq; Listening'da shu ibora bilan rad etilgan variant — tuzoq.

kahoot.q: 'The bank raised its charges across the board.' This means the charges went up…
kahoot.explain: Across the board — hamma uchun bir xil, istisnosiz.

lessons.title: Unit 7 Reading — Passage 2: Matching headings + Matching features + Sentence completion
lessons.grammar_topic: Uch savol turi bitta passage'da: Matching headings + Matching features + Sentence completion (Passage 2)
lessons.vocab_topic: Unit 7 (Relationships) — yolg'on va ishonch, oila va tug'ilish tartibi, do'stlik
lessons.book_ref: Complete IELTS Bands 5–6.5: Student's Book, Unit 7, 70–72-betlar (Reading Section 2); Workbook, Unit 7, 44–45-betlar. Practice 1–3 — Jony Academy matnlari.; Speaking — Jony Academy original materiali (Part 1 mavzusi: Making friends).
objectives: Bitta passage'da uch savol turi kelganda ishlash tartibini tanlash: xarita → sarlavhalar va variantlarni belgilash → sentence completion.
Matching headings'da xatboshining asosiy g'oyasini tafsilotdan ajratish va "bir xil so'z" tuzog'iga tushmaslik.
Matching features'da variantlarni (odam, tajriba, guruh) matnda tez topib tagiga chizish va bitta harf bir necha marta ishlatilishi mumkinligini hisobga olish.
Sentence completion'da so'z chegarasi (ONE WORD ONLY), so'z turi, grammatika va imloni tekshirish.
Passage 2 ni 20 daqiqada tugatish: har savol guruhiga vaqt ajratish.
Speaking: Relationships (oila, do'stlik va ishonch) bo'yicha IELTS Part 1–3 savollariga Band 6 darajasida javob berish (javob + sabab + misol) va 4 mezon bo'yicha sherikni baholash.
materials: Student's Book, Unit 7, 70–72-betlar (Reading Section 2: "The truth about lying") — sinfda birga ishlanadi.
Workbook, Unit 7, 44–45-betlar ("Establishing your birthrights") — mustaqil mashq.
Practice 1–3 matnlari chop etilgan varaqlar (har o'quvchiga) — pastdagi Reading bo'limidan.
Rangli qalamlar: sarlavha kalit so'zlari — bir rang, matching features variantlari — ikkinchi rang.
Doskada uch ustun: "Headings → har xatbosh", "Features → variantlar qayerda?", "Sentences → matn tartibida".
Part 2 kartochkasi (har juftlikka chop etilgan), taymer, S6_CLASS rubrikasi varaqasi.

Xulosa va vazifa
Practice 2 "Good neighbours" uyga (17 daqiqa); Practice 3 — qo'shimcha, ixtiyoriy; 30-Day Reading Challenge (Day 4, Day 29); Speaking Part 2 ovozli yozuv; xatolar daftari to'ldiriladi.

intro: IELTS 6.0 darajasida Passage 2 da ko'pincha uch xil savol turi keladi. Bugungi kombinatsiya: Matching headings (1–6), Matching features (7–10) va Sentence completion (11–13). Uchalasining TARTIB qoidasi har xil — shuni bilish vaqtni tejaydi.

Matching headings — xatboshilar A, B, C... tartibida keladi, sarlavhalar ro'yxati esa aralash. Har xatboshiga bitta sarlavha, ro'yxatda 2–3 ta ortiqcha sarlavha bor. Sarlavha xatboshining ASOSIY g'oyasini beradi, bitta gapini emas.

Matching features — gaplar (7–10) matn tartibida EMAS. Variantlar ro'yxati (odamlar, tajribalar, guruhlar) matnda turli joyda uchraydi. Shuning uchun birinchi ish — variantlarni matnda topib, tagiga chizish. "You may use any letter more than once" — ba'zi harf ikki marta, ba'zisi umuman ishlatilmasligi mumkin.

Sentence completion — gaplar matn tartibida keladi (ALWAYS). Gapdagi kalit so'z bilan joyni toping, javobni matndan AYNAN ko'chiring. So'z chegarasi: ONE WORD ONLY — faqat bitta so'z; "their feelings" yoki "real clues" — 0 ball.

Qaysi tartibda ishlash kerak? Tavsiya: 1) 1 daqiqa xarita — uch guruhni ko'zdan kechiring, sarlavhalardagi kalit so'zlarni va features variantlarini (Koko, children, TV programme) belgilang. 2) Matnni xatboshima-xatbosh o'qing: har xatboshidan keyin sarlavha tanlang va shu xatboshida qaysi variant (A/B/C) borligini chetiga yozing. 3) Features gaplarini belgilangan joylar bilan solishtiring. 4) Sentence completion — oxirida, tartib bilan skanerlab.

Headings tuzog'i: xatboshidagi bitta tafsilot sarlavhaga mos kelib qoladi ("detail trap") yoki sarlavhadagi so'z matnda aynan uchraydi. Masalan, SB D xatboshida "liars ... do not appear nervous" bor — bu yolg'onchilar nima QILISHI emas, odamlarning noto'g'ri ishonchi haqida.
Vaqt: Passage 2 ga 20 daqiqa. Taxminan: xarita — 1, headings — 8, features — 5, sentence completion — 4, tekshirish va transfer — 2 daqiqa.
formulas: Har xatbosh chetiga variant harfini yozing
Sentence completion — tartib bilan, aynan ko'chirish
presentation: Headings'ni birinchi qilamanmi yoki oxirida?
Xatboshini o'qiyotganda darhol qiling — keyin qayta o'qish shart bo'lmaydi. Qiyin xatboshini belgilab o'tib keting.
Features'da bitta harf ikki marta chiqdi. Xatomi?
Yo'q. "You may use any letter more than once" — bu normal. Ba'zi harf umuman ishlatilmasligi ham mumkin.
Features gaplari matn tartibidami?
Yo'q. Shuning uchun variantlarni oldindan tagiga chizish kerak — gapni variant joylari bilan solishtirasiz.
Sarlavhadagi so'z xatboshida bor. Demak shu sarlavhami?
Shart emas. Butun xatbosh shu haqidami — tekshiring. Bir xil so'z ko'pincha tuzoq.
"nervous" o'rniga "nervously" yozsam bo'ladimi?
Yo'q. Bo'shliqdan keyin "behaviour" (ot) — oldidan sifat kerak. So'z turi xato bo'lsa — 0 ball.
Sentence completion javobi matnda boshqa shaklda bo'lsa-chi?
Matndagi so'zni o'zgartirmay yozing. Agar gapga grammatik mos kelmasa — boshqa so'zni qidiring.
notes: 5.0 da matching headings (10-dars), sentence completion (15-dars) va matching features'ni alohida o'rgangan edik. Endi uchalasi bitta passage'da — asosiy ko'nikma tartib va vaqtni boshqarish.
SB matnida har xatboshidan keyin o'quvchilardan so'rang: "Asosiy g'oya nima?" va "Bu xatboshida qaysi tajriba bor?" — ikkala savolga bir vaqtda javob berishga o'rgating.
Kuchli o'quvchilarga: ishlatilmagan sarlavhalar (iii, vii) nega mos kelmasligini isbotlash.

class_ex.title: Nega bu javoblar xato? (SB, 4-mashq)
class_ex.instr: Bu javoblar 11–13-savollarga yozilgan va 0 ball olgan. Har biri uchun sababni ayting: so'z soni, so'z turi, imlo yoki noto'g'ri ma'lumot.
items: 11 — body language
11 — nervously
12 — their feelings
12 — themsleves
12 — feeling
13 — real clues
13 — use
why: ONE WORD ONLY — ikki so'z. Bo'shliqdan keyin "behaviour" keladi, oldidan sifat kerak, ot emas. Mazmuni ham teskari: matn aynan body language yolg'onni fosh qilmaydi deydi.
"display ___ behaviour" — otdan oldin sifat: nervous. Ravish (nervously) grammatikaga mos emas.
"their own" gapda allaqachon bor. Ikki so'z yozildi — chegara buzildi.
To'g'ri imlo "themselves". Bundan tashqari, gapda "their own" dan keyin "themselves" grammatikaga to'g'ri kelmaydi.
Matnda "several references to his feelings" — ko'plik. "feeling" — boshqa shakl.
Ikki so'z; bundan tashqari "real clues" — gapda "people's ___ rather than their movements" ga mos emas. Javob — words.
"people's ___" — egalik shaklidan keyin ot kerak. "use" bu yerda fe'l — matnda "the words that people use".
class_ex.note: Mashqdan keyin doskaga yozing: ONE WORD ONLY → 1) so'z soni, 2) so'z turi, 3) imlo, 4) gapga qo'yib qayta o'qish.

class_ex.title: Asosiy g'oya yoki tafsilot?
class_ex.instr: Ustoz qisqa xatboshini o'qiydi. O'quvchilar ikki sarlavhadan birini tanlaydi va ikkinchisi nega tuzoq ekanini aytadi.
items: "Many people believe that liars avoid eye contact. However, films of real liars show that they look at you just as often as honest people do. Our ideas about lying are often simply wrong." — A) Liars avoid eye contact  B) A common belief that is not true

"Twins often share a room, clothes and friends. As a result, it can be hard for them to develop separate identities, and parents may need to treat them as individuals." — A) Twins who share clothes  B) The challenge of being an individual

"Children begin to tell simple lies at about three. By five or six, their lies become more believable, because they understand what other people know and do not know." — A) How lying develops with age  B) Three-year-olds are honest

"The survey was repeated in 60 countries. In every place, people gave almost the same answers about how to spot a liar." — A) Surprising differences between cultures  B) Similar views around the world
why: Asosiy g'oya — oxirgi gap: fikrimiz noto'g'ri. A — xatboshidagi birinchi gap, lekin keyin rad etiladi. Bu SB D xatboshisiga o'xshaydi.
Kiyim — bitta tafsilot. Butun xatbosh egizaklarning alohida shaxs bo'lish qiyinligi haqida.
Xatbosh yosh bilan o'zgarish haqida (3 → 5–6). B — teskari: uch yoshda ham yolg'on gapiradi.
"Almost the same answers" — o'xshashlik. A — teskari ma'no tuzog'i.
class_ex.note: Har javobdan keyin so'rang: "Xatboshini bir gapda qanday aytasiz?" — o'quvchi o'z so'zi bilan aytib bera olsa, sarlavhani to'g'ri tanlaydi.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 1: Making friends
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda so'rang va javob bering; har javob 2–3 gap: javob + sabab/misol (because, for example, to be honest).
items: Is it easy for you to make new friends?
Where do young people usually make friends in your country?
Do you still keep in touch with your childhood friends?
Do you prefer having a few close friends or lots of friends?
answers: Actually, it depends on the situation. At school I find it quite easy because we share the same interests, but in a completely new place I'm a bit shy at first, so it usually takes me a few days to open up.

Mostly at school and in the mahalla, where children grow up playing together in the yard. These days a lot of teenagers also make friends at sports clubs or language courses, and some even meet people online.
Yes, with a couple of them. My best friend from primary school moved to Tashkent three years ago, but we've stayed in touch on Telegram, and we always meet up when he comes back for the holidays.
To be honest, I'd rather have a few close friends. If you have too many, you can't really rely on all of them, whereas a small group of people you trust will support you when things go wrong.
why: 'It depends on...' + but bilan ikki vaziyat solishtiriladi; 'to open up' — tabiiy phrasal verb.
'where' bilan relative clause va 'These days' bilan hozirgi holat; mahalliy misol (mahalla, language courses) javobni kengaytiradi.
Past simple (moved) va present perfect (we've stayed in touch) farqi to'g'ri; 'meet up' — og'zaki ibora.
'I'd rather...' + first conditional (If you have...) va whereas bilan qarama-qarshi fikr; box'dagi 'rely on' ishlatilgan.
class_ex.note: Mavzu: IELTS Speaking Part 1 to'plami (Making friends) — faqat savol g'oyalari olindi; namuna javoblar Jony Academy original.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 2: A family member you get on well with
class_ex.instr: 1 daqiqa tayyorlanish (qog'ozga 5–6 kalit so'z), keyin 1–2 daqiqa to'xtovsiz gapiring; sherigingiz vaqtni o'lchaydi va S6_CLASS bo'yicha band qo'yadi.
items: Describe a member of your family that you get on well with.
You should say:
who this person is
what he or she is like
what you do together
and explain why you get on so well.
class_ex.answers: I'd like to talk about my grandfather, who lives with us in our family house in Namangan. He's seventy-two and used to be a maths teacher, so everyone in our mahalla knows him and treats him with a lot of respect. As for what he's like, he's calm, patient and has a great sense of humour. Although he's quite strict about good manners, he never raises his voice, and he always listens carefully before giving advice. We do lots of things together. Every evening after dinner we drink green tea in the courtyard and play chess, and he has taught me some clever tricks that I still use in maths lessons. At weekends I help him look after his apricot trees while he tells me stories about his childhood, which I find fascinating. The main reason why we get on so well is that we have a lot in common. We both love solving problems, and we're both early risers. More importantly, I can rely on him completely. When I fell out with my best friend last year, he didn't take sides; he just helped me see the situation from both points of view. I've always been close to him, and I really look up to him. If I become half as wise as he is, I'll be very happy.
why: FC: kartochka tartibida — kim → qanday odam → nima qilamiz → nega yaxshi chiqishamiz; 'As for...', 'The main reason why ... is that', 'More importantly' bandlarni bog'laydi.
LR: box iboralari tabiiy ishlatilgan (get on well, have a lot in common, rely on, fell out with, close to, look up to) va 'take sides', 'early risers' — Band 6+ uchun 'less common' lug'at.
GRA: zamonlar xilma-xil — used to, present perfect (has taught, I've always been), past simple (fell out), conditional (If I become...), relative clause (who lives..., which I find...).
Hajmi ~215 so'z = 1:50–2:00 gapirish; Band 7 uchun yanada aniq misollar va ko'proq idiomatik til kerak bo'lardi.
box: to get on well with — (kim bilan) yaxshi chiqishmoq, til topishmoq
to look up to — (kimnidir) o'rnak deb bilmoq, hurmat qilmoq
to have a lot in common — umumiy jihatlari ko'p bo'lmoq
to rely on — (kimga) tayanmoq, ishonmoq
a white lie — beozor, yaxshi niyatdagi yolg'on
to be close to — (kim bilan) yaqin bo'lmoq
to fall out with — (kim bilan) urishib qolmoq, aloqani uzmoq
to see eye to eye — fikri bir joydan chiqmoq, kelishmoq

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 3: Honesty, family and friendship
class_ex.instr: Ustoz savol beradi, 2–3 o'quvchi javob beradi: fikr → sabab → misol → qarama-qarshi fikr yoki xulosa (40–60 soniya).
items: Is it ever acceptable to tell a lie?
Does the order in which children are born affect their personality?
How have family relationships changed in your country in recent years?
Why is trust so important in a friendship?
answers: I think in most situations honesty is the best policy, because once people catch you lying, it is very hard to win back their trust. However, I'd say a white lie is sometimes acceptable if it protects someone's feelings. For example, if a friend has spent hours cooking for you and the food isn't great, telling them it is delicious does no real harm. So small, kind lies are fine, but lies that only benefit yourself are not.

To some extent, yes. In many Uzbek families the eldest child is expected to look after the younger ones, so they often grow up more responsible and serious. The youngest, on the other hand, tends to be a little spoilt and may become more relaxed or even rebellious. That said, I don't think birth order decides everything, because parenting style, school and friends probably have a much bigger influence on who we become.

They've changed quite noticeably. In the past, three generations usually lived under one roof, and grandparents played a central role in bringing up children. Nowadays, more young couples move into their own flats, especially in cities, so families are smaller and more independent. On the positive side, parents and children now talk more openly. However, because everyone is busy and glued to their phones, families probably spend less quality time together than they used to.

Mainly because friendship is built on the feeling that you can be yourself without being judged. If you trust someone, you can share your problems and rely on them in difficult moments. Without trust, every conversation becomes careful and shallow. For instance, if a friend repeated your secrets to others, you would probably never see eye to eye again, even if they apologised. So I'd say trust is the foundation, and once it is broken, it is very hard to repair.
why: Fikr (honesty is the best policy) → However bilan istisno (a white lie) → aniq misol → xulosa; 'win back their trust' — kollokatsiya.
'To some extent' — ehtiyotkor javob; passive (is expected to), 'on the other hand' va 'That said' bilan qarama-qarshi fikr; Reading'dagi tug'ilish tartibi g'oyasi o'z so'zlar bilan.
O'tmish va hozirni solishtirish: present perfect (have changed), past simple (lived), Nowadays / In the past; ijobiy va salbiy tomon, 'used to' bilan yakun.
Sabab (Mainly because...) → oqibat (Without trust...) → second conditional (if a friend repeated..., you would...) → xulosa; box'dagi 'rely on', 'see eye to eye' ishlatilgan.

tasks.type: Matching headings — ikkita sarlavha ortiqcha
tasks.instr: Har xatboshining ASOSIY g'oyasini o'z so'zingiz bilan bir gapda ayting, keyin ro'yxatdan mos sarlavhani tanlang. Ro'yxatda ortiqcha sarlavhalar bor.

why: Gorillalar tajribasi: trenerlar "reliable evidence of intentional deceit" topgan — maymunlar ham aldaydi. vii tuzog'i: xatboshida yolg'onchi bilan "muomala" qilish haqida gap yo'q.
Bolalar tajribasi: "lying starts to emerge the moment we learn to speak" — qachon boshlanadi degan savolga javob.
TV dasturi, 30 000 dan ortiq qo'ng'iroq: "viewers were unable to tell the difference". Ommaviy sinov — public test.

"People fail to detect lies because they are basing their opinions on behaviours that are not actually associated with deception". Tuzoq i: "liars do not necessarily look away" — bu yolg'onchilar nima QILMASLIGI, asosiy g'oya noto'g'ri ishonchlar.
"Liars tend to say less and provide fewer details" va "fewer references to themselves" — yolg'onchilar aslida nima qiladi.
TV, gazeta va radio solishtiriladi: "the radio listeners scored an impressive 73% accuracy rate". Qaysi aloqa shakli yolg'onni yaxshiroq fosh qiladi.
tasks.note: Ishlatilmagan sarlavhalar: iii "How wrong is it to lie?" (yolg'onning axloqiy tomoni muhokama qilinmaydi) va vii "Dealing with known liars" (hech bir xatbosh bu haqida emas). F xatboshidagi "the real clues to deceit are in the words" — i ga o'xshaydi, lekin xatboshining asosiy qismi uch aloqa shaklini solishtirish.

readings.title: Practice 1: The science of friendship
readings.qtype: Matching headings (1–6) + Matching features (7–10) + Sentence completion (11–13)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 2 darajasi)
text: A Most of our close relationships are given to us. We do not choose our parents, our brothers and sisters or, in many cases, our neighbours and colleagues. Friendship is different. It is entered into freely, it is not held together by any written contract, and it can end quietly without anyone announcing it. Both people must keep choosing to continue it. Perhaps for this reason, psychologists paid it relatively little attention for much of the twentieth century, preferring to study families and romantic partners. Over the last thirty years, however, friendship has become a serious subject of research.

B One of the strongest findings concerns health. In 2010, a team of researchers combined the results of 148 earlier studies, which together had followed more than 300,000 people for several years. They found that people with strong social relationships were around 50 per cent more likely to survive over the period studied than those with weak ones. The researchers pointed out that the size of this effect was comparable to that of giving up smoking, and larger than the effect of lack of exercise. Loneliness, they argued, should therefore be treated as a public health issue rather than a purely private matter, and in recent years some governments have begun to discuss it in exactly those terms.

C How many friends can one person have? The British anthropologist Robin Dunbar approached this question by comparing monkeys and apes. He noticed that species with a larger outer layer of the brain, the part used for complex thinking, lived in larger social groups. Applying the same relationship to humans, he predicted that we can maintain about 150 meaningful relationships. Within this number, he argued, there are layers: roughly five very close friends, fifteen good friends and fifty friends we see less often. The figure of around 150 has since become known as 'Dunbar's number', although other researchers argue that it varies a great deal from one person to another.

D Other researchers have asked how friendships are formed. The American communication researcher Jeffrey Hall surveyed adults who had recently moved to a new city, as well as first-year university students. He estimated that it takes around 50 hours of shared time to turn an acquaintance into a casual friend, and more than 200 hours to become close friends. What people did together also mattered: hours spent chatting, joking and catching up increased closeness far more than hours spent working side by side. His conclusion was simple: friendship cannot be rushed, and people who move to a new place should expect the process to take months rather than weeks.

E Friendships also end, and usually not because of an argument. More often, one person moves away, changes job, marries or has children, and the two simply see each other less. Dunbar and his colleagues followed a group of students after they left school and found that when contact decreased, feelings of closeness to friends fell quite quickly. Relationships with family members, by contrast, were far more resistant to lack of contact. Friendships that survive distance tend to be those in which both people make a regular effort to call or visit.

F Can technology change these patterns? Social media allows people to keep hundreds of online friends, and it certainly helps people stay in touch across long distances. Some researchers suggest that video calls are more effective than written messages, because they allow people to see each other's faces and share a laugh. Yet research on social media users suggests that the number of people they could rely on in a crisis is still only a handful, similar to the innermost layer of Dunbar's model. It seems that the closest relationships still depend on time and, above all, on meeting face to face.
glossary: anthropologist — antropolog (inson va jamiyatni o'rganuvchi olim)
paraphrases: a larger outer layer of the brain
what people did together also mattered
relationships with family members ... far more resistant to lack of contact

readings.title: Practice 2: Good neighbours
readings.qtype: Matching headings (1–6) + Matching features (7–10) + Sentence completion (11–13)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 2 darajasi)
text: A In many large cities, it is now common for people to live next door to someone for years without learning their name. Surveys in several countries have found that a large proportion of city residents cannot name a single neighbour. Neighbourhood apps have become popular, but they are mostly used to report lost pets or complain about noise, and rarely lead to real conversations. The change is often explained by longer working hours, frequent moves and the fact that many people now work and socialise far from where they live. For many, the person on the other side of the wall has become a stranger.

B This matters for practical reasons. A neighbour can take in a parcel, keep a spare key or notice that something is wrong. During a heatwave, health services often advise people to check on older residents nearby, especially those who live alone, because they may not ask for help themselves. In an emergency, the people next door are usually closer than any friend or relative. Some research has even suggested that areas where neighbours know each other recover more quickly after floods or storms.

C Several community schemes have tried to change this. The simplest is the street party. Once a year, usually on a Sunday in summer, residents close their road to traffic and bring tables, chairs and food outside. Children are usually the first to mix, and parents often meet each other through them. Organisers must first obtain permission from the local council to close the road. In one northern town, a street party that began with thirty households has become an annual tradition, and residents say that people who met there now greet each other throughout the year.

D A second idea is the tool-sharing scheme, sometimes called a 'library of things'. Instead of each household buying a drill or a ladder that is used only a few times, members borrow items from a shared store, usually run by volunteers from a community hall. Items range from pasta machines to camping tents, and each one is checked for safety before it is lent out. Members pay a small annual fee to cover repairs. Apart from saving money and reducing waste, the organisers report an unexpected benefit: people often start conversations when they bring items back, and some end up helping each other with repairs.

E A third scheme focuses on older people who live alone. Volunteers agree to visit the same person once a week for an hour, simply to talk. Before they begin, every volunteer receives training, and visits are arranged by a coordinator. The scheme does not offer shopping or personal care; its only aim is companionship. Many of the people who receive visits have no close family nearby, and volunteers often say they gain as much from the conversations as the people they visit. Several pairs have continued to meet long after the formal arrangement ended.

F Not everyone welcomes these efforts. Some residents value their privacy and feel uncomfortable being invited to join in. Schemes also depend heavily on a few enthusiastic volunteers and often stop when those people move away. Researchers who study communities suggest that large events may matter less than small, repeated contact. In their view, a brief greeting on the stairs, repeated day after day, does more to build trust than a single party.

readings.title: Practice 3 (uyga): Do animals have friends?
readings.qtype: Matching headings (1–6) + Matching features (7–10) + Sentence completion (11–13)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 2 darajasi), uy vazifasi
text: A For much of the twentieth century, most biologists avoided using the word 'friend' when describing animals. It seemed unscientific to suggest that animals felt affection, so researchers spoke instead of 'preferred partners' or 'social bonds'. In recent decades, however, long-term studies of animals in the wild have shown that many species form close, selective and lasting relationships, and a growing number of scientists are now willing to call them friendships. Part of the change came from simply watching the same individuals for many years, which allowed researchers to see who spent time with whom. Such bonds have now been described in species as different as elephants, horses and chimpanzees.

B Some of the clearest evidence comes from baboons. Researchers who have observed wild baboons in Africa for many years found that females spend much of their time grooming a small number of preferred companions. Grooming, in which one animal cleans another's fur, appears to be the main way these bonds are built and kept. The females with the strongest and most stable bonds had more infants that survived their first year, and later studies found that these females also tended to live longer. For a baboon, it seems, good friends are a matter of life and death.

C Vampire bats provide a very different example. These bats feed only on blood, and an adult that fails to find a meal for two or three nights may starve. A well-fed bat will often bring up some of its meal to feed a hungry member of its group, including bats that are not relatives. Experiments with captive bats showed that they were more likely to share food with individuals that had shared with them in the past. Bats that had built up a wider network of partners coped better when one partner was removed. In this way, sharing works rather like insurance: a bat that gives food today may need to receive it tomorrow.

D Among bottlenose dolphins in Shark Bay, Western Australia, males form alliances of two or three individuals that cooperate to stay close to females. These small alliances sometimes join together into larger teams, and some partnerships last for decades. Dolphins also use individual 'signature whistles', which work rather like names, and experiments have shown that they can recognise the whistle of a former companion even after twenty years apart. Females form social networks too, although these are generally looser than the male alliances.

E Why should animals form friendships at all? Scientists point to several advantages. Friends can offer protection against predators and against aggressive members of the same group. They share food and information about where to find it. Friendships may also give access to safer resting places or a better position within the group. There is also evidence that close companions help to reduce stress: animals that lose a close partner often show a rise in stress hormones and try to form new bonds.

F Some researchers remain cautious. They warn against describing animals as if they were humans, and point out that scientists can measure behaviour, such as time spent together, but cannot observe feelings directly. Others reply that the same hormones involved in human bonding are active in other mammals. The debate is unlikely to end soon, but few now doubt that, for many animals, relationships are central to survival.
paraphrases: researchers spoke instead of 'preferred partners' ... now willing to call them friendships
more infants that survived their first year

kahoot.q: Passage 2 has headings, matching features and sentence completion questions. What should you do first?
options: Look quickly at all three question groups
Write your answers on the answer sheet
kahoot.explain: Avval 1 daqiqada uchala savol guruhini ko'zdan kechirasiz (xarita) — shunda matnda nimani qidirishni bilasiz.

kahoot.q: A correct heading matches a paragraph's…
kahoot.explain: Sarlavha butun xatboshining asosiy g'oyasini beradi, bitta gap yoki tafsilotni emas.

kahoot.q: A paragraph is about world trade and mentions coffee only once. The heading 'Coffee prices' is probably…
kahoot.explain: Bir marta tilga olingan tafsilot sarlavha bo'lolmaydi — asosiy g'oya jahon savdosi.

kahoot.q: There are eight headings for six paragraphs. What does this tell you?
kahoot.explain: Ro'yxatda ortiqcha sarlavhalar bor: har xatboshiga bitta, ikkitasi ishlatilmay qoladi.

kahoot.q: In matching features, are the statements in the same order as the information in the text?
kahoot.explain: Features gaplari matn tartibida kelishi shart emas — shuning uchun variantlarni (ism, tajriba) oldindan matnda tagiga chizasiz.

kahoot.q: The instructions say 'You may use any letter more than once.' What does this mean?
options: One letter may answer several statements
Every letter must be used exactly once
You must write two letters in each box
Each statement has two correct letters
kahoot.explain: Bitta harf bir necha gapga javob bo'lishi, boshqasi esa umuman ishlatilmasligi mumkin — bu normal.

kahoot.q: Matching features: why do you underline EVERY place where a person's name appears?
options: A name may appear in several places
It shows you how many words to write
The names are always in the first line
The first mention is always the answer
kahoot.explain: Bitta odam matnda bir necha joyda uchrashi mumkin — faqat birinchisini belgilasangiz, javobni o'tkazib yuborasiz.

kahoot.q: In sentence completion, the answers come…
kahoot.explain: Sentence completion gaplari matn tartibida keladi — oldingi javob joyidan keyin davom etib qidirasiz.

kahoot.q: ONE WORD ONLY. Text: 'She felt anxious before the interview.' Gap: 'Before the interview, she was ___.' Which answer is correct?
kahoot.explain: Faqat bitta so'z va to'g'ri so'z turi (sifat): 'anxiously' — ravish, 'felt anxious' — ikki so'z.

kahoot.q: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS. Text: 'a very close friend'. Gap: 'He shared a flat with a ___.' Which answer gets the mark?
kahoot.explain: 'close friend' — ikki so'z va gapga mos; 'very close friend' — uch so'z, 'a' esa gapda allaqachon bor.

kahoot.q: Your answer is spelt 'relationshp'. The meaning is right. How is it marked?
kahoot.explain: IELTS'da imlo xatosi bo'lsa javob 0 ball — so'zni matndan harfma-harf ko'chiring.

kahoot.q: About how long should you spend on one reading passage in the IELTS exam?
kahoot.explain: 60 daqiqada 3 ta passage — har biriga taxminan 20 daqiqa, javoblarni ko'chirish ham shu vaqt ichida.

kahoot.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'deception'?
kahoot.explain: deception — aldash, aldov; 'trickery' ham shu ma'noda.

kahoot.q: Your siblings are your…
kahoot.explain: sibling — aka-uka yoki opa-singil, ya'ni bir ota-onaning farzandlari.

kahoot.q: 'In the end, he confessed.' This means he…
kahoot.explain: confess — o'z aybini tan olmoq.

kahoot.q: Complete: 'There is strong ___ between the two sisters — each wants to be the best.'
kahoot.explain: rivalry — raqobat: har biri eng yaxshi bo'lishni xohlaydi.

kahoot.q: A child who always gets what they want and behaves badly as a result is…
kahoot.explain: spoilt — erka, ko'p erkalatilgani uchun injiq bo'lib qolgan bola.

kahoot.q: A reliable friend is someone you can…
kahoot.explain: reliable — ishonchli; 'count on' — ishonmoq, tayanmoq.

kahoot.q: 'Her voice gave her away.' What does this mean?
options: It showed what she was hiding
It made her sound confident and relaxed
It was a present from a friend
kahoot.explain: give somebody away — sirini fosh qilmoq: ovozi u yashirayotgan narsani ko'rsatib qo'ydi.

kahoot.q: An acquaintance is someone you…
options: have known and trusted for years
kahoot.explain: acquaintance — tanish: taniysiz, lekin yaqin do'st emas.

intro: Section 3 — o'quv mavzusidagi suhbat: odatda ikki talaba (ba'zan ustoz bilan) loyiha, taqdimot yoki tadqiqot haqida gaplashadi. Til Section 1–2 ga qaraganda murakkabroq: fikrlar almashadi, gapiruvchilar bir-birini to'g'rilaydi va rozi bo'lmaydi.

6.0 darajasida Section 3 ko'pincha ikki turdan iborat: Multiple choice (A, B, C) va flow chart (yoki notes) completion. Ular orasida odatda qisqa pauza bo'ladi — o'sha paytda ikkinchi topshiriqni yana bir bor ko'zdan kechiring.

Tayyorlanish vaqtini ikkiga bo'ling. MCQ uchun: savol o'zagidagi kalit g'oyaning tagiga chizing ("what PROBLEM", "MUST include", "arrange to") — variantlarga emas (SB 2-mashq). Flow chart uchun: har bo'shliqqa qanday so'z kerakligini yozing (ot? ko'plik? joy?) va o'qlar tartibini ko'ring — bosqichlar audioda xuddi shu tartibda keladi.

SIGNAL iboralar javob yaqinlashayotganini bildiradi: "That's the trouble...", "The thing about Mr Dresden is...", "He said that the important thing was...", "The very first thing you need to do is...", "After that...", "The next thing might be...", "Or better still...". Signalni eshitsangiz — keyingi gapga to'liq diqqat.

MCQ TUZOG'I: Section 3 da uchala variant deyarli har doim tilga olinadi. Biri rad etiladi ("Mr Dresden didn't ask for data"), biri boshqa odam yoki boshqa vaqt haqida ("I have to go in the library" — Victor, Fumiko emas). Kim gapiryapti va kim haqida — shuni tekshiring.

FLOW CHART TUZOG'I: gapiruvchi avval bir so'zni aytadi, keyin boshqasi uni to'g'rilaydi yoki yaxshiroq variant taklif qiladi: "places" → "You mean the 'contexts'? — Yes, that's the word"; "future changes" → "or better still, the influences". Oxirgi, kelishilgan so'z — javob.
Transfer: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS — "the animal world" emas, "animal world"; ko'plik -s (key terms, contexts, stages, influences) ko'p ball olib qo'yadi.
formulas: what PROBLEM / MUST include / arrange to
presentation: MCQ da uchala variant ham eshitildi. Qaysi biri?
Savol o'zagiga qayting: KIM haqida va NIMA so'ralyapti? Qolgan ikkitasi odatda rad etilgan yoki boshqa odam haqida.
Flow chart bo'shliqlari ham tartibdami?
Ha. O'qlar bosqichlar ketma-ketligini ko'rsatadi, audio ham shu tartibda boradi.
Gapiruvchi so'zni o'zgartirdi. Qaysi birini yozaman?
Oxirgi, ikkala gapiruvchi rozi bo'lgan so'zni: "Yes, that's the word", "OK, influences".
Signal ibora nima uchun kerak?
U javob yaqinlashayotganini bildiradi. Signalni eshitsangiz, savolni ko'z bilan kuzating va keyingi gapni diqqat bilan tinglang.
"the animal world" deb yozsam bo'ladimi?
Yo'q. Bo'shliq oldidan "the" allaqachon bor — faqat "animal world". Artikl ham so'z hisoblanadi.
Bitta javobni o'tkazib yubordim. Nima qilaman?
To'xtamang — keyingi bosqichga o'ting. Oxirida mantiqan eng mos so'zni yozing, bo'sh qoldirmang.
notes: 5.0 da MCQ va flow chart'ni alohida o'rgangan edik. Endi ular bitta Section 3 da ketma-ket — o'rtadagi pauzadan to'g'ri foydalanish asosiy ko'nikma.
Tekshiruvda har javobdan keyin skriptdan aynan o'sha gapni ekranga chiqaring va signal iborani boshqa rang bilan ko'rsating (SB 3- va 6-mashqlar).
Kuchli o'quvchilarga: Workbook audiosidan keyin Maya'ning jadval va diagrammalarini (1 table, 2 tables, pie chart) xotiradan sanab berish.

Grammatika bo'limidagi SB misollari (Tushuntirish kartasidagi tuzoq va transfer misollari, Formulalarning 4–6-bosqich misollari, "the animal world" savol-javobi, Tipik xatolar jadvali) — SB Track 7 javoblarining o'zi. Tushuntirish, Formulalar va Tipik xatolar kartalari proyektor rejimida ham ko'rinadi — grammatika bo'limini Track 7 tekshiruvigacha proyektorga chiqarmang. Doskadagi 10 daqiqalik tushuntirishda strategiyani umumiy misol bilan bering, masalan: rad etilgan variant — "We thought about a poster, but posters are a bit old-fashioned, so let's make a podcast instead" → podcast; o'zini tuzatish — "Then we'll send the forms by post — no, wait, email is quicker" → email; so'z chegarasi — "Bring the ___ to the workshop", eshitiladi "the lab coats" → lab coats ("the" takrorlanmaydi, -s tushmaydi). SB misolini o'sha savolni tekshirganda ko'rsating. Lug'at jadvali ham (sources, key terms, stages, questionnaire misollari) SB va WB javoblarini ochadi — uni WB Track 8 tekshiruvidan keyin oching, aks holda WB imtihon rejimi va uning normativi (10 dan 8) ma'nosini yo'qotadi.

Ma'lumot ko'p: internetda "fascinating reports ... how much has been written"; "I think I've got plenty" esa g'oyalar haqida (Victor: "is it ideas that you need?"). Muammo — mavzuni toraytira olmaslik

how: CORE — o'quv loyihasi va tadqiqot so'zlari; STRONG — ma'lumotni taqdim etish; SUPER — Section 3 dagi signal iboralar. Ro'yxatni SB va WB tinglangandan keyin ko'rsating: misollar audiodagi gaplarga juda yaqin, oldin ko'rsatilsa javoblarni ochib qo'yadi.
Har o'quvchi o'z loyihasi (maktab yoki kurs) haqida 3 gap aytadi va kamida ikkita yangi so'z ishlatadi.

Bu semestr menda psixologiya loyihasi bor.

class_ex.title: Signal iboralar: qaysi savolga? (SB, 3-mashq)
class_ex.instr: Tinglashdan oldin: har signal ibora 1–5-savollardan qaysi biriga javob olib kelishini taxmin qiling. Tinglagandan keyin tekshiring.
items: a The thing about Mr Dresden is ...
b That's the trouble ...
c He said that the important thing was ...
d Look, tell you what, I'll text you ...
e So what reading have you done so far?
why: 2-savol — tutor haqida: "The thing about Mr Dresden is that he likes to find out what you really enjoy working on".
1-savol — muammo: "that's the trouble — I don't really know where to start".
4-savol — loyihada nima bo'lishi SHART: "the important thing was to read about the topic and definitely include a list of all our sources".
5-savol — nima kelishishdi: "I'll text you in half an hour".
3-savol — nima o'qigan: Victor savoli javob yaqinligini bildiradi.
class_ex.note: Kitobda b → 1 namuna sifatida berilgan. Mashqdan keyin doskaga signal iboralar ro'yxatini yozing — dars davomida to'ldirib boriladi.

class_ex.title: Flow chart bo'shliqlarini oldindan aytish (SB, 4-mashq)
class_ex.instr: 6–10-savollarga javob bermasdan, har bo'shliqqa qanday so'z va qanday ma'lumot kerakligini ayting.
items: 6 — "Define ___ using a diagram"
7 — "Background: relationships in the ___, e.g. apes"
8 — "Present an overview of the ___ for human relationships, e.g. work, home"
9 — "Look at six ___ involved in a friendship"
10 — "Predict the future ___ on friendship"
why: "Define" fe'lidan keyin ot — nimani ta'riflaysiz? Loyiha boshida odatda atamalar ta'riflanadi.
"the ___, e.g. apes" — maymunlar misol bo'ladigan soha yoki olam.
"e.g. work, home" — ish va uy — joy yoki vaziyat; ko'plik.
"six ___" — son, demak ko'plik -s.
"future ___ on friendship" — "on" predlogi bilan: effect on / influence on.
class_ex.note: 10-savol uchun o'quvchilar "changes" deyishi mumkin — tinglashda gapiruvchi aynan shu so'zni aytib, keyin to'g'rilaydi. Buni oldindan aytmang, tekshiruvda ko'rsating.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 1: Teamwork
class_ex.instr: Juftlikda so'rang va javob bering; har javob 2–3 gap: javob + sabab/misol (because, for example, to be honest).
items: Do you prefer working alone or in a team?
Did you do much teamwork at school?
What makes a good team member?
Have you ever had a problem when working in a team?
answers: Well, it depends on the task. For things like revising vocabulary I prefer working alone, because I can go at my own pace, but for bigger projects I'd rather be in a team, since everyone brings different ideas.

Yes, quite a lot, actually. Our teachers often divided us into groups of four for science experiments and presentations, which I really enjoyed, although there was usually one person who didn't pull their weight.
I'd say a good team member is someone who listens to others and keeps their promises. If you say you'll finish your part by Friday, you should do it, otherwise the whole group suffers.
Yes, once. Last year two people in my group couldn't agree on the topic of our presentation, so we wasted almost a week. In the end, we reached a compromise and combined both ideas.
why: 'it depends on' bilan javobni ikki holatga ajratish, 'at my own pace' va 'I'd rather' — tabiiy, kam uchraydigan ibora.
'which I really enjoyed' relative clause, 'although' bilan qarama-qarshi detal va 'pull their weight' idiomasi.
'someone who ...' ta'rif tuzilmasi va 1-tur shart gap (If you say ..., you should ...) — oddiy + murakkab gap aralash.
Past simple bilan qisqa hikoya (couldn't agree, wasted) va 'In the end, we reached a compromise' — natija bilan yakun.
class_ex.note: Mavzu: IELTS Speaking Part 1 to'plami (Teamwork); namuna javoblar — Jony Academy original matni.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 2: A time you worked with others to achieve something
class_ex.instr: 1 daqiqa tayyorlanish (qog'ozga 5–6 kalit so'z), keyin 1–2 daqiqa to'xtovsiz gapiring; sherigingiz vaqtni o'lchaydi va S6_CLASS bo'yicha band qo'yadi.
items: Describe a time when you worked with other people to achieve something.
You should say:
what the goal was
who you worked with
what your role was
and explain whether the teamwork was successful.
answers: I'd like to talk about a project I did with my classmates last spring, when we organised a charity fair at our school in Samarkand. The goal was to raise money for new books for a village school near our city, and we had just three weeks to do it.

There were eight of us from the same class, and our English teacher, Ms Dilnoza, helped us with the paperwork. At the first meeting we had a common goal but no real plan, so I decided to take the lead. We divided the tasks: two people baked cakes, three made posters, and the rest of us collected second-hand books and toys to sell.

My role was to keep everyone on schedule. To be honest, it wasn't easy, because one boy didn't pull his weight at first, and two girls argued about the price of the cakes. Eventually, we reached a compromise and agreed to sell them for five thousand som each.

Looking back, I'd say the teamwork was really successful. Everyone pulled together in the last week, we met the deadline, and we raised almost three million som, which was more than we had expected. It was exhausting, but in the end it was worth it.
why: FC: kartochka tartibida — maqsad → kim bilan → o'z roli → natija; To be honest / Eventually / Looking back bilan bog'langan, taxminan 1:50 ga yetadi.
LR: box iboralarining hammasi o'z joyida (take the lead, divide the tasks, pull his weight, reach a compromise, pull together, meet the deadline) va 'second-hand', 'paperwork' kabi aniq so'zlar.
GRA: past simple hikoya, past perfect (than we had expected), relative clause (which was ...), 'so' va 'because' bilan sabab-oqibat.
Nega Band 7 emas: tuzilma va lug'at yaxshi, lekin fikrlar oddiy, nozik ma'noli idioma va murakkab tuzilmalar kam — Band 6–6.5 uchun namunaviy daraja.
box: to pull together — birgalikda kuch birlashtirib ishlamoq
to divide the tasks — vazifalarni taqsimlamoq
to take the lead — boshchilikni o'z zimmasiga olmoq
to pull your weight — o'z ulushini to'liq bajarmoq
to reach a compromise — murosaga kelmoq
a common goal — umumiy maqsad
to meet the deadline — belgilangan muddatga ulgurmoq
in the end it was worth it — oxir-oqibat bunga arzidi
class_ex.note: Namunani ustoz o'qiydi (taxminan 1:50); o'quvchilar box iboralarini eshitganda qo'l ko'taradi va sanab boradi (8 tadan nechtasi?).

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Part 3: Friendship and teamwork today
class_ex.instr: Ustoz savol beradi, 2–3 o'quvchi javob beradi: fikr → sabab → misol → qarama-qarshi fikr yoki xulosa (har javob 30–40 soniya).
items: How has social media changed the way people make and keep friends?
Why is teamwork important in the workplace?
Should a team always have a leader?
answers: I think it has made it much easier to stay in touch. For example, my cousin moved to Seoul for work two years ago, but we still message each other almost every day. On the other hand, social media has made some friendships more superficial, because people collect hundreds of online friends they hardly know. So overall, it's a useful tool for keeping friends, but real friendships are still built face to face.

Well, most jobs today are too complex for one person to do alone. In a hospital, for instance, doctors, nurses and technicians have to share information constantly, otherwise patients could be put at risk. Teamwork also allows people to learn from each other, which makes the whole organisation stronger. Having said that, teams only work well when everyone knows their responsibilities; if the roles aren't clear, teamwork can actually slow things down.

In most cases, yes. A leader can make the final decision when the team can't reach a compromise, and they make sure the group meets its deadlines. However, I don't think the leader always has to be the same person. In small teams, like a group of students working on a project, the role could change depending on who knows the most about each task. That way, everyone gets a chance to develop leadership skills.
why: Strategiya: fikr (easier to stay in touch) → shaxsiy misol → 'On the other hand' qarama-qarshi fikr (superficial) → 'So overall' xulosa; present perfect o'zgarishni ko'rsatadi.
Umumiy fikr → aniq misol (hospital) → qo'shimcha sabab (which makes ...) → 'Having said that' bilan cheklov; passive (be put at risk) va shart gap bor.
Qisqa javob (In most cases, yes) → 2 sabab → 'However' bilan nozik fikr → misol → 'That way' xulosa; box iboralari (reach a compromise, meet deadlines) qayta ishlatiladi.

class_ex.title: Speaking rubrikasi — IELTS band 5–7 (4 mezon)
head: Mezon
Band 5
Band 6 (kurs maqsadi)
Band 7
Sherik tekshiradi
rows: Ko'p to'xtaydi va takrorlaydi; faqat and, but, because.
Uzoq gapiradi, ba'zan to'xtab o'zini tuzatadi; firstly, also, however bor, lekin mexanik.
Zo'riqishsiz gapiradi; on the other hand, as a result, what I mean is tabiiy ishlatiladi.
Part 2 da 1:40–2:00 gapirdimi? Necha marta uzoq to'xtadi?
Mavzu so'zlari yetarli, 1–2 'less common' ibora; so'z topolmasa boshqacha aytadi.
Idioma va kollokatsiyalar (to settle in, a sense of belonging) o'z joyida.
Oddiy + murakkab gaplar (because, which, if, when); xatolar bor, lekin ma'no aniq.
Turli tuzilmalar (present perfect, conditional, passive) asosan xatosiz.
Kamida 2 ta murakkab gap bo'ldimi? Zamon to'g'rimi?
Umuman tushunarli; ayrim tovush/urg'u xatolari (th, w/v, so'z urg'usi).
Oson tushuniladi; urg'u va intonatsiya ma'noni ta'kidlaydi.
x.25 → x.5 ga, x.75 → keyingi butun songa yaxlitlanadi
Sherik bandni raqam bilan yozadi va 1 maslahat beradi
class_ex.answers: Sherik har mezonga band qo'yadi, o'rtachani yaxlitlaydi va 1 maslahat yozadi.
class_ex.note: To'liq 0–9 jadval — 9- va 18-darslarda (S6_FULL).

listenings.title: Student's Book, Track 7: Fumiko's psychology project (Q1–10)
intro: Fumiko psixologiya loyihasi haqida Victor bilan gaplashadi; ikkinchi qismda ular birga reja tuzadi. Tinglashdan oldin: 1–5 da savol o'zagidagi kalit g'oyani belgilang (SB 2-mashq), 6–10 da bo'shliq turini yozing.
Q1–5 va Q6–10 orasida qisqa pauza bor. Flow chart ko'rsatmasi: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer. Savollar sahifasi quyida rasm sifatida.

tasks.title: Questions 1–5
tasks.type: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C
tasks.instr: Uchala variant ham eshitiladi. Kim haqida va nima so'ralyapti — shuni tekshiring.
items: 1 What problem does Fumiko have with her psychology project? A) She isn't interested in the topic. B) She can't find enough information. C) She doesn't know what to focus on.
2 What point does Victor make about Fumiko's tutor? A) He explores his students' key interests. B) He is a very hard-working member of staff. C) He uses a limited range of project titles.
3 What has Fumiko already read on her topic? A) book extracts B) journal articles C) internet material
4 According to Mr Dresden, Fumiko's project must include A) some graphic data. B) a bibliography. C) a public survey.
5 Victor and Fumiko arrange to A) get in contact in half an hour. B) meet up in the library. C) have lunch together.
why: "That's the trouble — I don't really know where to start ... can't seem to narrow it down". A — tuzoq: "I'm really enjoying it"; B — "I think I've got plenty" g'oyalar haqida, ma'lumot esa ko'p: "there are some fascinating reports".
"The thing about Mr Dresden is that he likes to find out what you really enjoy working on". C — tuzoq: u "broad" (keng) mavzular beradi, cheklangan emas.
"Have you been on the Internet? — I have, and there are some fascinating reports". A — kitoblarni endi olgan, hali o'qimagan; B — jurnal maqolalarini "put them away ... without looking at them".
"Definitely include a list of all our sources" = bibliography. A — tuzoq: "Mr Dresden didn't ask for data"; C — so'rovnoma Fumiko'ning o'z g'oyasi.
"Tell you what, I'll text you in half an hour". B — kutubxonaga Victor yolg'iz boradi; C — kofe va faqat seminar tez tugasa, tushlik emas.
tasks.note: 5-savol yaxshi misol: "library" va "canteen" ikkalasi ham eshitiladi, lekin aniq kelishilgan narsa — yarim soatdan keyin xabar yozish.

tasks.title: Questions 6–10 — Fumiko's plan
tasks.type: Complete the flow chart. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer.
tasks.instr: O'qlar tartibi = suhbat tartibi. Victor Fumiko'ning so'zini to'g'rilaganda yaxshi tinglang.
why: "The very first thing you need to do is give a definition of what you mean by your key terms". "Using a diagram" = "you could just do a diagram".
"You could do a bit of background on the animal world ... relationships among ape groups". "the" formada bor — ikki so'z yoziladi.
Fumiko "places" deydi, Victor: "You mean the 'contexts' for relationships" — "Yes, that's the word". Kalitda — contexts.
"Why don't you go through the stages in a friendship? ... just select six".
"Maybe the future changes in ... — Yeah, or better still, the influences". "changes" — tuzoq.
tasks.note: 8 va 10-savol — Section 3 ning asosiy tuzog'i: birinchi aytilgan so'z emas, tuzatilgan so'z javob.
rows: Background: relationships in the (7), e.g. apes
Present an overview of the (8) for human relationships, e.g. work, home
Look at six (9) involved in a friendship (plus survey)

tasks.title: 6-mashq: signal so'zlar (qayta tinglab)
tasks.type: Bitta so'z yozing
tasks.instr: Track 7 ning ikkinchi qismini qayta tinglang va har signal iboradagi bo'shliqni to'ldiring. Bu iboralar 6–10-javoblardan oldin keladi.
items: 6 I think the very ___ thing you need to do is ...
7 After ___, you could do ...
8 'You mean ... ?' 'Yes, ___ the word.'
9 The ___ thing might be to ...
10 Why don't I ___ by ..., or better still, ...
why: "I think the very first thing you need to do is give a definition..."
"Right. After that, you could do a bit of background..."
"You mean the 'contexts' for relationships. — Yes, that's the word."
"Or the next thing might be to select one type of relationship..."
"Why don't I end by looking into the future? — Yeah, or better still, the influences".
tasks.note: Kitobda bu mashq uchun alohida CD2 Track 8 bor; bu yerda o'sha qism Track 7 dan qayta eshittiriladi.

listenings.title: Student's Book: recording script (CD2 Track 7) — ustoz uchun
intro: Recording script sahifasi — tekshiruvdan keyin ekranga chiqariladi.
transcript: [Ustoz uchun] Tekshiruvdan keyin ekranga chiqaring. Har javob gapini, signal iborani va tuzoq gapni alohida rang bilan ko'rsating.

listenings.title: Workbook, Track 8: Maya's presentation on lifelong friendships (Q1–10)
listenings.qtype: Multiple choice + Flow chart — imtihon rejimi
intro: Jack va Maya Maya'ning taqdimoti haqida gaplashadi: avval tadqiqot qanday o'tgani (MCQ), keyin taqdimot tuzilishi (flow chart). Avval Workbook 1-mashqini bajaring.
Keyin imtihondagidek: tayyorlanish vaqti, audio BIR MARTA, 10 savol. Flow chart: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.

tasks.title: 1-mashq: 6–10 uchun qanday so'z kerak?
tasks.type: Choose A, B or C
tasks.instr: Tinglashdan oldin flow chart'ni ko'zdan kechiring.
items: 1 What kind of word will be required for all of Questions 6–10? A) adverbs B) verbs C) nouns
why: "change of ___", "Effects of ___", "descriptions of ___", "Changes in ___" — predlogdan keyin ot; 10 esa sarlavha ("___ (e.g. sports, musical tastes)") — ham ot.

tasks.title: Questions 1–5
tasks.type: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C
tasks.instr: Maya har savolda bir nechta narsani aytadi — savol o'zagidagi kalit g'oyaga mos kelganini tanlang.
items: 1 Maya chose the topic of lifelong friendships because A) it was an unusual area of research. B) she had a particular interest in it. C) someone suggested it to her.
2 Maya says that the sample of people she used A) was smaller than she wanted it to be. B) was typical of the population in general. C) was the basis for further work.
3 The problem with the questionnaire was that A) it wasn't well constructed. B) the subjects couldn't engage with it. C) too much time was required to complete it.
4 Maya says that when she conducted the interviews, A) she kept brief notes. B) the subjects were all very relaxed. C) they followed a clear structure.
5 What does Maya say about other research in the area? A) A lot of it contradicted her findings. B) It wasn't very easy to find. C) It was carried out in the same way as hers.
why: "There's been a lot of research on how people form friendships ... but there's not much on this particular topic". B — tuzoq: ota-onasining do'stlari — bu tadqiqot usuli, sabab emas.

"I'd collate the results from that small sample so that I could compare them with more general conclusions from research". A — "small" ni Jack aytadi, Maya norozi emas; B — "representative" keyinroq, taqqoslash natijasi haqida.
"They just couldn't analyse their friendships in that 'cold' way". C — tuzoq: "they hadn't had time" — bahona edi.
"I adapted my questionnaire and sat down with each person" — intervyu anketa asosida, aniq tuzilma bilan. A — tuzoq: yozib olgan, "rather than having to write notes".
"There's not a lot of that, but I managed to locate some academic research". A — tuzoq: "one or two disparities", lekin umuman "confirmed what I found".
tasks.note: 4-savol eng qiyin: "structure" so'zi eshitilmaydi. Anketani moslashtirib, har odam bilan u bo'yicha gaplashgan — shuning uchun intervyu tuzilmali bo'lgan.

tasks.title: Questions 6–10 — Lifelong friendships presentation
tasks.type: Complete the flow chart. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer.
tasks.instr: Har bosqichda Maya kategoriya nomini aytadi va qanday ko'rsatganini (table / pie chart) qo'shadi.
why: "The first category I've called 'Change of Location' ... goes to live somewhere else"; "a couple of separate tables" = 2 tables.
"What happens to the friendship when one or both of the friends get married" — "That's a pie chart".
"The next one concerns 'Personality' ... I picked out the most extreme changes".
"How much people had in common in terms of political opinions ... I've constructed another pie chart".
"I've categorised this as 'Shared Interests' ... sports doesn't change ... whereas their musical tastes do".
tasks.note: 7-savolda "married" (fe'l) emas, "marriage" (ot) yoziladi: "Effects of ___" — predlogdan keyin ot. 1-mashqdagi "nouns" javobi shu yerda yordam beradi.
rows: Origins of friendship (age, where began, circumstances, etc.): 1 table
Comparisons between descriptions of (8): patterns of extreme change
(10) (e.g. sports, musical tastes): continuing or changing

listenings.title: Workbook: recording script (Track 8) — ustoz uchun
intro: Recording script sahifasi — tekshiruvdan keyin ekranga chiqariladi.
transcript: [Ustoz uchun] Skript bilan qayta tinglashda xato qilingan savollarning gapini topishga ishlatiladi. Jack'ning bosqichlarni almashtiruvchi savollarini ("OK, what comes next?", "What then?") belgilang.

listenings.title: Jony Academy mashqi: Friendship project
intro: Ben va Sara — sotsiologiya talabalari — birinchi kurs talabalarining do'st orttirishi haqidagi loyihani rejalashtiradi.
Suhbat BIR MARTA; 1–5 va 6–10 orasida qisqa pauza bor. Flow chart: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer.
transcript: [Ustoz uchun] Ustoz ikki rolni o'qiydi (yoki kuchli o'quvchi bilan) — oddiy tezlikda (taxminan 150 so'z/daqiqa), rollarni ovoz bilan farqlab. BIR MARTA.
[Ustoz uchun] 1–5 va 6–10 orasida 20 soniya pauza qiling.
BEN: Hi Sara. Have you got a minute to talk about our sociology project?
SARA: Sure, I was going to message you anyway. Have you decided on the focus?
BEN: Well, at first I wanted to look at friendship in general, but Dr Hughes said that was far too wide. So I thought we could look at how first-year students make friends in their first term.
SARA: That sounds manageable. But why first-years?
BEN: Partly because they're easy to find — they're all around us. But mainly because nobody in our department has studied them before. Dr Hughes checked the list of past projects for me.
SARA: Great. And what did he say about the length?

BEN: The written report can be up to three thousand words, but the thing he really stressed was the presentation. It mustn't go over fifteen minutes — he'll stop us if it does. He said he doesn't mind if we don't have many statistics.
SARA: Fifteen minutes isn't much. What about collecting the data? I assumed we'd do an online questionnaire.
BEN: I thought so too, but online surveys get very few replies. My cousin tried one last year and got eleven answers out of two hundred.
SARA: Wow. So what then — interviews?
BEN: Interviews take ages. I think the best option is a short paper questionnaire that we hand out at the start of lectures. Students fill it in on the spot.
SARA: OK. I'm a bit worried about one thing, though. Some students might not want to write about their friends. It's quite personal.
BEN: True. That's why we should make it anonymous — no names at all. And we'll keep it to ten questions, so it's quick.
SARA: And will lecturers let us use their time?
BEN: I've already asked two of them, and they're both happy to give us the first five minutes.
SARA: Perfect. Shall we meet on Thursday to write the questions?
BEN: Thursday's difficult — I've got a seminar all afternoon. How about Wednesday morning, in the café next to the library?
SARA: Wednesday's fine, but that café's always so noisy. Let's book one of the study rooms in the library instead.
BEN: Good idea. I'll book one tonight.
(Pause — 20 seconds)
SARA: Right, let's put the stages in order. What comes first?
BEN: I think the very first thing is to find out what other people have already written. Dr Hughes wants a short literature review — just two or three pages.
SARA: Fine. After that, we write the questions. Should we just use them straight away?
BEN: No — Dr Hughes said we should test them first on a small group. He called it a pilot study.
SARA: Who with? Our flatmates?
BEN: They're second-years, so no. It should be people like our real sample — maybe five first-years from the sports club.
SARA: OK. Then we hand out the questionnaires. We're aiming for two hundred, aren't we?
BEN: Yes. And the next stage is putting all the answers into a spreadsheet. That'll take a while.
SARA: I can do that — I'm quite quick at typing. Then we look for patterns. For example, do students who live in halls make friends faster than students who live at home?
BEN: Exactly — that comparison could be the most interesting part. And we finish with recommendations — what the university could do to help new students. Maybe more social events in the first week?
SARA: Or better still, a buddy scheme, where every new student gets a second-year partner. I think that would help most.
BEN: Agreed. Let's make that our main recommendation.

tasks.title: Questions 1–5
tasks.type: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C
tasks.instr: Uchala variant ham eshitiladi — savol o'zagiga mosini tanlang.
items: 1 What was Ben's MAIN reason for choosing first-year students for the project? A) They are easy to contact. B) No one in the department has researched them. C) The tutor recommended them.
2 What did Dr Hughes say was most important? A) the length of the written report B) keeping the presentation within the time limit C) including a lot of statistics
3 How will the students collect their data? A) an online questionnaire B) interviews C) a paper questionnaire in lectures
4 What is Sara worried about? A) Students may find the topic too personal. B) The questionnaire may be too long. C) Lecturers may refuse to help.
5 Where will Ben and Sara meet to write the questions? A) in a café B) in a library study room C) in the seminar room
why: "Partly because they're easy to find ... But mainly because nobody in our department has studied them before". Savolda MAIN reason so'ralgan: "partly" va "mainly" — asosiy sabab "mainly" dan keyin keladi. A — tuzoq: bu ham sabab, lekin faqat "partly" (qisman); C — tutor mavzuni "far too wide" degan va eski loyihalar ro'yxatini tekshirgan, birinchi kursni tavsiya qilmagan.

"The thing he really stressed was the presentation. It mustn't go over fifteen minutes". A — 3000 so'z tilga olinadi, lekin "but" bilan chetga suriladi; C — "doesn't mind if we don't have many statistics".
"The best option is a short paper questionnaire that we hand out at the start of lectures". A — kam javob; B — "Interviews take ages".
"Some students might not want to write about their friends. It's quite personal". B — Ben aytadi ("ten questions"), Sara xavotiri emas; C — ikki o'qituvchi allaqachon rozi.
"Let's book one of the study rooms in the library instead". A — kafe shovqinli, rad etildi; C — seminar Ben'ning payshanba kungi darsi.

tasks.title: Questions 6–10 — Project stages
tasks.type: Complete the flow chart. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer.
tasks.instr: Signal iboralarni kuting: "the very first thing", "After that", "the next stage", "Or better still".
why: "Dr Hughes wants a short literature review — just two or three pages".
"We should test them first on a small group. He called it a pilot study". "small group" — tuzoq, bu bosqich nomi emas.
"The next stage is putting all the answers into a spreadsheet".
"Do students who live in halls make friends faster than students who live at home?"
"Maybe more social events ...? — Or better still, a buddy scheme" — "Agreed". "social events" — tuzoq.
tasks.note: 7-savol uchun "flatmates" ham eshitiladi — Ben uni rad etadi ("They're second-years, so no"). 10-savol — SB dagi "or better still" tuzog'ining aynan takrori.
rows: Read previous research and write a short (6)
Write ten questions and test them in a (7) with five first-years
Hand out the questionnaires (target: 200) and enter all answers into a (8)
Look for patterns, e.g. students living in (9) vs students living at home
Recommendations — main one: a (10) for new students

homework_intro: Bugun Section 3 da ikki savol turini ketma-ket yechdik: avval multiple choice, keyin flow chart. Eng ko'p ball ikki joyda yo'qoladi — rad etilgan variantni tanlashda va tuzatilgan so'z o'rniga birinchi eshitilgan so'zni yozishda.

Birinchi vazifa — shadowing: ustoz guruhga SB Track 7 audiosini va skript rasmini yuboradi. Track 7 ning ikkinchi qismini ("Right, so let's design a plan" dan oxirigacha) skript bilan 3 marta tinglang, keyin Victor'ning gaplarini u bilan bir vaqtda takrorlang. Oxirgi urinishni ovozli xabar qilib guruhga yuboring.

Ikkinchi vazifa — diktant: ustoz guruhga WB Track 8 audiosini yuboradi. Uning taqdimot qismini (pauzadan keyin) tinglang va Maya'ning 6 ta gapini to'liq yozing — har bir kategoriya nomi bilan (Change of Location, Personality va h.k.). Diktantni ustoz belgilagan muddatgacha guruhga yuboring; muddat tugagach ustoz skript rasmini yuboradi — solishtiring va xatolarni qizil bilan belgilang.
Uchinchi vazifa — signal iboralar ro'yxati: ikkala audiodan kamida 8 ta signal iborani yozing ("That's the trouble", "After that", "What then?" ...) va har biriga o'z gapingizni tuzing.
Speaking vazifasi — bugungi Part 2 kartochkasini uyda ovozli yozib yuboring (1 daqiqa tayyorlanish, 2 daqiqa gapirish).

homework.title: Shadowing: SB Track 7 (2-qism)
homework.instr: Ustoz guruhga SB Track 7 audiosi va skript rasmini yuboradi. 3 marta tinglash, keyin Victor bilan bir vaqtda takrorlash; ovozli xabar guruhga.
homework.answers: Ustoz talaffuz va ritmni tekshiradi; signal iboralar aniq eshitilishi kerak.

homework.title: Diktant: WB Track 8 (taqdimot qismi)
homework.instr: Ustoz guruhga WB Track 8 audiosini yuboradi. Maya'ning 6 ta gapi to'liq yozilib, muddatgacha guruhga yuboriladi; muddat tugagach, skript rasmi bilan tekshiriladi.
homework.answers: Diktant topshirish muddati tugagach ustoz WB skript rasmini guruhga yuboradi (oldinroq emas); o'quvchi o'zi solishtiradi, xatolarni qizil bilan belgilaydi. Keyingi darsda ustoz 2 ta gapni tasodifiy so'raydi.

homework.title: Signal iboralar ro'yxati
homework.instr: Kamida 8 ta signal ibora + har biriga o'z gapingiz.
homework.answers: Iboralar audiodan bo'lishi shart; o'z gapi yo'q qator qabul qilinmaydi.

homework.title: Speaking (og'zaki): Part 2 ovozli yozuv — A time you worked with others to achieve something
homework.instr: Bugungi Part 2 kartochkasi: 1 daqiqa tayyorlanish, 1:40–2:00 gapiring, ilovaga ovozli yuboring; oxirida Part 1 dan 2 savolga javob qo'shing.
homework.answers: Ustoz S6_CLASS bo'yicha 4 mezonga band qo'yadi; tekshiruv: 2:00 gacha to'xtovsiz, box'dan 3 ibora, kamida 1 murakkab gap (because/which/if).

normativ: 1:40–2:00 to'xtovsiz, 3 ta yangi ibora, 4 mezon o'rtachasi ≥ 5.5 (S6_CLASS)

kahoot.q: What do you usually hear in IELTS Listening Section 3?
options: One speaker giving a talk on local facilities
A phone call to book a room or a service
A lecture by a professor with no dialogue
kahoot.explain: Section 3 — o'quv mavzusidagi suhbat: 2–3 talaba (ba'zan ustoz bilan) loyiha, taqdimot yoki tadqiqotni muhokama qiladi.

kahoot.q: Section 3 has MCQs (1–5) and a flow chart (6–10). How should you use the preparation time?
options: Mark key words in stems; predict word types for gaps
Read every option in detail and skip the flow chart
Study the flow chart only, as MCQs are easier
Write a guessed answer for all ten questions
kahoot.explain: Vaqtni ikkiga bo'ling: MCQ o'zagidagi kalit g'oya, flow chart'da esa har bo'shliqqa qanday so'z kerakligi.

kahoot.q: In a Section 3 multiple-choice question, what should you underline first?
options: the key idea in the question stem
every word in all three options
the names of the two speakers only
the longest of the three options
kahoot.explain: Savol o'zagi nima so'ralayotganini aytadi (what PROBLEM, MUST include); variantlarning esa ikkitasi tuzoq.

kahoot.q: 'I thought about writing on climate, but the reading is very technical — so I've gone for urban gardens.' What is the speaker's topic?
kahoot.explain: Climate tilga olinadi, lekin "but" bilan rad etiladi; yakuniy tanlov — "I've gone for urban gardens".

kahoot.q: An option is mentioned, but it is the OTHER student's plan, not the plan of the person in the question. Is it the answer?
options: No — check who the question is about
Yes — every option you hear is right
Yes — if it is the last thing you hear
Only if both speakers say it twice
kahoot.explain: Section 3 da bir necha odam gapiradi: variant eshitilsa ham, u savoldagi odamga tegishli bo'lishi shart.

kahoot.q: The question asks what the tutor thinks is MOST important. Which phrase signals the answer?
kahoot.explain: "Most", "above all", "the main thing" kabi ta'kid iboralari savoldagi MOST ga mos keladi — javob shundan keyin keladi.

kahoot.q: In a flow-chart completion task, in what order do the answers usually come in the recording?
options: in the same order as the chart
in a random order across the talk
in reverse order, from the end
all together at the very end
kahoot.explain: O'qlar bosqichlar ketma-ketligini ko'rsatadi, audio ham shu tartibda boradi.

kahoot.q: 'Let's end with a short video — or better still, a live demonstration.' 'Yes, much better.' How will they end the talk?
options: with a quiz for the class
kahoot.explain: "Or better still" birinchi g'oyani yaxshirog'i bilan almashtiradi, ikkinchi gapiruvchi ham rozi — javob shu.

kahoot.q: 'The first step is collecting the data — no, sorry, choosing the sample comes first.' What is the first step?
kahoot.explain: Gapiruvchi o'zini tuzatdi ("no, sorry"): birinchi aytilgan so'z tuzoq, tuzatilgani — javob.

kahoot.q: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS. Gap: 'Visit the ___ in week 3.' You hear 'the science museum'. What do you write?
kahoot.explain: "the" gapda bor va artikl ham so'z hisoblanadi: "the science museum" uch so'z bo'lib qoladi.

kahoot.q: Gap: 'Interview four ___ of the club.' You hear 'four members' but write 'member'. Is your answer correct?
options: No — the plural -s is needed here
Yes — small spelling slips are fine
Yes — the singular is always accepted
Only if you also write 'the' before it
kahoot.explain: "four" dan keyin ko'plik kerak; -s tushib qolsa, javob noto'g'ri hisoblanadi.

kahoot.q: There is a short pause between Questions 1–5 and 6–10. What is the best use of it?
options: Read the flow chart again and predict
Relax and wait for the next part
Change all your answers to Questions 1–5
Copy your answers onto the answer sheet
kahoot.explain: Pauza — ikkinchi topshiriqni yana bir bor ko'rib, bo'shliqlarni bashorat qilish vaqti; qog'oz imtihonda javoblar varaqaga eng oxirida (10 daqiqada) ko'chiriladi.

kahoot.q: At a British university, what is a 'tutor'?
options: a teacher who guides a small group
a student who lives in the same flat
an office that handles student fees
a person who only marks exams
kahoot.explain: Tutor — kichik guruh yoki alohida talabaga yo'l ko'rsatadigan o'qituvchi (kurator).

kahoot.q: What is a 'questionnaire'?
options: a set of written questions to answer
a spoken interview for a new job
a list of all the books for the course
a table of final test results
kahoot.explain: Questionnaire — anketa: odamlar yozma javob beradigan savollar to'plami.

kahoot.q: Which phrase means 'to do a survey'?
kahoot.explain: "carry out a survey" — so'rovnoma o'tkazmoq; qolgan fe'llar bu ma'noni bermaydi.

kahoot.q: 'The project is part of my assessment.' What does this mean?
options: It counts towards my final mark.
It is just an optional extra task.
It must be done in a group.
kahoot.explain: Assessment — baholash: loyiha natijasi yakuniy bahoga qo'shiladi.

kahoot.q: 'First, give some background on the topic.' What should you give first?
options: basic facts that set the scene
the final conclusions of your study
kahoot.explain: Background — mavzuga kirish uchun umumiy ma'lumot, asos.
